R023.title: Higher-regularity conjecture for conjugacies near irreducible toral automorphisms
R023.statement: Let $L$ be a hyperbolic automorphism of $\mathbb T^d$, $d\geq 3$, with simple real spectrum and irreducible characteristic polynomial over $\mathbb Z$. Let $\mathcal U$ be the neighborhood from Theorem A, and let $f\in\mathcal U$ satisfy Property $\mathcal A$ and $g\in\mathcal U$ have the same periodic data. **Higher-regularity conjecture.** In the context of Theorem A, one can actually conclude that $f$ and $g$ are $C^{r-\varepsilon}$ conjugate, where $\varepsilon$ is an arbitrarily small positive number. Theorem A gives only $C^{1+\nu}$ conjugacy under its stated assumptions; the conjecture asserts the same near-optimal regularity known in dimension two.
R023.source_name: Andrey Gogolev, “Smooth conjugacy of Anosov diffeomorphisms on higher dimensional tori”, arXiv:0804.3901 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3901

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

R023.title: Fiber regularity conjecture for general linear projections
R023.statement:
Let $X\subset \mathbf{P}^r$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, and let $\pi:X\to\mathbf{P}^{n+c}$ be a general linear projection. If $Z\subset X\subset\mathbf{P}^r$ is any fiber, its Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity as a subscheme of $\mathbf{P}^r$ is defined by $\operatorname{reg} Z$. **Fiber regularity conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg} Z\leq n/c+1.
$$

The conjecture is sharp in the examples discussed in the source: Lazarsfeld's examples give fibers of regularity $n+1$ when $c=1$, and the Reye congruence gives nondegenerate Enriques surfaces in $\mathbf{P}^5$ whose projected fibers have regularity $3$.
R023.source_name: Roya Beheshti and David Eisenbud, “Fibers of Generic Projections”, arXiv:0806.1928 (2009).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.1928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

R023.title: Comparison conjecture between fiber regularity and the invariant q
R023.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbf{P}^r$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, and let $\pi:X\to\mathbf{P}^{n+c}$ be a general linear projection. If $Z\subset X\subset\mathbf{P}^r$ is any fiber, write

$$
Z=X\cap\Lambda,
$$

where $\Lambda$ is a linear subspace containing the projection center in codimension $1$. Let $q(X,\Lambda)$ denote the invariant introduced earlier in the source, and let $\operatorname{reg}Z$ be the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $Z$. **Comparison conjecture.** The fiber satisfies

$$
\operatorname{reg} Z\leq q(X,\Lambda).
$$

This conjecture would, together with the paper's bound $q(X,\Lambda)\leq n/c+1$, imply the fiber regularity conjecture. The source gives no resolution of this comparison.
R023.source_name: Roya Beheshti and David Eisenbud, “Fibers of Generic Projections”, arXiv:0806.1928 (2009).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.1928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

R023.title: Casselman's regularity conjecture for cell languages
R023.statement: Let $W$ be a Coxeter group with generating set $S$, and let $C\subset W$ be a cell. Write $\mathtt{Red}(C)$ for the language of reduced expressions of elements of $C$. **Casselman's regularity conjecture.** For any Coxeter group $W$ and any cell $C\subset W$, there exists a finite state automaton accepting the language $\mathtt{Red}(C)$. That is, the language $\mathtt{Red}(C)$ is regular. This conjecture asks whether the generally infinite combinatorial data of every cell can be encoded by a finite-state automaton. The source gives no resolution in the stated generality; in the paper, regularity is established for cells in the affine Weyl groups studied there.
R023.source_name: Paul E. Gunnells, “Automata and cells in affine Weyl groups”, arXiv:0807.2463 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.2463

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2008).

R023.title: Accessibility-class regularity conjecture for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms
R023.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $f\colon M\to M$ be a $C^r$, partially hyperbolic, $r$-bunched diffeomorphism. An **accessibility class** for $f$ is the set of points reachable from one another by piecewise paths tangent to the stable and unstable distributions of $f$.

**Accessibility-class regularity conjecture.** Every accessibility class for $f$ is an injectively immersed, $C^r$ submanifold of $M$.

This conjecture would imply the saturated section theorem used in the paper, concerning smoothness of continuous sections whose images are accessibility classes for lifted fibered partially hyperbolic maps. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is open or resolved.
R023.source_name: Amie Wilkinson, “The cohomological equation for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms”, arXiv:0809.4862 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4862

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the left-Garside category of self-distributive terms
R023.statement: Let $\mathcal{LD}^{\scriptscriptstyle+}$ be the left-Garside category of self-distributive terms. **Regularity conjecture.** The category $\mathcal{LD}^{\scriptscriptstyle+}$ is regular. This regularity would, via the preceding embedding argument, imply right-cancellation for $\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal{LD}^{\scriptscriptstyle+})$ and contribute to the Embedding Conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is resolved.
R023.source_name: Patrick Dehornoy, “Left-Garside categories, self-distributivity, and braids”, arXiv:0810.4698 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.4698

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

R023.title: The decomposability-or-regularity conjecture for ultrafilters
R023.statement:
Let $
obreak\break 
obreak\lambda<\mu$ be cardinals, and let $D$ be a $(\lambda^+,\mu)$-regular ultrafilter. **Decomposability-or-regularity conjecture.** $D$ is either $
obreak\break 
obreak\lambda$-decomposable, or $(\lambda',\mu)$-regular for some regular $
obreak\break 
obreak\lambda'\leq\lambda$. The source says that this may be true and provides no resolution.
R023.source_name: Paolo Lipparini, “More Results on Regular Ultrafilters in ZFC”, arXiv:0810.5587 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.5587

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2008).

R023.title: The GK-pair conjecture for connected complex symmetric pairs
R023.statement:
Let $F=\mathbb{C}$ and let $(G,H)$ be a connected symmetric pair, with $H=G^\theta$ for an involution $\theta$ of a reductive group $G$. A pair is a **GK-pair** when it satisfies the Gelfand–Kazhdan property defined in the paper.

**GK-pair conjecture.** Any connected symmetric pair over $\mathbb{C}$ is a GK-pair.

The paper states that this stronger conjecture would imply van Dijk's Gelfand-pair conjecture. It in turn would follow from the conjecture that every good symmetric pair is a GK-pair, and hence from the regularity conjecture for all symmetric pairs.
R023.source_name: Avraham Aizenbud, Dmitry Gourevitch and Eitan Sayag, “Generalized Harish-Chandra descent, Gelfand pairs and an Archimedean analog of Jacquet-Rallis' Theorem”, arXiv:0812.5063 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.5063

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

R023.title: The epsilon-regularity conjecture for the almost complex Calabi–Yau equation
R023.statement:
Let $(M,\Omega)$ be a compact symplectic four-manifold equipped with an almost complex structure $J$ tamed by $\Omega$. Let $\tilde{\omega}$ be a symplectic form cohomologous to $\Omega$ and compatible with $J$, and let $\tilde{g}$ and $g$ be the metrics associated to $\tilde{\omega}$ and $\Omega$, respectively. Given a smooth volume form $\sigma$, suppose that

$$
\tilde{\omega}^2=\sigma.
$$

**Epsilon-regularity conjecture.** There exist constants $\varepsilon,C,r_0>0$, depending only on $\Omega$, $J$, and $\sigma$, such that if

$$
\frac{1}{r^2}\int_{B_g(p,r)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\tilde{g}\,dV_g\leq\varepsilon
$$

for some $p\in M$ and $0<r<r_0$, then

$$
\sup_{B_g(p,r/2)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\tilde{g}\leq\frac{C}{r^4}\int_{B_g(p,r)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\tilde{g}\,dV_g.
$$

This is motivated by epsilon-regularity for harmonic maps and is intended to provide local control toward the global estimates. The source presents it as an expectation and gives no resolution.
R023.source_name: Valentino Tosatti and Ben Weinkove, “The Calabi-Yau equation, symplectic forms and almost complex structures”, arXiv:0901.1501 (2009).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.1501

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2009).

R023.title: Automatic regularity of Butson matrices
R023.statement:
Let $H_n(l)$ be the set of $n\times n$ Hadamard matrices whose entries are $l$-th roots of unity. A Butson matrix is **regular** when the scalar product of each pair of rows decomposes as a sum of cycles, with the cycles corresponding to the prime divisors of $l$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every Butson matrix is regular.

All known examples of Butson matrices in the source appear to be regular, but the asserted automatic regularity is not established there.
R023.source_name: Teodor Banica, Julien Bichon and Jean-Marc Schlenker, “Representations of quantum permutation algebras”, arXiv:0901.2331 (2009).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2331

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2009).

R023.title: Global regularity conjecture for wave maps
R023.statement:
Let ${\mathcal S}$ be the space of classical data $(\phi_0,\phi_1)$, where $\phi_0:{\mathbf R}^2\to{\mathbf H}$ is Schwartz modulo constants and $\phi_1:{\mathbf R}^2\to T{\mathbf H}$ is Schwartz with $\phi_1(x)\in T_{\phi_0(x)}{\mathbf H}$ for every $x$. A **classical wave map** is a map $\phi:{\mathbf R}\times{\mathbf R}^2\to{\mathbf H}$ solving the wave-map equation, with initial data $\phi[0]=(\phi_0,\phi_1)$. **Global regularity for wave maps.** For every $(\phi_0,\phi_1)\in{\mathcal S}$ there exists a unique global classical wave map

$$
\phi:{\mathbf R}\times{\mathbf R}^2\to{\mathbf H}
$$

with $\phi[0]=(\phi_0,\phi_1)$. This is the global regularity problem for energy-critical wave maps from $2+1$-dimensional Minkowski space into the hyperbolic target; the paper and its predecessors aim to prove it, so the conjecture remains open in the supplied source context.
R023.source_name: Terence Tao, “Global regularity of wave maps VII. Control of delocalised or dispersed solutions”, arXiv:0908.0776 (2009).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.0776

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for secant varieties of smooth curves
R023.statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be a smooth curve of genus $g$ and degree $d \geq 2g+2k+1$. Let $\Sigma_k$ denote its $k$th secant variety, and let $\mathcal{I}_{\Sigma_k}$ be the ideal sheaf of $\Sigma_k$. **Regularity conjecture.** The regularity of $\mathcal{I}_{\Sigma_k}$ is $2k+1$ if $X$ is a rational normal curve and $2k+3$ otherwise.

This extends the known regularity result for the first secant variety. The conjecture holds for genus $0$ curves, while the result for genus $1$ is known; the general case remains open.
R023.source_name: Jessica Sidman and Peter Vermeire, “Equations defining secant varieties: geometry and computation”, arXiv:0910.0989 (2011).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.0989

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2009). “This conjecture holds for genus 0 curves, as the $k$th secant variety of a rational normal curve has ideal generated by the maximal minors of a matrix of linear forms, and thus the ideal is resolved by an Eagon-Northcott complex.”

R023.title: Benson's strong regularity conjecture for group cohomology
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime number, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$. A **very strongly quasi-regular system of parameters** is a system of parameters of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,k)$ with the stronger quasi-regularity property described in the source.

**Benson's strong regularity conjecture.** The cohomology ring $H^*(G,k)$ always contains a very strongly quasi-regular system of parameters.

Benson conjectured, and Symonds proved, that $H^*(G,k)$ has Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity zero, equivalently that it contains a strongly quasi-regular system of parameters. This stronger form remains open and is relevant to the structure of group cohomology and central essential cohomology.
R023.source_name: David J. Green and Simon A. King, “The computation of the cohomology rings of all groups of order 128”, arXiv:1001.2577 (2010).
R023.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0710.2311](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.2311), [arXiv:math/0612133](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612133).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2577

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2010).

R023.title: Asymptotic regularity bound for symbolic powers of reduced ideal sheaves
R023.statement:
Let $\mathscr{I}$ be an ideal sheaf defining a reduced subscheme $Z$ of $\mathbb{P}^n$, and let $s=s(\mathscr{I})$ be the $s$-invariant.

**Asymptotic regularity conjecture.** There is a constant $e$ such that for all $p\geq 1$, one has

$$
\operatorname{reg} \mathscr{I}^{(p)}\leq sp+e.
$$

The preceding results establish this type of linear bound under additional hypotheses, including when the non-locally-complete-intersection locus has dimension at most zero. The conjecture proposes that the same bound holds for symbolic powers of every ideal sheaf defining a reduced subscheme of projective space.
R023.source_name: Wenbo Niu, “A Vanishing Theorem and Asymptotic Regularity of Powers of Ideal Sheaves”, arXiv:1009.0314 (2011).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0911.5537](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.5537).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.0314

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

R023.title: Robust exponential decay for smooth Lorenz attractors
R023.statement: Let a Lorenz attractor be generated by a flow of regularity $C^{1+\alpha}$. **The Lorenz-attractor conjecture.** $C^{1+\alpha}$ Lorenz attractors have robust exponential decay of correlations. The preceding discussion explains that this would remove the regularity restriction used in the paper's construction of an open family with exponential decay; the conjecture remains open in the source.
R023.source_name: Vitor Araujo and Paulo Varandas, “Robust exponential decay of correlations for singular-flows”, arXiv:1101.2915 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2915

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

R023.title: The strong-versus-weak F-regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring of characteristic $p>0$, and let $I^*$ denote the tight closure of an ideal $I$ in $R$. The ring $R$ is **strongly $F$-regular** when every suitable Frobenius splitting condition holds; the source uses this standard notion.

**Strong-versus-weak F-regularity conjecture.** $R$ is strongly $F$-regular if and only if

$$
I^*=I
$$

for all ideals $I$.

A number of special cases are known, and the forward implication follows from the method cited in the source. The converse was presented as an important open problem in tight closure theory.
R023.source_name: Karl Schwede and Kevin Tucker, “A survey of test ideals”, arXiv:1104.2000 (2011).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.2000

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2011). “Perhaps the most important open problem in tight closure theory is the following.”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for uniquely $K_r$-saturated graphs
R023.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. A graph is **uniquely $K_r$-saturated** if it is $K_r$-free and adding any missing edge creates exactly one copy of $K_r$; a **dominating vertex** is a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. A graph is **regular** if all its vertices have the same degree.

**Regularity conjecture.** For each $r$, a uniquely $K_r$-saturated graph with no dominating vertex is regular.

All examples known in the source are regular, which motivates this conjecture. Its resolution is not supplied and remains open in the paper's context.
R023.source_name: Derrick Stolee, “Isomorph-free generation of 2-connected graphs with applications”, arXiv:1104.5261 (2011).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.5261

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2011).

R023.title: The equations, resolution, and regularity conjecture for Kalman varieties
R023.statement:
Fix $d$. For $s=1,\dots,d$, let $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}_{s,d,n}$ be the normalization of the corresponding Kalman variety and define

$$
B_s=\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}_{s,d,n}\left(-\frac{s(s-1)}{2}\right).
$$

**Kalman-variety resolution conjecture.** There is a long exact sequence

$$
0\to\mathcal{O}_{1,d,n}\to B_1\to B_2\to\cdots\to B_d\to0.
$$

Furthermore, the ideal of $\mathcal{O}_{1,d,n}$ has minimal generators in degrees $d,d+1,\dots,\frac{d(d+1)}{2}$, the projective dimension of $\mathcal{O}_{1,d,n}$ is $d(n-d)-d+1$, and its regularity is $\frac{d(d+1)}{2}-1$. This conjecture predicts simultaneously an exact-sequence description, the generator degrees, the projective dimension, and the regularity of these Kalman varieties; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Steven V Sam, “Equations and syzygies of some Kalman varieties”, arXiv:1105.5756 (2011).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.5756

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

R023.title: Global regularity for homogeneous Schwartz data
R023.statement: Let $(u_0,0,T)$ be a homogeneous Schwartz set of data. **Global regularity for homogeneous Schwartz data.** There exists a smooth finite energy solution $(u,p,u_0,0,T)$ with the indicated data. This is one of the standard global regularity conjectures for the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equation and concerns existence for arbitrary homogeneous Schwartz data; its resolution is not supplied here.
R023.source_name: Terence Tao, “Localisation and compactness properties of the Navier-Stokes global regularity problem”, arXiv:1108.1165 (2012).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.1165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).

R023.title: Winter–Tikuisis regularity conjecture for simple nuclear C*-algebras
R023.statement:
Let $A$ be a simple, unital, separable, nuclear, infinite-dimensional C$^*$-algebra. **Winter–Tikuisis regularity conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

1. $A$ has finite nuclear dimension.
2. $A$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable.
3. $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements.

This conjecture proposes the equivalence of the principal regularity properties used in the classification of simple nuclear C$^*$-algebras. It connects nuclear dimension, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability, and strict comparison, but the supplied source does not establish its resolution.
R023.source_name: Ilijas Farah, Andrew S. Toms and Asger Törnquist, “The descriptive set theory of C^*-algebra invariants”, arXiv:1112.3576 (2012).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1105.6074](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.6074).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.3576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2011).

R023.title: Near-extremal Reissner–Nordström–de Sitter regularity conjecture
R023.statement: Let the initial data be sufficiently close to a Reissner–Nordström–de Sitter solution whose parameters are sufficiently close to extremal but still subextremal, and let $(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}},\widetilde{g})$ be extensions supplied by the preceding stability theorem. **Near-extremal regularity conjecture.** The extensions can be chosen so that $\widetilde{g}$ is Lipschitz and the scalar field extends to $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$ as an $H^1_{\rm loc}$ function. For generic such initial data, for all subextremal values of the Reissner–Nordström–de Sitter reference solution, $\widetilde{g}$ cannot be $C^2$ and $\phi$ cannot extend $C^1$. The conjecture predicts improved metric and scalar-field regularity near extremality while retaining a lower-order singularity; it is motivated by linearized analysis and is not established in the source.
R023.source_name: Mihalis Dafermos, “Black holes without spacelike singularities”, arXiv:1201.1797 (2013).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.1797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

R023.title: Regularity and arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay conjecture for secant varieties of graph curves
R023.statement: Let $C_G$ be a graph curve embedded under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.3, and let $k$th secant variety denote the union of the linear spans of length-$k+1$ subschemes of $C_G$. **Secant-variety regularity conjecture.** Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.3, the $k$th secant variety of $C_G$ has regularity equal to $2k+1$ and is arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay. This is presented as the graph-curve analogue of a conjecture for secant varieties of smooth curves; the source does not give a resolution status.
R023.source_name: Gregory Burnham, Zvi Rosen, Jessica Sidman and Peter Vermeire, “Line arrangements modeling curves of high degree: equations, syzygies and secants”, arXiv:1201.5010 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

R023.title: Regularity of subFinsler spheres in Carnot groups
R023.statement:
Let $G_\infty$ be the asymptotic cone, equipped with its Pansu limit metric $d_\infty$, and let a Riemannian distance on $G_\infty$ be fixed. The **unit sphere** is the boundary of

$$
B_{d_\infty}(\operatorname{id},1)=\{g\in G_\infty:d_\infty(\operatorname{id},g)\leqslant 1\}.
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** The unit sphere of $d_\infty$ is rectifiable with respect to every Riemannian distance on $G_\infty$. In particular, if $G_\infty$ has topological dimension $n$, then the sphere has finite $(n-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. This remains open for general Carnot groups and is proposed because such regularity would imply the desired volume asymptotics for the associated Stoll metric.
R023.source_name: Emmanuel Breuillard and Enrico Le Donne, “On the rate of convergence to the asymptotic cone for nilpotent groups and subFinsler geometry”, arXiv:1204.1613 (2012).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.1613

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2012). “It remains an open problem for $r>2$.”

R023.title: The asymptotic minimum regularity of maximal (2,3)-antichains
R023.statement: A **maximal $(2,3)$-antichain** on $n$ points is a family of subsets in which every member has size $2$ or $3$, no member contains another, and which is maximal under these conditions. Its **regularity** is the common number of members containing each point. The authors construct such antichains with regularity $(13n/14-2)$ for every $n\equiv 0\pmod{14}$. **The asymptotic minimum-regularity conjecture.** The smallest possible regularity of a maximal $(2,3)$-antichain on $n$ points is $(13/14+o(1))n^2$. This conjecture asserts that the first construction in the theorem is asymptotically optimal; determining the exact minimum regularity remains open.
R023.source_name: Thomas Kalinowski, Uwe Leck, Christian Reiher and Ian T. Roberts, “Minimizing the regularity of maximal regular antichains of 2- and 3-sets”, arXiv:1206.3752 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.3752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

R023.title: The in-degree bound for arc-coloured digraph constructions
R023.statement:
Let $D=(N,A_0\cup A_1)$ be an arc-coloured digraph. Suppose every triangle has the form

$$
\{u,v,w\}\text{ with }(u,v),(v,w)\in A_0\text{ and }(u,w)\in A_1
$$

or

$$
\{u,v,w\}\text{ with }(u,v),(v,w)\in A_1\text{ and }(u,w)\in A_0,
$$

and every node has exactly $d$ incoming arcs in each of $A_0$ and $A_1$. **The in-degree bound conjecture.** Then

$$
d\leqslant \lvert N\rvert/7.
$$

This would establish that $13n/14$ is best possible for the class of constructions described in the paper. The conjecture is presented as a first step toward the asymptotic minimum-regularity conjecture for maximal $(2,3)$-antichains, and no resolution is supplied.
R023.source_name: Thomas Kalinowski, Uwe Leck, Christian Reiher and Ian T. Roberts, “Minimizing the regularity of maximal regular antichains of 2- and 3-sets”, arXiv:1206.3752 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.3752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for simple nuclear C*-algebras
R023.statement:
Let $A$ be a simple nuclear separable unital infinite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra. The properties of having **finite nuclear dimension**, being **$\mathcal{Z}$-stable**, and having **strict comparison** are defined for $A$ by the three conditions below. **Regularity conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

$$
\begin{array}{ll}
(1) & A\text{ has finite nuclear dimension};\\
(2) & A\text{ is }\mathcal{Z}\text{-stable};\\
(3) & A\text{ has strict comparison}.
\end{array}
$$

The conjecture proposes equivalence among central regularity properties used in the classification of simple nuclear separable $C^*$-algebras. The implications $(1)\Longrightarrow(2)$ and $(2)\Longrightarrow(3)$ had been established by the third named author and Rørdam, respectively, while the reverse implications and hence the full equivalence were unresolved in the source.
R023.source_name: Andrew Toms, Stuart White and Wilhelm Winter, “Z-stability and finite dimensional tracial boundaries”, arXiv:1209.3292 (2012).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2012). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0903.4914](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.4914).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.3292

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2012).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for critical graphs at maximum degree eight
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a critical graph, meaning that deleting any vertex lowers its chromatic number, with chromatic number $\chi$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every critical graph with

$$
\chi \geq \Delta = 8
$$

is regular.

The conjecture is motivated by the absence of known critical, or connected even, counterexamples to the Borodin–Kostochka conjecture for $\Delta=8$ other than a regular example. Its status is left unresolved in the source.
R023.source_name: Landon Rabern, “Coloring graphs with dense neighborhoods”, arXiv:1209.3646 (2012).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.3646

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2012).

R023.title: Conjecture on semiperfect quasi-$\pi_\infty$-regularity of finitely presented algebra extensions
R023.statement:
Let $S\in\mathscr{L}\!\mathscr{T}_2$ be a semiperfect quasi-$\pi_\infty$-regular ring, and let $\varphi:S\to R$ be a ring homomorphism. Regard $R$ as a right $S$-module via $\varphi$, and let $\mathcal{I}_S$ denote the relevant family of ideals. Assume that $R$ is finitely presented and Hausdorff as a right $S$-module, and that for every $r\in R$ and $I\in\mathcal{I}_S$ there is $J\in\mathcal{I}_S$ such that

$$
R\varphi(J)r\subseteq R\varphi(I).
$$

**Semiperfect quasi-$\pi_\infty$-regularity conjecture.** Then $R$ is semiperfect and quasi-$\pi_\infty$-regular with respect to some topology. The condition on $J$ ensures that the topology on $R$ generated by cosets of the left ideals $R\varphi(I)$ is a ring topology.
R023.source_name: Uriya A. First, “Semi-Invariant Subrings”, arXiv:1212.2124 (2013).
R023.references:

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2012).

R023.title: Higher regularity conjecture for quasisymmetric maps between relative Schottky sets
R023.statement:
Let $S$ and $\tilde S$ be relative Schottky sets of measure zero, not necessarily contained in Jordan domains, and let $f:S\to\tilde S$ be an orientation-preserving quasisymmetric map. A derivative at $p\in S$ is understood in the sense of

$$
f'(p)=\lim_{q\to p,\,q\in S}\frac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}.
$$

**Higher regularity conjecture.** The map $f$ is conformal at every point $p\in S$ and belongs to $C^{\infty}(S)$; that is, derivatives of all orders exist on $S$ in the sense of the displayed limit.

The conjecture predicts smooth regularity beyond the established conformality and local bi-Lipschitz continuity for quasisymmetric maps between relative Schottky sets of measure zero in Jordan domains. It is motivated by the cited work of Heinonen and Sullivan and is stated here for relative Schottky sets without the Jordan-domain assumption.
R023.source_name: Sergei Merenkov, “Planar relative Schottky sets and quasisymmetric maps”, arXiv:1305.4158 (2013).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.4158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

R023.title: The p-harmonic boundary extension conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $1 < p \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $X$ be a metric measure space. Let $\Delta_p(X)$ denote the $p$-harmonic boundary of $X$, and let $BD^p(X)$ and $HBD^p(X)$ denote the bounded Royden algebra and bounded $p$-harmonic Royden algebra, respectively. For $x \in \Delta_p(X)$, let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in $X$ converging to $x$. **The p-harmonic boundary extension conjecture.** If $f$ is a continuous function on $\Delta_p(X)$, then there exists a $p$-harmonic function $h$ on $X$ such that

$$
\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} h(x_n) = f(x).
$$

Moreover, if $f \in BD^p(X)$, then $h \in HBD^p(X)$ and $h=f$ on $\Delta_p(X)$. The conjecture proposes an extension result without the $(p,p)$-Sobolev inequality assumed earlier in the paper; the source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Marcello Lucia and Michael Puls, “The p-Royden and p-harmonic boundaries for metric measure spaces”, arXiv:1309.3596 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3596

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

R023.title: Strong regularity conjecture for the graph of integral distances
R023.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ be the quadratic form defining the integral-distance graph on $\mathbb{F}_q^m$, and let $\mathcal{A}(m,q)$ denote the corresponding common-neighbor count for nonisotropic pairs. If $\mathcal{B}(m,q)$ denotes the number of common neighbors of $0$ and an element $v$ with $\langle v,v\rangle=0$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^m\backslash\{0,v\}$, then for $m\ge 2$ we have

$$
\mathcal{B}(m,q)=\begin{cases}
\mathcal{A}(m,q)&\text{for }m\text{ even},\\
\mathcal{A}(m,q)-(-1)^{\frac{(q-1)(m-1)}{4}}\cdot q^{\frac{m-3}{2}}\cdot\frac{q^2-1}{4}& \text{for }m\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Strong regularity conjecture.** For even dimension $m$, the graph of integral distances $\mathfrak{G}_{m,q}$ is a strongly regular graph. The conjecture predicts that the common-neighbor counts needed for strong regularity agree in even dimension; the odd-dimensional correction term explains why the corresponding assertion is not made there.
R023.source_name: Sascha Kurz and Harald Meyer, “Integral point sets in higher dimensional affine spaces over finite fields”, arXiv:1401.4348 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.4348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

R023.title: Navier–Stokes global regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $u_0: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be a divergence-free vector field in the Schwartz class. A smooth vector field $u: [0,+\infty) \times \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a smooth function $p: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ should exist such that

$$
\partial_t u + (u \cdot \nabla)u = \nu \Delta u - \nabla p, \qquad \nabla \cdot u = 0, \qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,
$$

for every $\nu>0$, together with $u \in L^\infty_t L^2_x([0,T] \times \mathbb{R}^3)$ for every $0<T<\infty$.

**Navier–Stokes global regularity conjecture.** For every $\nu>0$ and every such initial data $u_0$, such a global smooth finite-energy solution exists.

This is the three-dimensional homogeneous global regularity problem for the Navier–Stokes equations. The paper uses finite-time blowup for an averaged equation to identify a supercriticality barrier; the conjecture itself remains unresolved.
R023.source_name: Terence Tao, “Finite time blowup for an averaged three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation”, arXiv:1402.0290 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.0290

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

R023.title: Polynomial bound relating homological degree and regularity
R023.statement:
Let $A$ be a standard graded algebra of dimension $d$, and let $\operatorname{hdeg}(A)$ and $\operatorname{reg}(A)$ denote its homological degree and Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity.

**Homological-degree regularity conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $f(t)$ of degree $d$ such that

$$
\operatorname{hdeg}(A)<f(\operatorname{reg}(A)).
$$

The source notes that this holds for one known homological-degree function and asks for such a polynomial bound in general; no resolution is given.
R023.source_name: Wolmer V. Vasconcelos, “Complexity Degrees of Algebraic Structures”, arXiv:1402.1906 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1906

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for weakly closed graphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected weakly closed graph, let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]$, and let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal. Let $\ell$ denote the length of the longest induced path of $G$. **Regularity conjecture for weakly closed graphs.** If the longest induced path of $G$ has length $\ell$, then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/J_G)=\ell.
$$

The claim extends the corresponding result for connected closed graphs and the authors establish it for trees, where the relevant graphs are precisely caterpillar trees; the supplied text reports that the general weakly closed-graph case is motivated by computer experiments and leaves it as a conjecture.
R023.source_name: Faryal Chaudhry, Ahmet Dokuyucu and Rida Irfan, “On the binomial edge ideals of block graphs”, arXiv:1402.2041 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2041

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

R023.title: Isett's generic energy-profile regularity conjecture for Hölder Euler flows
R023.statement:
Let $\alpha<1/3$. Consider weak periodic solutions of the incompressible Euler equations in the class $v\in C_tC_x^\alpha(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^n)$, and define their energy profile by

$$
e(t)=\int_{\mathbb{T}^n}|v|^2(t,x)\,dx.
$$

**Generic energy-profile regularity conjecture.** A generic solution with regularity at most $1/3$ fails to conserve energy and has an energy profile of minimal regularity. More precisely, for every $\alpha<1/3$, there exists a solution such that

$$
e\notin W^{2\alpha/(1-\alpha)+\epsilon,p}(I)
$$

for every $\epsilon>0$, $p\geq1$, and every open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$; moreover, the set of all such solutions is residual in the space of weak solutions in $C_tC_x^\alpha(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}^n)$ endowed with the topology induced by the $C_tC_x^\alpha$ norm. This strengthens Onsager's conjecture by prescribing the sharp failure of energy-profile regularity; the source presents it as a main concern, and the parser supplies no evidence of resolution.
R023.source_name: Philip Isett and Sung-Jin Oh, “On Nonperiodic Euler Flows with Hölder Regularity”, arXiv:1402.2305 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2305

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for amenable d-sequences
R023.statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M$ a finite unmixed $R$-module. Let ${\mathbf x}=x_1,\ldots,x_r$ be a partial system of parameters of $M$. The sequence ${\mathbf x}$ is **amenable** relative to $M$ if the Koszul homology module $\mathrm{H}_1({\mathbf x};M)$ has finite length, and it is a **d-sequence** relative to $M$ in the sense used in the source. Set

$$
\mathrm{G}=\operatorname{gr}_{({\mathbf x})}(R).
$$

**Regularity conjecture for amenable d-sequences.** If ${\mathbf x}$ is an amenable d-sequence relative to $M$,

$$
\dim \mathrm{H}^0_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{gr}_{({\mathbf x})}(M))=r
$$

and $\mathrm{j}_1({\mathbf x};M)=0$, then ${\mathbf x}$ is a regular sequence on $M$.

The claim is a proposed sufficient condition for regularity in the study of partial systems of parameters and Hilbert coefficients of $j$-transforms. The supplied status evidence says that this statement is disproved, so the asserted implication does not hold in general.
R023.source_name: Shiro Goto, Jooyoun Hong and Wolmer V. Vasconcelos, “Hilbert polynomials of j-transforms”, arXiv:1403.6549 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.6549

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2014). “Then $\xx$ is a regular sequence on $M$. } The unmixedness hypothesis serves various purposes that begin from avoiding trivial counterexamples to the enabling of several constructions for cohomological calculations.”

R023.title: The second-minimal total irregularity conjecture for connected graphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{irr}_{t}(G)$ denote its total irregularity. A graph is **regular** if all its vertices have the same degree. **Second-minimal total irregularity conjecture.** If $G$ is not a regular graph, then

$$
\operatorname{irr}_{t}(G)\geq 2n-4.
$$

The paper identifies $0$ as the minimal total irregularity, attained by regular graphs, and proposes $2n-4$ as the second-minimal value for simple connected graphs on $n$ vertices. The claim is presented as an open problem for further research.
R023.source_name: Yingxue Zhu, Lihua You and Jieshan Yang, “The Minimal Total Irregularity of Graphs”, arXiv:1404.0931 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.0931

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2014).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for $H(I,I+2)$
R023.statement:
Let $H(I,J)$ be the least positive integer $n$ such that there exist $I$ disjoint Golomb rulers, each a $J$-subset of $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$. **Regularity conjecture.** For every integer $I\geq8$,

$$
H(I,I+2)=I(I+2).
$$

Thus the conjecture predicts regular disjoint Golomb rulers in this parameter range. The paper reports that the assertion has been confirmed computationally for $I\in\\{8,\ldots,150\\}$, but treats the unrestricted statement as conjectural.
R023.source_name: Xiu Baoxin, Changjun Fan and Meilian Liang, “On Disjoint Golomb Rulers”, arXiv:1405.4535 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.4535

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2014). “Conjecture holds for any $k \in \{8, \cdots, 150\}$, which was confirmed based on Golomb rulers shown in .”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the rational functions $A_{g,r}(z)$
R023.statement:
Let $A_{g,r}(z)\in K_g(z)$ be the rational functions defined by

$$
\sum_{r\geq 1}A_{g,r}(z)T^r=(q-1)\operatorname{Log}\left(\sum_{\lambda}q^{(g-1)\langle\lambda,\lambda\rangle}J_{\lambda}(z)H_{\lambda}(z)T^{|\lambda|}\right),
$$

and let $\mu_r$ be the set of $r$th roots of unity. The associated polynomials satisfy

$$
A_{g,r,d}=-\sum_{\xi\in\mu_r}\xi^{-d}\operatorname{Res}_{z=\xi}\left(A_{g,r}(z)\frac{dz}{z}\right).
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** The rational function $A_{g,r}(z)$ is regular at every nontrivial $r$th root of unity.

Together with the fact that $A_{g,r}(z)$ is regular outside $\mu_r$ and has at most simple poles there, this is equivalent to $(1-z)A_{g,r}(z)\in K_g[z]$ and would imply that $A_{g,r,d}$ is independent of $d$. The conjecture is proved by direct computation when $r$ is prime, but is open in general.
R023.source_name: Olivier Schiffmann, “Indecomposable vector bundles and stable Higgs bundles over smooth projective curves”, arXiv:1406.3839 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.3839

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2014).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for $L^2$-Alexander torsion
R023.statement:
Let $K$ be an oriented knot, let $\pi_K$ denote its knot group, and let $\gamma\colon\pi_K\to\Gamma$ be an admissible epimorphism. **$L^2$-Alexander torsion regularity conjecture.** The function $\tau^{(2)}(K,\gamma)(t)$ is monomial in the limit, is continuous, and satisfies that

$$
\tau^{(2)}(K,\gamma)(t)\cdot\max\{1,t\}
$$

is convex.

These properties would provide the basic regularity needed to define degree and leading data for general $L^2$-Alexander torsions. The source assumes the first property later in its discussion, but does not report a resolution of the full conjecture.
R023.source_name: Jérôme Dubois, Stefan Friedl and Wolfgang Lück, “Three flavors of twisted invariants of knots”, arXiv:1410.6924 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6924

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2014). “We refer to for various other conjectures and open questions regarding the twisted Alexander torsion of hyperbolic knots.”

R023.title: Unit regularity conjecture for proatomic $*$-regular rings
R023.statement:
Let $R$ be a $*$-regular ring, and let $\overline{L}(R)$ denote its associated modular ortholattice. Suppose that $\overline{L}(R)$ is **proatomic**, meaning that it has the proatomic property considered in the source, and has an orthogonal large partial $n$-frame. A ring is **unit regular** if for every $a\in R$ there is a unit $u$ such that $aua=a$; it is **directly finite** if $xy=1$ implies $yx=1$.

**Unit-regularity conjecture.** If $R$ is $*$-regular and $\overline{L}(R)$ is proatomic with an orthogonal large partial $n$-frame, then $R$ is unit regular. Every representable ring is directly finite, and is unit regular if it is simple.

The source presents these assertions together in the discussion of regularity properties of representable rings. It gives no resolution, although it attributes a related direct-finiteness question to Handelman.
R023.source_name: Christian Herrmann and Michael S. Roddy, “Proatomic modular ortholattices: Representation and equational theory”, arXiv:1501.02477 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.02477

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

R023.title: Regularity formula for Schubert singularities
R023.statement:
Let $w=(n-r+1,n-r+2,dots,n,a_{r+1},dots,a_{n-1},N)\in\mathcal W_r$, set $a_r=n$ and $a_n=N$, and for $r\leq i\leq n-1$ define $m_i=a_{i+1}-a_i$. Thus $m_i>0$ and $mathcal U_i$ appears in $mathcal U_w$ with multiplicity $m_i$. **Regularity conjecture.** With this notation, 
$$
\operatorname{reg} \mathbb C[Y_P(w)]=\sum_{i=r}^{n-1}(m_i-1)i.
$$
 Based on the examples calculated in the paper, this predicts the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of the Schubert singularity $Y_P(w)$ from the multiplicities $m_i$; the source provides no resolution status beyond presenting it as a conjecture.
R023.source_name: Manoj Kummini, V. Lakshmibai, Pramathanath Sastry and C. S. Seshadri, “Free resolutions of some Schubert singularities”, arXiv:1504.04415 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04415

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

R023.title: The endpoint Besov regularity conjecture for periodic symmetric-stable noises
R023.statement:
Let $w_{\alpha}$ denote a periodic symmetric-$\alpha$-stable noise on $\mathbb{T}^d$, with $0<p<\alpha<2$. **The endpoint regularity conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(w_{\alpha}\in B_{p,\infty}^{d(1/\alpha-1)}(\mathbb{T}^d)\right)=1.
$$

The paper obtains regularity results below the exponent $1/\alpha-1$, while results for symmetric-stable processes on the real line motivate this endpoint assertion. Whether the stated periodic Besov regularity holds for the full range $0<p<\alpha<2$ remains open.
R023.source_name: Julien Fageot, Michael Unser and John Paul Ward, “On the Besov Regularity of Periodic Lévy Noises”, arXiv:1506.05740 (2015).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.05740

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

R023.title: Bochner–Riesz regularity conjecture for ${}_{\mathrm{S}^{d-1}}L_p^k$
R023.statement: Let ${}_{\mathrm{S}^{d-1}}L_p^k$ be the Hardy-type space associated with the unit sphere, and let the Bochner–Riesz operator of order $\lambda>0$ be given as in the source. **Bochner–Riesz regularity conjecture.** There exists $l\in\mathbb{N}$, depending on $\lambda$, such that the Bochner–Riesz operator of order $\lambda$ acts continuously from ${}_{\mathrm{S}^{d-1}}L_p^k$ to $L_p$ for every $p$ and every $k>l$. The conjecture extends known improvements in continuity properties obtained by replacing $L_p$ with ${}_{\Sigma}L_p$; its resolution is not given in the source.
R023.source_name: Dmitriy M. Stolyarov, “Functions whose Fourier transform vanishes on a surface”, arXiv:1601.04604 (2016).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.04604

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for minimizers of the extended K-energy
R023.statement: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, let $(\mathcal E^1,d_1)$ be the metric completion of the space of Kähler potentials, and let the extended Mabuchi K-energy be a map $\mathcal K:\mathcal E^1\to(-\infty,+\infty]$. A point $u\in\mathcal E^1$ is a **minimizer** of $\mathcal K$ if it attains the infimum of $\mathcal K$ on $\mathcal E^1$. A Kähler metric is **constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK)** if its scalar curvature is constant. **Regularity conjecture.** If $u$ is a minimizer of the extended K-energy, then $u$ is a smooth cscK metric. This conjecture is presented as the regularity question linked to the general modified properness conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution.
R023.source_name: Robert J. Berman, Tamás Darvas and Chinh H. Lu, “Regularity of weak minimizers of the K-energy and applications to properness and K-stability”, arXiv:1602.03114 (2018).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1510.01260](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.01260).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03114

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2016). “It was proved in this context in , and this paper also linked the resolution of the general conjecture to a regularity question on weak minimizers of the K-energy that we elaborate now.”

R023.title: Minkowski's measure regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $Q$ be Minkowski's question-mark function on $[0,1]$, and let $\b5$ be the singular-continuous measure whose distribution function is $Q$, so that

$$
Q(x)=\int_0^x d\mu.
$$

**Minkowski's measure regularity conjecture.** Minkowski's measure $\mu$ is regular in the sense of Ullman--Stahl--Totik. This is a problem in logarithmic potential theory and orthogonal polynomials; the paper gives theoretical arguments and numerical evidence, but no proof is supplied.
R023.source_name: Giorgio Mantica, “Minkowski's Question Mark Measure”, arXiv:1603.05815 (2016).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05815

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

R023.title: Boundary regularity conjecture for the Liouville density of the discrete Gaussian free field
R023.statement: Let $D$ be a domain, let $t\in\mathbb R$, and let $\rho^D(t,\mathord\cdot)$ denote the density from Theorem 2.7. **Boundary regularity conjecture.** For each $t\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto\rho^D(t,x)$ is bounded and tends to zero as $x$ approaches $\partial D$. In particular, the function admits a continuous extension to all of $\overline D$. The preceding results establish absolute continuity of the relevant measure and an integrability condition for this density, but do not determine its boundary regularity; the conjecture is motivated by the stated asymptotics and simulations.
R023.source_name: Marek Biskup and Oren Louidor, “Full extremal process, cluster law and freezing for the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian Free Field”, arXiv:1606.00510 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00510

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

R023.title: The local-cohomology regularity equality conjecture for degree-wise coherent FI_G-modules
R023.statement:
Let $V$ be a degree-wise coherent ${\mathscr{FI}}_G$-module, let $H^i_\mathfrak{m}(V)$ denote its local cohomology modules, and let $\operatorname{reg}(V)$ and $\deg(H^i_\mathfrak{m}(V))$ denote its regularity and the degree of its local cohomology modules. **The local-cohomology regularity conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg}(V)=\max_i\{\deg(H^i_\mathfrak{m}(V))+i\}.
$$

The preceding corollary establishes the corresponding inequality. The conjecture is the FI_G-module analogue of the classical local-cohomology formula for regularity over a polynomial ring; the equality remains to be proved in the stated setting.
R023.source_name: Eric Ramos, “On the degree-wise coherence of FI_G-modules”, arXiv:1606.04514 (2016).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04514

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

R023.title: Fractional Triebel–Lizorkin regularity conjecture for principal Beltrami solutions
R023.statement:
Let $0<s<2$ and $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $s<\frac{2}{p}$. Let $\mu,\nu\in F^s_{p,q}\cap L^\infty_c$ satisfy the ellipticity condition, and let $f$ be the principal solution to the Beltrami equation. Here $p_\kappa$ and $p_\kappa'$ denote the exponents associated with the ellipticity parameter $\kappa$. **Regularity conjecture.** If

$$
\frac{1}{p}<\frac{1}{p_\kappa'},
$$

then

$$
\bar{\partial}f\in F^s_{p,q}\qquad\text{for every }\frac{1}{q}>\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p_\kappa}.
$$

The conjecture seeks the optimal Triebel–Lizorkin regularity of the derivative of a principal Beltrami solution in the subcritical range; the stated result would improve the previously known critical-space estimates under the indicated exponent restriction.
R023.source_name: Martí Prats, “Beltrami equations in the plane and Sobolev regularity”, arXiv:1606.07751 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07751

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

R023.title: The monotonicity-free approximation regularity conjecture for conformal iterated function systems
R023.statement: Let $\Phi$ be an iterated function system with attractor $X$, and let $\theta$ range over the class of functions used in the definition of an approximation regular pair. Theorem 1.2 asserts approximation regularity under the stated monotonicity assumptions. **Monotonicity-free approximation regularity conjecture.** Theorem 1.2 should hold with no underlying monotonicity assumptions on the class of $\theta$. This asks whether the monotonicity restrictions in approximation regularity can be removed, analogous to the Duffin–Schaeffer problem. The source does not provide a resolution of this conjecture.
R023.source_name: Simon Baker, “An analogue of Khintchine's theorem for self-conformal sets”, arXiv:1609.04588 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04588

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2016).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for Diophantine quadruples
R023.statement:
Let $\{a,b,c,d\}$ be a **Diophantine quadruple**, meaning that each of $ab+1$, $ac+1$, $ad+1$, $bc+1$, $bd+1$, and $cd+1$ is a perfect square. Suppose that $ab+1=r^2$, $ac+1=s^2$, and $bc+1=t^2$, and define

$$
d_+=a+b+c+2abc+2rst.
$$

**The regularity conjecture for Diophantine quadruples.** If $d>\max\{a,b,c\}$, then $d=d_+$. All known Diophantine quadruples were regular when this conjecture was formulated, and the source describes it as a stronger version of the nonexistence theorem for Diophantine quintuples that remained open there.
R023.source_name: Bo He, Alain Togbè and Volker Ziegler, “There is no Diophantine quintuple”, arXiv:1610.04020 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.04020

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for intersected polynomial factors
R023.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For any nondecreasing function $r':\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ and parameters $\delta,\eta,r,d$, there exists a constant $K$ such that a polynomial factor $\mathcal{B}$ of $V$, given by the decomposition theorem, has the following property. If $\mathcal{B}$ is defined by polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_C$, define

$$
\Delta_hP_i(x)=P_i(x+h)-P_i(x)-P_i(h)
$$

for $1\leq i\leq C$, and let $S$ be the set of $h\in V$ for which the factor defined by $P_1,\dots,P_C,\Delta_hP_1,\dots,\Delta_hP_C$ is $r'$-regular. **Regularity conjecture.** $S$ contains a subspace of $V$ of codimension at most $K$.

This conjecture is introduced as an additional assumption for a conditional result verifying the critical-threshold conjecture in the case $N=N_{\ell,c,1}$. Its general status is not resolved in the source.
R023.source_name: Sammy Luo, “A Counting Lemma for Binary Matroids and Applications to Extremal Problems”, arXiv:1610.09587 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09587

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

R023.title: The two-thirds regularity conjecture for prime knots
R023.statement:
Let $\operatorname{cr}(X)$ denote the crossing number of a knot $X$. A prime knot $P$ is **$\lambda$-regular** if

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K)\geq \lambda\cdot\operatorname{cr}(P)
$$

whenever $P$ is a factor of a knot $K$. **Two-thirds regularity conjecture.** Each prime knot is $\frac23$-regular. The paper records Lackenby's result that every knot is $\frac1{152}$-regular and studies the consequences of the stronger conjecture; no resolution is supplied.
R023.source_name: Andrei Malyutin, “On the question of genericity of hyperbolic knots”, arXiv:1612.03368 (2016).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.03368

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

R023.title: Precise Gevrey regularity of invariant manifolds at parabolic infinity in restricted three-body problems
R023.statement: In the Sitnikov problem, let $e\in(0,1)$ denote the eccentricity, and in the restricted planar three-body problem (RPTBP), let $\mu\in(0,1/2]$ denote the mass parameter. An invariant manifold at **parabolic infinity** is an invariant manifold associated with the parabolic fixed point at infinity. **Precise Gevrey-regularity conjecture.** The parabolic infinity in the Sitnikov problem, with $e\in(0,1)$, and in the RPTBP, with $\mu\in(0,1/2]$, possesses invariant manifolds which are precisely $1/3$-Gevrey, that is, they are not $\gamma'$-Gevrey for any $0\leq\gamma'<1/3$. The preceding results establish $1/3$-Gevrey upper bounds, while numerical computations and an explicit time-periodic example motivate the conjecture that these bounds are optimal; the required lower bounds are not proved here.
R023.source_name: Inmaculada Baldomá, Ernest Fontich and Pau Martín, “Gevrey estimates for one dimensional parabolic invariant manifolds of non-hyperbolic fixed points”, arXiv:1702.05961 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

R023.title: Asymptotic upper-bound conjecture for distant irregularity strength
R023.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and without an isolated edge. Write $s_r(G)$ for the least number of colours needed in an edge-colouring whose induced vertex sums distinguish vertices at distance at most $r$. The **asymptotic distant-irregularity conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 2$ and each such graph $G$,

$$
s_r(G)\leq (1+o(1))\Delta^{r-1}.
$$

Here the asymptotic term is with respect to the relevant growth of $\Delta$. The conjecture is presented as an asymptotically optimal upper bound, while the supplied text gives no resolution. It concerns improving the second-order terms in the paper's bounds, particularly for graphs with relatively large minimum degree.
R023.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “Distant irregularity strength of graphs with bounded minimum degree”, arXiv:1703.02787 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02787

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2017). “The conjecture is still open, while thus far the following general upper bounds were subsequently proved: $s_1(G)\leq 30$ in , $s_1(G)\leq 16$ in , $s_1(G)\leq 13$ in , and finally $s_1(G)\leq 5$ from .”

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for the $k$-abelian complexity of automatic sequences
R023.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $\omega$ be an $\ell$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $\ell$-kernel is finite. The $k$-abelian complexity of $\omega$ is the sequence counting the $k$-abelian equivalence classes of factors of each length.

**Automatic-sequence regularity conjecture.** The $k$-abelian complexity of any $\ell$-automatic sequence is an $\ell$-regular sequence.

The conjecture generalizes the previously conjectured—and independently proved—case of the $2$-abelian complexity of the Thue–Morse sequence. The paper presents the $3$-regularity of the $k$-abelian complexity of the Cantor sequence as supporting evidence; the general assertion remains open in the supplied source.
R023.source_name: Jin Chen, Xiaotao Lü and Wen Wu, “On the k-abelian complexity of the Cantor sequence”, arXiv:1703.04063 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04063

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2017). “This is proved in and independently.”

R023.title: Diregularity conjecture for geodetic cages
R023.statement:
A $(d,k,+\epsilon)$-digraph is a digraph with minimum out-degree at least $d$, diameter parameter $k$, and excess $\epsilon$. A **geodetic cage** is a $(d,k,+\epsilon)$-digraph with smallest possible excess; a digraph is **diregular** when its in-degree and out-degree are constant and equal.

**Diregularity conjecture.** All geodetic cages are diregular.

This conjecture asserts that the smallest-excess digraphs in this setting have uniform in- and out-degree. The paper notes that all $(2,2)$-geodetic cages are diregular, but does not establish the claim in general.
R023.source_name: James Tuite, “Digraphs with degree two and excess two are diregular”, arXiv:1703.08739 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08739

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

R023.title: Chen's regularity conjecture for K-energy minimizers
R023.statement:
Let $(M,[\omega],J)$ be a compact Kähler manifold, let

$$
\mathcal H_\omega=\{\phi\in C^\infty(M):\omega_\phi=\omega+\sqrt{-1}\partial\bar\partial\phi>0\},
$$

and let $\mathcal K$ be the K-energy on Kähler potentials. A $C^{1,\bar 1}$ potential is a weak Kähler potential whose complex Hessian is bounded, and a minimizer of $\mathcal K$ is one attaining the minimum in the given Kähler class. **Chen's conjecture.** A $C^{1,\bar 1}$ minimizer in a given Kähler class of the K-energy is a smooth Kähler metric with constant scalar curvature. The cited work proves this regularity statement in part by showing that weak CSCK solutions with a uniform $L^\infty$ bound are smooth; the supplied evidence indicates that the broader conjecture is regarded as resolved through the known minimizer and convexity results.
R023.source_name: Weiyong He and Yu Zeng, “Constant scalar curvature equation and the regularity of its weak solution”, arXiv:1705.01236 (2017).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1506.06423](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06423).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01236

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2017).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for Burau images of pure braids in $B_4$
R023.statement: Let $B_4$ be the braid group on four strands, let $\rho$ denote the representation used in the paper, and let $T_4$ be the object on which the braid acts. For a Laurent polynomial, write its lowest degree for the least exponent of its variable. Let $\Delta$ and $a$ be the braids appearing in the statement, and let $\sigma\in B_4$ be a non-trivial pure braid not equivalent to $\Delta^m$ for any $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $\sigma$ acts non-trivially on $T_4$. **Regularity conjecture.** There exist sufficiently large $l_0\in\mathbb{N}$, depending on the length of $\sigma$, and sufficiently large $m_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $m>m_0$ and $l\ge l_0$, the Laurent polynomials $\rho_{11}(a^m\sigma a^{-l})$ and $\rho_{31}(a^m\sigma a^{-l})$ are non-zero and the difference of their lowest degrees is equal to $-1$. The conjecture records an experimentally observed regularity in these matrix entries of Burau images; its resolution would clarify the structure of images of braids of this special form, but no resolution is supplied here.
R023.source_name: A. Beridze and P. Traczyk, “Forks, Noodles and the Burau representation for n=4”, arXiv:1705.02641 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02641

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

R023.title: F-regularity conjecture for nearly commuting matrix components
R023.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be $n\times n$ matrices of indeterminates over a field $K$, let $R=K[X,Y]$, and let $I$ be generated by the off-diagonal entries $u_{ij}$ of $XY-YX$. Let $P=\operatorname{Rad}(J)$, where $J$ is generated by all entries of $XY-YX$, and let $Q$ be the other minimal prime of $I$.

**F-regularity conjecture for nearly commuting matrices.** The rings

$$
R/P,\qquad R/Q,\qquad R/(P+Q)
$$

are $F$-regular.

The conjecture is motivated by computer-algebra experiments and is stated to hold when $n=2$. The source explains that, under a linkage reduction, it suffices to establish the $F$-regularity of $R/(P+Q)$, while the general case remains unresolved there.
R023.source_name: Zhibek Kadyrsizova, “Nearly Commuting Matrices”, arXiv:1705.10957 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.10957

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2017). “A. Knutson in his paper conjectured that $\mathbb{V}(I)$ has only two irreducible components and it was proved in all characteristics by H.Young in his thesis, .”

R023.title: F-regularity conjecture for the irreducible polynomial of a generic matrix
R023.statement:
Let $X=(x_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ matrix of indeterminates over a field $K$, and let $\mathcal{P}(X)$ be the irreducible polynomial specified in the source's Definition `poly`.

**F-regularity conjecture for $\mathcal{P}(X)$.** The quotient ring

$$
K[X]/\mathcal{P}(X)
$$

is $F$-regular.

This is one of the source's proposed conjectures about rings arising from the nearly commuting-matrix calculations. The defining polynomial is not included in the supplied context, and no resolution is stated.
R023.source_name: Zhibek Kadyrsizova, “Nearly Commuting Matrices”, arXiv:1705.10957 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.10957

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2017). “A. Knutson in his paper conjectured that $\mathbb{V}(I)$ has only two irreducible components and it was proved in all characteristics by H.Young in his thesis, .”

R023.title: F-regularity conjecture for partial commutator ideals
R023.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be $n\times n$ matrices of indeterminates over a field $K$, let $R=K[X,Y]$, and let $u_{ij}$ be the off-diagonal entries of $XY-YX$. For a subset

$$
Z\subseteq\{u_{ij}\mid 1\leq i\neq j\leq n\}
$$

of cardinality at most $n^2-n-1$, let $\mathcal{I}_Z$ be the ideal of $R$ generated by the elements of $Z$.

**F-regularity conjecture for partial commutator ideals.** The quotient $R/\mathcal{I}_Z$ is $F$-regular. In particular, $\mathcal{I}_Z$ is a prime ideal.

This predicts strong singularity properties for every proper partial collection of the off-diagonal commutator equations. The source gives no verification or resolution for the general values of $n$ and $Z$.
R023.source_name: Zhibek Kadyrsizova, “Nearly Commuting Matrices”, arXiv:1705.10957 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.10957

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2017). “A. Knutson in his paper conjectured that $\mathbb{V}(I)$ has only two irreducible components and it was proved in all characteristics by H.Young in his thesis, .”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for Butson matrices
R023.statement: A partial complex Hadamard matrix $H\in M_{M\times N}(\mathbb T)$ is regular when the scalar products between its rows decompose as sums of cycles. A Butson matrix is a complex Hadamard matrix whose entries are roots of unity of finite order. **Regularity conjecture.** Any Butson matrix $H\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ is regular. Thus a vanishing sum of roots of unity that is not a sum of cycles cannot be used to construct a complex Hadamard matrix. The conjecture is presented as a difficult question with substantial computer evidence, but no proof is given.
R023.source_name: Teodor Banica, Duygu Ozteke and Lorenzo Pittau, “Isolated partial Hadamard matrices, and related topics”, arXiv:1706.00986 (2017).
R023.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1302.4153](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.4153), [arXiv:1109.4888](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.4888).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00986

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

R023.title: Ene–Herzog–Hibi regularity conjecture for binomial edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $J_G$ be its binomial edge ideal, and let $\operatorname{in}_{<_{\mathrm{lex}}}(J_G)$ be its initial ideal with respect to the lexicographic order. **Ene–Herzog–Hibi's conjecture.**

$$
\reg(J_G)=\reg\bigl(\operatorname{in}_{<_{\mathrm{lex}}}(J_G)\bigr).
$$

This is a partial form of a broader conjecture concerning the extremal Betti numbers of $J_G$ and its initial ideal. The paper proves the equality for additional classes through closure under graph joins, but the general assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: Sara Saeedi Madani and Dariush Kiani, “Binomial edge ideals of regularity 3”, arXiv:1706.09002 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09002

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

R023.title: Benzi's single-temperature walk-regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Benzi's conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists $\beta>0$ such that

$$
S^V(G,\beta)=\log n_G.
$$

Benzi's earlier theorem proves the implication from equality of the walk entropy on any set of real temperatures having an accumulation point; this conjecture asks whether one positive temperature suffices and remains open in the source.
R023.source_name: Kyle Kloster, Daniel Král' and Blair D. Sullivan, “Walk entropy and walk-regularity”, arXiv:1708.09700 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

R023.title: Estrada's walk-regularity conjecture at temperature one
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Estrada's conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if

$$
S^V(G,1)=\log n_G.
$$

The paper proves that some positive temperature has this characterization, but does not identify such a temperature explicitly; temperature $1$ is presented as an open conjectural choice.
R023.source_name: Kyle Kloster, Daniel Král' and Blair D. Sullivan, “Walk entropy and walk-regularity”, arXiv:1708.09700 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

R023.title: Rational-temperature walk-regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Rational-temperature conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists a rational $\beta>0$ such that

$$
S^V(G,\beta)=\log n_G.
$$

The preceding result shows that a non-walk-regular graph can attain maximum walk entropy at only finitely many positive temperatures, while the source offers this rational-temperature strengthening as a further conjecture.
R023.source_name: Kyle Kloster, Daniel Král' and Blair D. Sullivan, “Walk entropy and walk-regularity”, arXiv:1708.09700 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.09700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

R023.title: Low-regularity scattering conjecture for defocusing nonlinear wave equations
R023.statement:
Let $s_c\geq0$, $mu=-1$, and let $(u_0,u_1)\in\dot{H}^{s_c}\times\dot{H}^{s_c-1}$. **Low regularity conjecture.** The corresponding solution $u$ is global and scatters: there exist unique $(u_0^{\pm},u_1^{\pm})\in\dot{H}^{s_c}_x(\mathbb{R}^d)\times\dot{H}^{s_c-1}$ such that

$$
\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\|u(t)-S(t)(u_0^{\pm},u_1^{\pm})\|_{\dot{H}_x^{s_c}(\mathbb{R}^d)}=0.
$$

This asserts global scattering for arbitrary data at the critical regularity, without assuming an a priori critical-norm bound. It is presented as an open extension of the critical-norm results.
R023.source_name: Changxing Miao and Jiqiang Zheng, “Dynamics of nonlinear wave equations”, arXiv:1711.01172 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.01172

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017).

R023.title: Persistence of singular-hyperbolic large deviations for $C^1$ flows
R023.statement: Consider the statements of Theorem~ and the sectional-hyperbolic attracting-set conjecture for $C^2$ flows. **$C^1$ regularity conjecture.** The statements of Theorem~ and Conjecture~ should remain valid for $C^1$ flows. The source raises this as a regularity question and gives no resolution; in particular, the conjectured extension to $C^1$ flows remains open here.
R023.source_name: Vitor Araujo, Andressa Souza and Edvan Trindade, “Upper large deviations bound for singular-hyperbolic attracting sets”, arXiv:1711.09626 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09626

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

R023.title: Gevrey regularity conjecture for the parametrization of invariant circles
R023.statement: Let $u_{\varepsilon}$ denote the parametrization of the quasi-periodic invariant circle for the dissipative standard map, viewed as a function of the complex parameter $\varepsilon$. **Gevrey-regularity conjecture.** The parametrization $u_{\varepsilon}$ belongs, as a function of $\varepsilon$, to a Gevrey class $G^\sigma$ whose index $\sigma$ is close to $1$. The formal series is not analytic in a neighborhood of $\varepsilon=0$, because no ball around the origin has a convergent formal power series, but the numerical coefficient growth suggests regularity very close to the analytic class; the precise Gevrey index remains unspecified.
R023.source_name: Adrian P. Bustamante and Renato C. Calleja, “Computation of Domains of Analyticity for the dissipative standard map in the limit of small dissipation”, arXiv:1712.05476 (2017).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

R023.title: Regularity suffices for recoverability in product-topology codes
R023.statement:
Let $T_{m,n}(a,b,0)$ be the product topology on an $m\times n$ array, and let an erasure pattern $E\subseteq [m]\times[n]$ be **regular** if, for every $U\subseteq[m]$ and $V\subseteq[n]$ with $|U|=u$ and $|V|=v$, 

$$
|E\cap(U\times V)|\leq uv-\max(u-a,0)\max(v-b,0).
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** For the topology $T_{m,n}(a,b,0)$, if an erasure pattern is regular, then it is recoverable.

This conjecture extends the established necessity of regularity for recoverability and the known sufficiency result when $a=1$. It asks whether the regularity condition exactly characterizes recoverable erasure patterns for arbitrary $a$ and $b$.
R023.source_name: D. Shivakrishna, V. Arvind Rameshwar, V. Lalitha and Birenjith Sasidharan, “On Maximally Recoverable Codes for Product Topologies”, arXiv:1801.03379 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.03379

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

R023.title: The additive-complexity regularity conjecture for automatic sequences
R023.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $\mathbf{w}=w_0w_1w_2\cdots$ be a $k$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $k$-kernel

$$
\{(w_{k^e n+c})_{n\geq 0}\mid e\geq 0,\ 0\leq c<k^e\}
$$

is finite. For each $n\geq 1$, let $\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n)$ denote the number of distinct digit sums of the length-$n$ factors occurring in $\mathbf{w}$. A sequence is **$k$-regular** if the $\mathbb{Z}$-module generated by its $k$-kernel is finitely generated.

**Additive-complexity regularity conjecture.** The sequence $(\rho^+_{\mathbf{w}}(n))_{n\geq 1}$ is $k$-regular.

The conjecture proposes that additive complexity preserves the regularity structure associated with automatic sequences. The paper establishes this property for the specific Thue–Morse-like sequence generated by $0\mapsto01$, $1\mapsto12$, and $2\mapsto20$, but no resolution of the general assertion is provided in the source.
R023.source_name: Jin Chen, Zhixiong Wen and Wen Wu, “On the additive complexity of a Thue-Morse like sequence”, arXiv:1802.03610 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for minimizers of the electrostatic Born–Infeld energy
R023.statement: Let $N$ be the ambient dimension, let $q>N$, let $\rho\in L^q_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^N)\cap\mathcal{X}^*$, and let $u_\rho$ be the minimizer associated with $\rho$. **Regularity conjecture.** The minimizer $u_\rho$ is $C^{1,\alpha}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$. This conjecture is motivated by the analogous regularity for the Poisson equation and the $p$-Laplacian, as well as by the radial example discussed in the paper; its general validity is not established in the supplied context.
R023.source_name: Denis Bonheure and Alessandro Iacopetti, “On the regularity of the minimizer of the electrostatic Born-Infeld energy”, arXiv:1804.02355 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02355

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

R023.title: Optimal regularity conjecture for two-dimensional KPZ scaling limits
R023.statement:
For any $\delta>0$, let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak{s};\mathrm{loc}}^{-\delta}(\mathbf{R}_{>0}\times\mathbf{T}^{2})$ and $\mathcal{C}^{-\delta}(\mathbf{T}^{2})$ denote the corresponding local parabolic and spatial negative Hölder spaces. **Optimal regularity conjecture.** The tightness statements in the paper's quantitative theorem hold in the spaces

$$
\mathcal{C}_{\mathfrak{s};\mathrm{loc}}^{-\delta}(\mathbf{R}_{>0}\times\mathbf{T}^{2})
$$

and

$$
\mathcal{C}^{-\delta}(\mathbf{T}^{2}),
$$

respectively, for every $\delta>0$. The theorem currently proves tightness only in the weaker spaces with regularities $-2-\delta$ and $-1-\delta$; improving these bounds to arbitrarily small negative regularity remains open.
R023.source_name: Sourav Chatterjee and Alexander Dunlap, “Constructing a solution of the (2+1)-dimensional KPZ equation”, arXiv:1809.00803 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.00803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

R023.title: Total regularity conjecture for mixed graphs with defect or excess one
R023.statement:
Let an $(r,z,k;-1)$-graph be a mixed graph with directed degree $r$, undirected degree $z$, diameter $k$, and defect one; let an $(r,z,k;+1)$-graph be a mixed graph with the same degree and diameter parameters and excess one. A mixed graph is **totally regular** when every vertex has the same indegree and outdegree, and every vertex has the same number of undirected neighbours.

**Total regularity conjecture.** All $(r,z,k;-1)$- and $(r,z,k;+1)$-graphs are totally regular.

The paper establishes total regularity for diameter two and defect one, and for $2$-geodetic mixed graphs with excess one. The analogous question for larger values of $k$ remains largely open.
R023.source_name: James Tuite and Grahame Erskine, “On total regularity of mixed graphs with order close to the Moore bound”, arXiv:1811.00650 (2018).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.00650

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

R023.title: Caffarelli Perron-solution regularity conjecture in dimension two
R023.statement:
Let a **strict supersolution** be understood in the sense of the Perron process for the one-phase free-boundary problem, and consider solutions obtained as infima of such strict supersolutions. **Caffarelli's conjecture.** Every solution obtained as the infimum of strict supersolutions is a classical solution in dimension two.

The source explains that Caffarelli proved partial regularity for these Perron solutions, with smooth free boundary outside a set of zero $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The conjecture proposes full classical regularity in dimension two, motivated by the known entire examples and their behavior at large scale.
R023.source_name: David S. Jerison and Nikola Kamburov, “Free boundaries subject to topological constraints”, arXiv:1902.00158 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.00158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).
