R023.title: Global bi-Lipschitz regularity conjecture for minimisers between doubly connected domains
R023.statement:
Let $D$ and $\Omega$ be doubly connected domains with smooth boundaries, and let $\rho$ be a smooth non-vanishing metric defined on the closure of $\Omega$. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(D)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(\Omega)$ for their moduli. **Global bi-Lipschitz regularity conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Mod}(D)\leq \operatorname{Mod}(\Omega),
$$

then the minimiser of the $\rho$-energy is globally bi-Lipschitz continuous and has a smooth extension up to the boundary. The conjecture is motivated by the critical J. C. C. Nitsche configuration, where the minimiser need not be bi-Lipschitz when the modulus inequality fails; the cited context notes that the corresponding Nitsche conjecture for annuli was solved, while this general metric-valued boundary regularity statement remains unresolved.
R023.source_name: David Kalaj, “Lipschitz property of minimisers between double connected surfaces”, arXiv:1902.04167 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

R023.title: Bourgain–Spencer regularity conjecture for homogenized coefficients
R023.statement:
Let $d$ denote the spatial dimension, let $\boldsymbol a$ be a random coefficient field satisfying suitable mixing conditions, and let $B$ be the convolution operator associated with the averaged solution in Lemma~. A convolution operator $B_0$ on $\operatorname{L}^2(\mathbb R^d)^d$ is required to satisfy

$$
B=-\nabla\cdot B_0\nabla.
$$

**Bourgain–Spencer conjecture.** Under suitable mixing conditions on the random coefficient field $\boldsymbol a$, such an operator $B_0$ exists and its Fourier symbol $\hat B_0$ is of Hölder class $C^{2d-\eta}$ at the origin for all $\eta>0$.

This conjecture extends the small-ellipticity-ratio iid result of Bourgain, in its nearly optimal form due to Kim and the third author, to general mixing conditions and beyond the perturbative regime. The statement concerns the regularity needed to define higher-order homogenized coefficients.
R023.source_name: Mitia Duerinckx, Antoine Gloria and Marius Lemm, “A remark on a surprising result by Bourgain in homogenization”, arXiv:1903.05247 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05247

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for zero-dimensional subschemes in toric varieties
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be the projective variety with Cox ring $S$, let $U\subset X$ be the open set used to define the Cox-ring setup, and let $I=\left\langle f_1,\ldots,f_n\right\rangle\subset S$ be a homogeneous ideal such that $V_X(I)$ is a zero-dimensional subscheme of $U$. Write $\alpha_i=\deg(f_i)\in\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ for the basepoint-free degrees of the generators, and let $\operatorname{Cl}(X)_+$ denote the positive degree semigroup. For a degree $\alpha$, let $\operatorname{Reg}(I)$ be the set of degrees for which the equivalent interpolation and Hilbert-function conditions in the definition of regularity hold. Let $\zeta_j$ be the points associated with the setup, and say that a point is a basepoint of $S_{\alpha_0}$ when every section of degree $\alpha_0$ vanishes there.

**Regularity conjecture.** Then

$$
\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_n\in\operatorname{Reg}(I)
$$

for every $\alpha_0\in\operatorname{Cl}(X)_+$ such that no $\zeta_j$ is a basepoint of $S_{\alpha_0}$.

This conjecture predicts a uniform degree in which the Cox-ring interpolation conditions become regular for zero-dimensional schemes, extending the familiar principle that sufficiently large basepoint-free degrees should recover the ideal component and the expected Hilbert function. The paper presents it as motivated by experimental evidence; no resolution is supplied in the given source.
R023.source_name: Simon Telen, “Numerical Root Finding via Cox Rings”, arXiv:1903.12002 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.12002

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

R023.title: Linear decay conjecture for the transformed gradient of p-harmonic maps
R023.statement:
Let $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $1<p<\infty$. Let $h\colon\Omega	o\mathbb{R}^n$ be $p$-harmonic on an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $V$ denote the standard nonlinear transformation associated with the $p$-Laplace equation. For a ball $B\subset\Omega$, write $\dashint_B$ for the average over $B$ and $\mean{V(
abla h)}_B$ for the average of $V(
abla h)$ over $B$. **Linear decay conjecture.** One has $V(
abla h)\in C^1(\Omega)$ and there exists $c>0$ such that

$$
\left(\dashint_{	heta B}\left|V(
abla h)-\mean{V(
abla h)}_{	heta B}ight|^2\,dxight)^{ rac12}\leq c\,	heta\left(\dashint_B\left|V(
abla h)-\mean{V(
abla h)}_Bight|^2\,dxight)^{ rac12}
$$

for every ball $B\subset\Omega$ and every $	heta\in(0,1]$. The conjecture proposes the natural $C^1$ regularity and linear oscillation decay for $V(
abla h)$ in arbitrary dimensions and for vectorial solutions; the preceding discussion notes that the corresponding linear behavior is not obtained from the available estimates, while planar regularity results motivate it. Its general validity remains open.
R023.source_name: Anna Kh. Balci, Lars Diening and Markus Weimar, “Higher Order Calderon-Zygmund Estimates for the p-Laplace Equation”, arXiv:1904.03388 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

R023.title: F. H. Lin's Lipschitz regularity conjecture for energy-minimizing maps on Alexandrov spaces
R023.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded open domain in an $n$-dimensional Alexandrov space with curvature bounded from below by $k$, and let $N$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold. Suppose $u$ is an energy-minimizing map, so that Theorem 1.1 gives local Hölder continuity in $\Omega$ away from a relatively closed subset of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-3$. **F. H. Lin's conjecture.** The Hölder continuity can be improved to Lipschitz continuity in Theorem 1.1. This conjecture asks whether the partial Hölder regularity of energy-minimizing maps from Alexandrov spaces can be strengthened to partial Lipschitz regularity; the supplied source does not indicate that it has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Huabin Ge, Wenshuai Jiang and Hui-Chun Zhang, “Partial regularity of harmonic maps from Alexandrov spaces”, arXiv:1907.09646 (2019).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1311.1331](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1331).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09646

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal, and let $G^c$ denote its complement. **Regularity conjecture for graphs with bounded edge-ideal regularity.** If

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G))\leq 3
$$

and $G^c$ has no induced $4$-cycle, then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G)^s)=2s
$$

for all $s\geq 2$. The source presents this as a related conjecture and records that analogous stabilization results are known for several graph classes; the stated general case remains open.
R023.source_name: Arindam Banerjee and Eran Nevo, “Regularity of Edge Ideals Via Suspension”, arXiv:1908.03115 (2019).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03115

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

R023.title: Isett–Oh optimal energy regularity conjecture for Hölder Euler solutions
R023.statement:
Let $v$ be a weak solution of the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^n$ with spatial-temporal Hölder regularity $v
\in C^\theta(\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^n)$, where $\theta<\frac{1}{3}$. Write $e_v(t)$ for its kinetic energy profile. The known estimate for $v\in L^\infty((0,T);C^\theta(\mathbb T^3))$ is

$$
|e_v(t)-e_v(s)|\leq C|t-s|^{\frac{2\theta}{1-\theta}}.
$$

**Isett–Oh conjecture.** For every $\theta<\frac{1}{3}$, there exists a weak Euler solution $v\in C^\theta(\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^n)$ such that

$$
e_v\notin W^{\frac{2\theta}{1-\theta}+\varepsilon,p}(I)
$$

for every $\varepsilon>0$, $p\geq1$, and every open interval $I\subset\mathbb R$. Moreover, the set of all such solutions is residual in the space of all $C^\theta(\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^n)$ weak solutions, equipped with the topology induced by the $C^\theta$ norm.

This conjecture asserts optimality of the Hölder exponent $\frac{2\theta}{1-\theta}$ for the energy profile below Onsager's threshold. The corresponding upper regularity estimate is known, as is energy conservation for $\theta>\frac13$; the sharp typicality and failure of every higher fractional Sobolev regularity remain the conjectural content.
R023.source_name: Luigi De Rosa and Riccardo Tione, “Sharp energy regularity and typicality results for Hölder solutions of incompressible Euler equations”, arXiv:1908.03529 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03529

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

R023.title: Alilooee–Banerjee–Beyarslan–Hà regularity conjecture for powers of edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal, and let ${\rm reg}(I(G))$ denote its Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity. For each integer $s\geq 1$, **Alilooee–Banerjee–Beyarslan–Hà's conjecture.**

$$
{\rm reg}(I(G)^s)\leq 2s+{\rm reg}(I(G))-2.
$$

This is a stronger form of the conjecture that the constant term in the eventual linear function ${\rm reg}(I(G)^s)$ is at most ${\rm reg}(I(G))-2$. It is known for several classes of graphs, including graphs with chordal complement, but remains open for arbitrary graphs.
R023.source_name: S. A. Seyed Fakhari, “On the regularity of small symbolic powers of edge ideals of graphs”, arXiv:1908.10845 (2019).
R023.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1805.01412](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01412), [arXiv:1801.06731](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06731), [arXiv:1702.00916](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00916).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10845

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

R023.title: Minh's symbolic-power regularity conjecture for edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal, and let $I(G)^{(s)}$ denote its $s$-th symbolic power. The invariant ${\rm reg}(-)$ denotes Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity. For every integer $s\geq 1$, **Minh's conjecture.**

$$
{\rm reg}(I(G)^s)={\rm reg}(I(G)^{(s)}).
$$

The conjecture asks whether ordinary and symbolic powers of every graph edge ideal have the same regularity. It is presented as a conjecture posed by Minh and is related to the study of regularity of symbolic powers; no general resolution is given in the source.
R023.source_name: S. A. Seyed Fakhari, “On the regularity of small symbolic powers of edge ideals of graphs”, arXiv:1908.10845 (2019).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1904.11480](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.11480).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10845

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

R023.title: The even-modulus regularity conjecture for area-minimizing currents
R023.statement:
Let $T$ be as in Theorem. For odd $p$, Theorem states that $\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ is $(m-1)$-rectifiable and has locally finite $(m-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure away from $\operatorname{spt}^{p}(\partial T)$.

**Even-modulus regularity conjecture.** The conclusions of Theorem hold for $p$ even as well; that is, when $p$ is even, $\operatorname{Sing}(T)$ is $(m-1)$-rectifiable and, for every compact $K$ with $K\cap\operatorname{spt}^{p}(\partial T)=\varnothing$,

$$
\mathcal{H}^{m-1}(\operatorname{Sing}(T)\cap K)<\infty.
$$

For odd $p$ these conclusions are proved in the paper, whereas the even-$p$ case is presented as an open extension and would give a uniform rectifiability and measure theory for singular sets of area-minimizing currents modulo every $p$.
R023.source_name: Camillo De Lellis, Jonas Hirsch, Andrea Marchese and Salvatore Stuvard, “Regularity of area minimizing currents mod p”, arXiv:1909.05172 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05172

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

R023.title: Continuity and monotonicity conjecture for local dimensions of CIFS spectra
R023.statement:
Let $F\subset[0,\infty)$ be the dimension spectrum of a CIFS. For $x\in F$, define the local Hausdorff dimension of $F$ at $x$ by

$$
\dim_x(F)=\inf\{\operatorname{HD}(F\cap B(x,\epsilon)): \epsilon>0\}.
$$

**Local-dimension regularity conjecture.** The map

$$
x\mapsto\dim_x(F)
$$

restricted to $x\in F$ is continuous and weakly decreasing, meaning nonincreasing. This conjecture predicts strong regularity for the local geometry of every CIFS dimension spectrum; the source provides no resolution.
R023.source_name: Tushar Das and David Simmons, “On the dimension spectra of infinite iterated function systems”, arXiv:1910.10259 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

R023.title: Kummini–Lakshmibai–Sastry–Seshadri regularity conjecture for Grassmannian Schubert patches
R023.statement:
Let $B\subseteq GL_n(\mathbb{C})$ be the Borel subgroup of upper triangular matrices, and let $w\in S_n$ be a Grassmannian permutation with descent at position $k$. Let $Y$ be the standard open patch associated with $w$, let $J_w$ be the prime ideal generated by the essential minors defining the corresponding patch $Y_w$, and suppose that for some $r\in[k-1]$ one has

$$
w_{k-r+i}=n-k+i\quad\text{for all }i\in[r]
$$

and $w_1=1$. Define $\widetilde w$ by $(\widetilde w_1,\ldots,\widetilde w_k)=(n-w_k+1,\ldots,n-w_1+1)$, write

$$
(\widetilde w_1,\ldots,\widetilde w_k)=(k-r+1,k-r+2,\ldots,k,a_{r+1},\ldots,a_{n-1},n),
$$

set $a_r=k$ and $a_k=n$, and, for $r\leq i\leq k-1$, define $m_i=a_{i+1}-a_i$. **Kummini–Lakshmibai–Sastry–Seshadri conjecture.** The regularity should satisfy

$$
\operatorname{reg}(\mathbb{C}[Y]/J_w)=\sum_{i=r}^{k-1}(m_i-1)i.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is false and provides a counterexample, replacing it with an alternate explicit combinatorial formula for the regularity.
R023.source_name: Jenna Rajchgot, Yi Ren, Colleen Robichaux, Avery St. Dizier and Anna Weigandt, “Degrees of symmetric Grothendieck polynomials and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity”, arXiv:1912.04477 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04477

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for generators of T-continuous semigroups
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be a Banach space, let $d4a5=\left\{F_t\right\}_{t\ge0}\subset C^k(\mathcal{D})$ be a semigroup on a domain $\mathcal{D}\subset X$, and let $T$-continuity mean continuity in the topology specified by the paper. Assume that for each $j=1,\ldots,k$, the family $\left\{{F_t}^{(j)}\right\}_{t\ge0}$ is $T$-continuous. **The generator regularity conjecture.** The strong limit

$$
f(x)=\lim_{t\to0^+} \frac1t\left(F_t(x)-x\right)
$$

exists uniformly on subsets strictly inside $\mathcal{D}$. Moreover, $f$ is bounded on every set that lies strictly inside $\mathcal{D}$ and belongs to $C^{k-1}(\mathcal{D},X)$. This conjecture extends the preceding differentiability result from $C^1$ semigroups to higher regularity: simultaneous $T$-continuity of the derivatives is expected to ensure existence and $C^{k-1}$ regularity of the infinitesimal generator. The supplied context gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
R023.source_name: Mark Elin, “Differentiability of semigroups of Lipschitz or smooth mappings”, arXiv:2001.09516 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

R023.title: The regularity formula for neighborhood ideals of forests
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a forest, let $R$ be the polynomial ring associated to its vertices, let $NI(G)$ denote its neighborhood ideal, and let $a_G$ be the invariant defined in the paper.

**Regularity conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{reg}(R/NI(G))=a_G.
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact combinatorial formula for the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of the quotient by the neighborhood ideal of a forest. The source gives no resolution status beyond stating it as the paper's concluding conjecture.
R023.source_name: Leila Sharifan and Somayeh Moradi, “Closed neighborhood ideal of a graph”, arXiv:2003.04841 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04841

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

R023.title: Partition regularity of the exceptional linear–quadratic equation
R023.statement:
Let $a,b,c$ be non-zero integers, and consider the Diophantine equation

$$
a(x_1^2-x_2^2)=by^2+cz.
$$

**Partition-regularity conjecture.** For every choice of non-zero integers $a,b,c$, this equation is partition regular.

This is the sole exceptional case not covered by the paper's linear–quadratic partition-regularity theorem. The authors state that their lack of knowledge of this case is an artefact of their methods and believe that the cited criterion gives the correct characterisation.
R023.source_name: Sean Prendiville, “Counting monochromatic solutions to diagonal Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2003.10161 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10161

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for sign uncertainty principles
R023.statement:
Let $s\in\{+,-\}$ and let $d\geq 1$. Write $\mathbb{A}_s(d)$ for the sign uncertainty constant in dimension $d$, and let $\mathbb{A}_s^{\mathcal B}(d)$ and $\mathbb{A}_s^{\mathcal{S}}(d)$ denote its versions for the function classes specified in the paper. **Regularity conjecture.** For any $s\in\{+,-\}$ and $d\geq 1$, it holds that

$$
\mathbb{A}_s(d)=\mathbb{A}_s^{\mathcal B}(d)=\mathbb{A}_s^{\mathcal{S}}(d).
$$

The theorem in the paper proves this equality for $(s,d)=(+,1)$, while several further cases are known from explicitly constructed minimizers; the conjecture remains open in full generality.
R023.source_name: Felipe Gonçalves, Diogo Oliveira e Silva and João P. G. Ramos, “On regularity and mass concentration phenomena for the sign uncertainty principle”, arXiv:2003.10765 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10765

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2020).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for quasiconformal homeomorphisms of rigid Carnot groups
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a Carnot group. A group is **rigid** if the space of smooth contact embeddings $G\supset U\to G$ is finite-dimensional for every connected open subset $U\subset G$. **Regularity conjecture.** If $G$ is a rigid Carnot group, then every quasiconformal homeomorphism

$$
G\supset U\to U'\subset G
$$

is $C^\infty$. This conjecture proposes that quasiconformal self-maps of rigid Carnot groups have the same smooth regularity as contact diffeomorphisms; whether it holds in full generality is not established in the supplied source.
R023.source_name: Bruce Kleiner, Stefan Muller and Xiangdong Xie, “Pansu pullback and rigidity of mappings between Carnot groups”, arXiv:2004.09271 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.09271

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

R023.title: Biregularity conjecture for non-natural involutions on Hilbert schemes of points on K3 surfaces
R023.statement:
Let $n \geq 2$ and $t=(n-1)k^2+1$ for $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $S$ be an algebraic K3 surface with $\operatorname{Pic}(S)=\mathbb{Z}H$ and $H^2=2t$. The non-natural non-symplectic involution generating $\operatorname{Bir}(S^{[n]})$ is biregular whenever $k\geq 3$.

**Biregularity conjecture.** If $k\geq 3$, then the non-natural non-symplectic involution which generates $\operatorname{Bir}(S^{[n]})$ is biregular.

This would improve the previously known sufficient bound $k\geq (n+3)/2$ for biregularity. The cases $k=1,2$ are known to yield non-biregular involutions, while the assertion for all $k\geq 3$ is presented as an expected strengthening and remains open in the supplied source.
R023.source_name: Pietro Beri and Alberto Cattaneo, “On birational transformations of Hilbert schemes of points on K3 surfaces”, arXiv:2005.05187 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.05187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

R023.title: F-regularity conjecture for the commutator ideals
R023.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of positive prime characteristic, and let $R$, $\mathcal{I}$, and $J$ be the ring and ideals defined from the commutator matrix in the paper. **F-regularity conjecture.** The quotient rings

$$
R/\mathcal{I}\quad\text{and}\quad R/J
$$

are $F$-regular. In particular, they are integral domains. This would strengthen the preceding results that $R/J$ is $F$-pure and reduced in positive characteristic, and would imply strong structural properties for the associated algebraic sets.
R023.source_name: Zhibek Kadyrsizova and Madi Yerlanov, “Algebraic sets defined by the commutator matrix”, arXiv:2006.13514 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13514

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

R023.title: Kloster–Král–Sullivan rational subgraph-regularity conjecture
R023.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph. It is walk-regular if $[A^r]_{ii}=[A^r]_{jj}$ for all vertices $i,j$ and every positive integer $r$, and it is $\beta$-subgraph regular if $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii}=[e^{\beta A}]_{jj}$ for all vertices $i,j$. **Kloster–Král–Sullivan conjecture.** The graph $\mathcal{G}$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists a rational number $\beta>0$ such that $\mathcal{G}$ is $\beta$-subgraph regular. The paper presents this as the rational-parameter refinement after the unrestricted single-parameter assertion was disproved.
R023.source_name: Francesco Ballini and Nikita Deniskin, “Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: a proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations”, arXiv:2007.08956 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.08956

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2020). “Some counterexamples for the closeness and betweenness centralities were found independently by Rombach and Porter and by Stevanovi\'c , but the conjecture remained open for degree and eigenvector centralities.”

R023.title: Regularity bound by the number of maximal cliques for binomial edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $S={\mathbb K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]$ be the polynomial ring over a field ${\mathbb K}$, and let $J_G\subseteq S$ be its binomial edge ideal. Let $c(G)$ denote the number of maximal cliques of $G$, and let

$$
\operatorname{reg} S/J_G=\max\{j-i:\beta_{i,j}(S/J_G)\neq 0\}.
$$

**The clique-count regularity conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{reg} S/J_G\leq c(G).
$$

The bound is known for closed, or proper interval, graphs. The source presents it as a conjecture posed in 2013, and the supplied material gives no resolution for arbitrary graphs.
R023.source_name: M. Rouzbahani Malayeri, S. Saeedi Madani and D. Kiani, “A proof for a conjecture on the regularity of binomial edge ideals”, arXiv:2007.09959 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.09959

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2020). “Later, in , this conjecture was proved by the second and the third authors of this paper.”

R023.title: The smooth regularity conjecture for \f-isoperimetric sets
R023.statement: Let $\phi$ be a norm of class $\mathrm{C}^\infty_+$, and let $\phi$-isoperimetric sets be isoperimetric sets for the norm $\phi$ in $\mathbb{H}^1$. **Smooth regularity conjecture.** Every $\phi$-isoperimetric set is of class $\mathrm{C}^2$. The conjecture concerns regularity at characteristic points, where the preceding results do not apply to general non-differentiable norms; it is presented as a condition needed for the subsequent result, and no resolution is given here.
R023.source_name: Valentina Franceschi, Roberto Monti, Alberto Righini and Mario Sigalotti, “The isoperimetric problem for regular and crystalline norms in H^1”, arXiv:2007.11384 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11384

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for even associated lattices
R023.statement: Let $a>2$ be even and let $b$ be sufficiently large. Consider an Ulam set with generators $v_1$ and $v_2$ whose associated lattice is generated by $(-a,b)$. **Regularity conjecture.** The Ulam set contains finitely many elements of the form $2xv_1+yv_2$ and is therefore regular. The claim is based on computations and is presented as unresolved in the source.
R023.source_name: Tej Bade, Kelly Cui, Antoine Labelle and Deyuan Li, “Ulam Sets in New Settings”, arXiv:2008.02762 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02762

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

R023.title: The non-virtual-regularity conjecture for scale group actions
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a compactly generated, topologically simple totally disconnected locally compact group, let $x\in G$ satisfy $s(x^{-1})>1$, and let $V_{--}\rtimes\langle x\rangle$ be the associated scale group acting on the boundary of the tree $T_{s(x^{-1})+1}$, with distinguished end $\omega$. **Non-virtual-regularity conjecture.** The action of $V_{--}\rtimes\langle x\rangle$ on

$$
\partial T_{s(x^{-1})+1}\setminus\{\omega\}
$$

is not virtually regular. This is presented as a companion to a criterion concerning two-transitive actions on tree boundaries. The paper states that the conjecture says nothing about compactly generated, topologically simple uniscalar groups, and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: George A. Willis, “Scale Groups”, arXiv:2008.05220 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05220

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

R023.title: Regularity up to the cohomological time for pluriclosed flow
R023.statement:
Let $(M^{2n},g_0,J)$ be a compact complex manifold with pluriclosed metric. Define

$$
\tau^*(g_0):=\sup\{t\geq 0\mid[\omega_0]-t c_1\in\mathcal P^{1,1}_{A}\}.
$$

Here $\omega_0$ is the fundamental form of $g_0$, $c_1$ is the first Chern class in Aeppli cohomology, and $\mathcal P^{1,1}_{A}$ is the positive Aeppli cone. **Pluriclosed-flow regularity conjecture.** The unique maximal smooth solution to pluriclosed flow exists on $[0,\tau^*(g_0))$. The preceding upper-bound lemma shows that the maximal smooth existence time cannot exceed $\tau^*(g_0)$; the conjecture asserts equality, but the supplied text gives no resolution status.
R023.source_name: Mario Garcia-Fernandez and Jeffrey Streets, “Generalized Ricci Flow”, arXiv:2008.07004 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.07004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

R023.title: Hildebrand's regularity conjecture for conformally invariant Lagrangians
R023.statement: In the setting of variational problems with a coercive conformally invariant Lagrangian of quadratic growth, consider its critical points. **Hildebrand's regularity conjecture.** Every such critical point is regular. This conjecture was fully settled by Rivière in 2007, establishing regularity in the stated conformally invariant setting.
R023.source_name: Chang-Yu Guo, Chang-Lin Xiang and Gao-Feng Zheng, “The Lamm-Riviere system I: L^p regularity theory”, arXiv:2008.07777 (2020).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.07777

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2020). “In 2007, this conjecture was fully settled down by Rivi\`ere in his remarkable work .”

R023.title: Lions' maximal regularity conjecture for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations
R023.statement:
Consider the viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation

$$
--\Delta u+|Du|^\gamma=f(x)\quad\text{in }\Omega,
$$

where $\Omega$ is a domain, $\gamma>1$, and $f\in L^q(\Omega)$ with $q>1$. Write $\gamma'=\frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}$ for the conjugate exponent. **Lions' conjecture.** If

$$
q>\frac{d}{\gamma'}=\frac{d(\gamma-1)}{\gamma},
$$

then every solution satisfies the a priori estimate

$$
\|D^2u\|_{L^q}+\||Du|^\gamma\|_{L^q}\leq C(\|f\|_{L^q},d,q,\gamma).
$$

Moreover, the estimate is false when $q\leq d/\gamma'$. This conjecture concerns maximal $L^q$-regularity for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with unbounded source terms; the source attributes it to P.-L. Lions. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Alessandro Goffi, “Transport equations with nonlocal diffusion and applications to Hamilton-Jacobi equations”, arXiv:2101.00615 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for shuffled projective modules in category O
R023.statement: Let $W$ be the Weyl group, let $\mathcal{O}_0$ be the principal block of category $\mathcal{O}$, and let $P$ be a projective generator of $\mathcal{O}_0$. For a parabolic subgroup of $W$, write $w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}$ for its longest element, and let $\mathrm{C}_{w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}}$ denote the corresponding shuffling functor. **Regularity conjecture.** If $w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}$ is the longest element in some parabolic subgroup of $W$, then $\mathcal{O}_0$ is $\mathrm{C}_{w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}}P$-regular. This extends the established case of simple reflections; the source also notes that $\mathcal{O}_0$ is not $\mathrm{C}_{st}P$-regular for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}_3$, so the general assertion is nontrivial.
R023.source_name: Hankyung Ko, Volodymyr Mazorchuk and Rafael Mrđen, “Some homological properties of category O, VI”, arXiv:2101.05550 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.05550

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for shuffled tilting modules in category O
R023.statement: Let $W$ be the Weyl group, let $\mathcal{O}_0$ be the principal block of category $\mathcal{O}$, and let $T$ be a characteristic tilting module for $\mathcal{O}_0$. For a parabolic subgroup of $W$, write $w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}$ for its longest element, and let $\mathrm{C}_{w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}}$ denote the corresponding shuffling functor. **Regularity conjecture.** If $w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}$ is the longest element in some parabolic subgroup of $W$, then $\mathcal{O}_0$ is $\mathrm{C}_{w_0^{\mathfrak{p}}}T$-regular. The simple-reflection case is proved in the source, while the general parabolic case is posed as a conjecture and is described as substantially harder because shuffling functors do not commute with projective functors.
R023.source_name: Hankyung Ko, Volodymyr Mazorchuk and Rafael Mrđen, “Some homological properties of category O, VI”, arXiv:2101.05550 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.05550

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the flip graph of generalized snake order polytopes
R023.statement: Let $\mathbf{w} in \mathcal{V}$, and consider the flip graph whose vertices are the regular triangulations of the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$. Let $k$ denote the dimension of its secondary polytope. **Regularity conjecture.** The flip graph of regular triangulations for $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$ is $k$-regular. The preceding ladder computations and computational evidence motivate this assertion; its general validity is left open.
R023.source_name: Matias von Bell, Benjamin Braun, Derek Hanely, Khrystyna Serhiyenko, Julianne Vega, Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez and Martha Yip, “Triangulations, order polytopes, and generalized snake posets”, arXiv:2102.11306 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for all triangulations of generalized snake order polytopes
R023.statement: Let $\mathbf{w} in \mathcal{V}$, and let $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$ be the associated order polytope. A triangulation is **regular** if it arises from a lifting function, equivalently is a regular subdivision triangulation. **All-triangulations regularity conjecture.** All triangulations of $\mathcal{O}(Q_{\mathbf{w}})$ are regular. The paper proves that all such triangulations are unimodular and reports computational support for regularity; the general statement remains open.
R023.source_name: Matias von Bell, Benjamin Braun, Derek Hanely, Khrystyna Serhiyenko, Julianne Vega, Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez and Martha Yip, “Triangulations, order polytopes, and generalized snake posets”, arXiv:2102.11306 (2021).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1512.08411](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.08411).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

R023.title: The asymptotic irregularity conjecture for orthomorphisms
R023.statement: Let $q$ range over prime powers, and let an **irregular orthomorphism** be an orthomorphism whose translate $T_g[\theta](x)=\theta(x+g)-\theta(g)$ is non-cyclotomic for every $g\in\mathbb{F}_q$. **Irregularity conjecture.** Asymptotically almost all orthomorphisms are irregular. The paper proves that almost all orthomorphisms of odd-order fields are irregular and conjectures that the same typical behaviour holds for fields of even order; the assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: Jack Allsop and Ian M. Wanless, “Degree of Orthomorphism Polynomials over Finite Fields”, arXiv:2103.02153 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02153

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021). “A related open question is to establish what is the largest field without irregular orthomorphisms.”

R023.title: Majda's global regularity conjecture for totally linearly degenerate systems
R023.statement: Let $d\geq 2$ and consider a $d$-dimensional nonlinear symmetric system that is totally linearly degenerate. Suppose the initial data belong to $H^s(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $s>\frac{d}{2}+1$. **Majda's global regularity conjecture.** Such a system typically has smooth global solutions unless the solution itself blows up in finite time; in particular, shock-wave formation never occurs for any smooth initial data. This conjecture concerns whether total linear degeneracy prevents shock formation in multidimensional nonlinear hyperbolic systems, extending the known global smooth small-data behavior for one-dimensional totally linearly degenerate systems. The qualifier “typically” leaves the precise scope of the assertion to be understood in the context of the conjecture.
R023.source_name: Fei Hou and Huicheng Yin, “Delayed singularity formation for the three dimensional compressible Euler equations with non-zero vorticity”, arXiv:2103.03474 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

R023.title: Interior regularity conjecture for non-degenerate nonlocal mean field games
R023.statement: Let $2\sigma\in(0,2)$ and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a non-degenerate nonlocal operator satisfying condition (LC), let $F$ satisfy the non-degeneracy and structural assumptions, and let $(f,g)\in\mathcal{R}_B(\alpha,M)$. Consider the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation associated with the mean field game system. **Interior regularity conjecture.** Assume (LC), the non-degeneracy condition on $F$, $(f,g)\in\mathcal{R}_B(\alpha,M)$, and assumptions (a:F1) and (a:F2). Then interior $(\alpha/2\sigma,\alpha)$-regularity estimates hold for the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation. The conjecture concerns interior regularity for a broad class of nonlocal operators, including fractional Laplacians and nonsymmetric operators, in the fully nonlinear setting. The source notes that no results beyond the affine case are available.
R023.source_name: Indranil Chowdhury, Espen R. Jakobsen and Miłosz Krupski, “On fully nonlinear parabolic mean field games with nonlocal and local diffusions”, arXiv:2104.06985 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06985

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

R023.title: The regularity formula for squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a forest. For a positive integer $k$, let $I(G)^{[k]}$ denote the $k$th squarefree power of the edge ideal of $G$, let $\operatorname{reg}$ denote Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity, let $\operatorname{aim}(G,k)$ denote the maximum cardinality of an induced $k$-matching of $G$, and let $\operatorname{mat}(G)$ denote the matching number of $G$.

**Forest regularity conjecture.** For every $1\leq k\leq \operatorname{mat}(G)$,

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G)^{[k]})= \operatorname{aim}(G,k)+k.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the upper bound established for squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests is always sharp. It is motivated by the preceding results and Macaulay2 computations, but the source provides no resolution.
R023.source_name: Nursel Erey and Takayuki Hibi, “Squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests”, arXiv:2105.09744 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09744

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

R023.title: Partial regularity conjecture for mean curvature flow
R023.statement: Let the initial surface be closed and embedded, and let the singular set be considered with its parabolic metric. **The partial regularity conjecture.** The parabolic Hausdorff dimension of the singular set is at most $1$. The source says standard dimension reduction would derive this from the multiplicity-one conjecture, while a direct approach is also possible.
R023.source_name: Robert Haslhofer, “Lectures on mean curvature flow of surfaces”, arXiv:2105.10485 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10485

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2021). “This is presumably the biggest open problem, ever since Brakke's pioneering work.”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for strongly elliptic operators
R023.statement:
Let $\mathcal L\in\operatorname{\mathcal S\mathcal E}$, and let $G\subset\mathbb C$ be a bounded simply connected domain. The domain $G$ is **$\mathcal L$-regular** when the associated $\mathcal L$-Dirichlet problem has the regularity property required in the source. **Regularity conjecture for strongly elliptic operators.** Every bounded simply connected domain $G\subset\mathbb C$ is $\mathcal L$-regular.

This conjecture is presented as a plausible result whose proof would clarify the general case of the inverse approximation statement. The source notes that the corresponding regularity assertion is known for operators with complex-conjugate characteristic roots, but leaves the general strongly elliptic case open.
R023.source_name: Astamur Bagapsh, Konstantin Fedorovskiy and Maksim Mazalov, “On Dirichlet problem for second-order elliptic equations in the plane and uniform approximation problems for solutions of such equations”, arXiv:2106.00773 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00773

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2021). “The inverse statement in Conjecture is very interesting open question.”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for Jordan-Lie inner ideals of simple locally finite associative algebras
R023.statement: Let $A$ be a simple locally finite associative algebra over $\mathbb{F}$, let $L=[A,A]$, and let $B$ be a Jordan-Lie inner ideal of $L$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every Jordan-Lie inner ideal $B$ of $L$ is regular. The conjecture proposes that the regularity results established for finite-dimensional associative algebras extend to simple locally finite associative algebras; its general validity remains open.
R023.source_name: Hasan Mohammed Ali Shlaka, “Generalization of Jordan-Lie of Finite Dimensional Associative Algebras”, arXiv:2107.00775 (2022).
R023.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1603.00045](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00045), [arXiv:1312.7778](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7778), [arXiv:1208.1972](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.1972).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00775

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

R023.title: The quasi-freeness conjecture for graded symmetric-group harmonics
R023.statement:
Let $cmathcal{R}_{k,n}$ and $p_{calpha}$ be as in Section 2, with $d(calpha)$ denoting the degree of $p_{calpha}$. Let $cmathcal{H}_{k,n}$ be the graded space of $S_n$-harmonics that is an orthogonal complement to the ideal $cmathcal{I}_{k,n}$ generated by the $p_{calpha}$ with $d(calpha)>0$. **Quasi-freeness conjecture.** If $m\leq n$ and, for each $calpha$ with $d(calpha)\leq m$, there is a homogeneous $h_{calpha}\incmathcal{H}_{k,n}$ such that $d(calpha)+\deg(h_{calpha})=m$, and if

$$
\sum_{d(\alpha)\leq m}h_{\alpha}p_{\alpha}=0,
$$

then $h_{calpha}=0$ for all $calpha$ with $d(calpha)\leq m$. This conjecture would give the stated stability formulas for the graded multiplicities and Hilbert series; it is proved in low degrees and has been checked in several small cases, but is not established in general.
R023.source_name: Marino Romero and Nolan Wallach, “Stability theorems for multiplicities in graded S_n-modules”, arXiv:2108.00036 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

R023.title: Bloch's semi-regularity conjecture for embedded deformations
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $Y\subset X$ be a closed locally complete intersection subvariety of codimension $p$. Let $N_{Y/X}$ be the normal bundle, and consider the semi-regularity map

$$
H^{1}(N_{Y/X})\to H^{p+1}(\Omega_{X/k}^{p-1}).
$$

**Bloch's semi-regularity conjecture.** The semi-regularity map annihilates every obstruction to embedded deformations of $Y$ in $X$. The conjecture concerns the obstruction theory of embedded deformations; the paper gives a different proof of Bloch's theorem establishing this annihilation result.
R023.source_name: Sen Yang, “Chern character, semi-regularity map and obstructions”, arXiv:2109.10626 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10626

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

R023.title: Semi-regularity conjecture via the universal obstruction space
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $Y\subset X$ be a closed locally complete intersection subvariety of codimension $p$. Let $\mathrm{\mathbb{H}ilb}$ be the local Hilbert functor, let $O_{\mathrm{\mathbb{H}ilb}}$ be its universal obstruction space, and let

$$
[v_e]:O_{\mathrm{\mathbb{H}ilb}}\to H^{1}(N_{Y/X})
$$

be the natural linear monomorphism. Let $H^{1}(N_{Y/X})\to H^{p+1}(\Omega_{X/k}^{p-1})$ be the semi-regularity map. **Bloch's semi-regularity conjecture.** The composition of morphisms of $k$-vector spaces

$$
O_{\mathrm{\mathbb{H}ilb}}\xrightarrow{[v_e]}H^{1}(N_{Y/X})\to H^{p+1}(\Omega_{X/k}^{p-1})
$$

is trivial. This is an equivalent formulation of the assertion that the semi-regularity map annihilates all obstructions to embedded deformations of $Y$ in $X$.
R023.source_name: Sen Yang, “Chern character, semi-regularity map and obstructions”, arXiv:2109.10626 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10626

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

R023.title: Sharp Sobolev regularity conjecture for restricted X-ray transforms
R023.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ and $1< p < 2$. Suppose $\gamma$ is a smooth nondegenerate curve, and let $\mathfrak R$ denote the associated restricted X-ray transform. With

$$
\alpha(p)=
\begin{cases}
1-\frac 1p, & 1\le p<\frac{2d}{2d-1},\\
\frac 1{2d}, & \frac{2d}{2d-1} \le p\le 2,
\end{cases}
$$

**Sharp Sobolev regularity conjecture.** The operator $\mathfrak R$ boundedly maps $L^p$ to $L_\alpha^p$ for $\alpha \le \alpha(p)$. The sharp $L^p$ regularity estimate is open in higher dimensions for $1<p<2$; in dimension $d=2$, the endpoint remains open for $\frac43\le p<2$.
R023.source_name: Hyerim Ko, Sanghyuk Lee and Sewook Oh, “Sharp Sobolev regularity of restricted X-ray transforms”, arXiv:2111.04339 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.04339

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

R023.title: Local Irregularity Conjecture for the locally irregular chromatic index
R023.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$ be the family consisting of all odd-length paths, all odd-length cycles, and the graphs obtained from the triangle by the recursive construction described in the source: identify a degree-$2$ vertex belonging to a triangle with an end-vertex of a path, whose other end is identified with a vertex of a triangle. For a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)$ be the smallest number of colors in a locally irregular edge-coloring of $G$. **Local Irregularity Conjecture.** For every connected graph $G\notin\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$, one has

$$
\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This conjecture concerns the three-color bound for connected graphs outside the known family of non-colorable graphs. The paper exhibits a bow-tie cactus with locally irregular chromatic index $4$, showing that the broader formulation is false; the stated conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Remarks on the Local Irregularity Conjecture”, arXiv:2111.08111 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08111

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021). “The best upper bound is that every graph without isolated edges admits a neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring with five colors , but the 1-2-3 Conjecture remains open.”

R023.title: Four-color local irregularity conjecture for connected graphs
R023.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$ be the family of odd-length paths, odd-length cycles, and the recursively constructed cactus graphs described above. For a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)$ denote its locally irregular chromatic index. **Four-color local irregularity conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ which does not belong to $\mathfrak{T}^{\prime}$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)\leq 4.
$$

This is presented as a weaker form of the three-color Local Irregularity Conjecture, prompted by the bow-tie graph, which has locally irregular chromatic index $4$. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Remarks on the Local Irregularity Conjecture”, arXiv:2111.08111 (2021).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08111

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2021). “The best upper bound is that every graph without isolated edges admits a neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring with five colors , but the 1-2-3 Conjecture remains open.”

R023.title: Ottazzi–Warhurst regularity conjecture for rigid Carnot groups
R023.statement:
Let $G$supset U$ and $U'

A quasiconformal homeomorphism is a homeomorphism $f:U\to U'$ that is quasiconformal. **Ottazzi–Warhurst regularity conjecture.** Every quasiconformal homeomorphism $f:U\to U'$ is $C^\infty$. This conjecture is motivated by regularity results for quasiconformal mappings between smooth rigid Carnot groups; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
R023.source_name: Bruce Kleiner, Stefan Muller and Xiangdong Xie, “Sobolev mappings between nonrigid Carnot groups”, arXiv:2112.01866 (2021).
R023.references:

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for big quantum cohomology of homogeneous spaces
R023.statement: Let $\mathrm{G}$ be a semisimple algebraic group and let $\mathrm{P}\subset \mathrm{G}$ be a parabolic subgroup. The ring $\operatorname{BQH}(\mathrm{G}/\mathrm{P})$ is the big quantum cohomology ring of the rational homogeneous space $\mathrm{G}/\mathrm{P}$. **Regularity conjecture.** The ring $\operatorname{BQH}(\mathrm{G}/\mathrm{P})$ is regular. Regularity implies generic semisimplicity in the setting considered here. The source proves the corresponding statement for coadjoint varieties, while the formulation is made for arbitrary semisimple groups and parabolic subgroups.
R023.source_name: Nicolas Perrin and Maxim Smirnov, “On the big quantum cohomology of coadjoint varieties”, arXiv:2112.12436 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12436

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2021). “Guided by the structure of $\QH(X)$ this conjecture has been proved in all cases except for types $\rE_6$, $\rE_7$ and $\rE_8$.”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for complex Monge–Ampère equations with bounded or Hölder right-hand side
R023.statement: Let $\varphi$ solve the complex Monge–Ampère equation considered in the paper, with right-hand side $F$. The question concerns estimates for the regularity of $\varphi$ under assumptions on $F$. **Regularity conjecture.** Does $\varphi$ satisfy a $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate when $F$ is only bounded, and a $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate when $F\in C^{\alpha}$? The $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate is known under additional regularity assumptions on the solution, but obtaining it without any extra regularity assumption remains open; the corresponding $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate is presented as a natural expectation motivated by the real Monge–Ampère theory.
R023.source_name: Xiuxiong Chen and Jingrui Cheng, “Gradient estimate for complex Monge-Ampere equation with continuous right hand side”, arXiv:2201.13330 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13330

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

R023.title: Regularity equals the degree of the Hilbert numerator for Schubert varieties
R023.statement:
Let $GL_n/B$ be the complete flag variety, with Schubert varieties $X_w$ indexed by permutations $w\in\mathfrak S_n$. For $v\leq w$ in Bruhat order, let $e_v=vB/B$ be the corresponding torus-fixed point, let $R_{v,w}$ be the associated graded ring of the local ring of $X_w$ at $e_v$, and write its Poincaré series as

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\dim(\mathfrak m_{e_v}^i/\mathfrak m_{e_v}^{i+1})q^i=\frac{H_{v,w}(q)}{(1-q)^{\ell(w)}}.
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** The Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity satisfies

$$
\operatorname{Reg}(R_{v,w})=\deg H_{v,w}(q).
$$

This predicts that the regularity of the tangent-cone ring at a torus-fixed point is determined by the degree of its Hilbert numerator. The source provides no resolution status or supporting evidence beyond stating the conjecture.
R023.source_name: Alexander Yong, “Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and Schubert geometry”, arXiv:2202.06362 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06362

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

R023.title: Quadratic growth of maximal Schubert regularity
R023.statement:
For each $n$, define

$$
\operatorname{maxReg}(n)=\max_{v\leq w\in\mathfrak S_n}\operatorname{Reg}(R_{v,w}),
$$

where $R_{v,w}$ is the associated graded ring of the local ring of the Schubert variety $X_w$ at the torus-fixed point $e_v$. **Maximal-regularity conjecture.** The maximal regularity has quadratic order of growth:

$$
\operatorname{maxReg}(n)=\Theta(n^2).
$$

This predicts quadratic asymptotic growth for the largest regularity among Schubert tangent cones in type $A$. The source gives no resolution status or supporting evidence beyond the conjectural assertion.
R023.source_name: Alexander Yong, “Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and Schubert geometry”, arXiv:2202.06362 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.06362

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for solutions of a singular fractional differential equation
R023.statement:
Consider the boundary-value problem

$$
\begin{cases}
D^{\alpha}_{0+}u(t)+h(t)=0,\quad t\in(0,1),\\
u(0)=0=u(1),
\end{cases}
$$

where $D^{\alpha}_{0+}$ is the Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative of order $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $C^1_{2-\alpha}[0,1]$ denote the weighted differentiability space used in the paper, and let

$$
E_\alpha=\{u\in C[0,1]:t^{\alpha-1}D^{\alpha-1}_{0+}u(t)\in C[0,1]\}.
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** If $h\in C[0,1]$ or $h\in L^1(0,1)$, then the solution $u$ belongs to $C^1_{2-\alpha}[0,1]$. Moreover, if $h\in C(0,1]$ satisfies $(H)$, then the solution $u$ belongs to $E_\alpha[0,1]$.
The claim concerns regularity of solutions when the forcing term is either regular or singular at the endpoint. The surrounding discussion states that the first assertion is known for continuous $h$ and that examples demonstrate the relevance of $E_\alpha$ for singular data; the status of the full proposition, including the $L^1$ case and the hypotheses $(H)$, is not established in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Jinsil Lee and Yong-Hoon Lee, “Regularity of solutions for singular fractional differential equation”, arXiv:2202.09015 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09015

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

R023.title: Fields Group superspace harmonic-generation conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $d_j:\Omega_n\to\Omega_n$ be defined for $j\geq1$ by

$$
d_j(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i\frac{\partial^j f}{\partial x_i^j},
$$

and let $\delta_n\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the Vandermonde determinant. Let $SR_n$ be the superspace coinvariant algebra and identify its harmonic space with the orthogonal complement of its defining ideal. **Fields Group harmonic-generation conjecture.** The harmonic space of $SR_n$ is generated by the $2^{n-1}$ elements

$$
d_1^{\epsilon_1}d_2^{\epsilon_2}\cdots d_{n-1}^{\epsilon_{n-1}}(\delta_n),
$$

where each $\epsilon_i\in\{0,1\}$. These elements are known to be harmonic, but the claimed generation and the resulting structure remain unresolved in the source.
R023.source_name: Brendon Rhoades, “Generalizations of the flag variety tied to the Macdonald-theoretic delta operators”, arXiv:2204.03386 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03386

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2022).

R023.title: Full generic regularity II for min-max minimal hypersurfaces
R023.statement: Let $M^{n+1}$ be a closed smooth manifold, and let $g$ be a Baire $C^\infty$-generic Riemannian metric on $M$. A **min-max $g$-minimal hypersurface** is a minimal hypersurface generated by min-max theory. **Full generic regularity II.** Every min-max $g$-minimal hypersurface is smooth. This extends the preceding generic regularity conjecture from area minimizers to min-max minimal hypersurfaces, which are not generally area minimizing. The conjecture is relevant to extending generic regularity and density results to higher dimensions.
R023.source_name: Yangyang Li and Zhihan Wang, “Minimal hypersurfaces for generic metrics in dimension 8”, arXiv:2205.01047 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01047

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2022). “This multiplicity one conjecture was confirmed by X. Zhou for dimensions $3 \leq n+1 \leq 7$, where he applied the min-max construction for hypersurfaces with prescribed mean curvature developed by J. Zhu and himself .”

R023.title: Green-function decay and boundary regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a one-sided NTA domain whose Green function with some pole $p$ satisfies, for some $\delta>0$ and constants $c_1,c_2>0$, bounds of the form

$$
c_1\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\Omega)^\delta\leq G(z,p)\leq c_2\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\Omega)^\delta
$$

for all $z\in\Omega$ sufficiently close to $\partial\Omega$. **Green-function decay conjecture.** Necessarily $\delta=1$, and $\partial\Omega$ has a certain weak smoothness, at least being rectifiable. The statement is presented as an easier conjecture related to the preceding boundary-regularity questions, but no general proof is supplied.
R023.source_name: Alexander Volberg, “One phase problem for two positive harmonic function: below the codimension 1 threshold”, arXiv:2205.03687 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03687

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2022). “Any solution of Conjecture should first eliminate the possibility of infinitely connected domain.”

R023.title: Conjecture on regularity of $J_p$-harmonic maps
R023.statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be hyperbolic surfaces, let $p>2$, and let $u_p:M\rightarrow N$ satisfy the $J_p$-Euler–Lagrange equations. **Regularity conjecture.** The map $u_p$ belongs to $C^{1,\alpha}$. The paper notes that minimizing $p$-harmonic maps have this regularity, while the corresponding higher regularity for $J_p$-minimizers is left as an open question.
R023.source_name: Georgios Daskalopoulos and Karen Uhlenbeck, “Analytic properties of Stretch maps and geodesic laminations”, arXiv:2205.08250 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08250

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the Hofstadter H sequence limit density
R023.statement: Let $mu$ be the absolutely continuous limit measure of the numbers $alpha H(n)\mod 1$, where $alpha$ is the real root of $x^3+x=1$ and $H$ is Hofstadter's $H$ sequence. **Regularity conjecture.** The probability density function of $mu$ is continuous but not differentiable. The paper notes that the rate of decay of the Fourier coefficients is unknown; the asserted regularity is presented as a consequence of the observed decay and remains unproved.
R023.source_name: Rodrigo Angelo, “A hidden signal in Hofstadter's H sequence”, arXiv:2206.00750 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00750

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2022). “These numbers have been extensively studied for instance Pisot proved they are precisely the ones with the property that $\| \alpha^n \| \rightarrow 0$ quickly. Another incredible property of these numbers conjectured by Vijay”

R023.title: Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $X\subseteq\mathbb P^r$ be a nondegenerate projective variety. Its Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity is denoted by $\operatorname{reg} X$, its degree by $\deg X$, and its codimension by $\operatorname{codim} X$. **Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{reg} X\leq\deg X-\operatorname{codim} X+1.
$$

This conjecture proposes a bound for the homological complexity of a projective variety in terms of its degree and codimension. It is refuted: counterexamples were found by McCullough and Peeva.
R023.source_name: Junho Choe, “Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of unprojections and the Eisenbud-Goto regularity conjecture”, arXiv:2206.06151 (2024).
R023.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2106.12667](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12667), [arXiv:1406.7404](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7404), [arXiv:1402.1906](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1906), [arXiv:1110.2124](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.2124), [arXiv:1012.5329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.5329).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06151

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “But counterexamples to the regularity conjecture have been found by McCullough and Peeva .”

R023.title: Eventual linearity of associated-prime counts for Inc-invariant monomial chains
R023.statement: Let ${\mathcal I}=(I_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be an $\operatorname{Inc}$-invariant chain of monomial ideals. **Associated-prime count conjecture.** The number of associated primes of $I_n$ is eventually a linear function of $n$. This expectation arises from computational experiments and is presented as an open problem related to the regularity conjecture; no proof or disproof is given in the source.
R023.source_name: Dinh Van Le and Hop D. Nguyen, “On regularity and projective dimension of invariant chains of monomial ideals”, arXiv:2206.15141 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15141

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

R023.title: The four-color bound for locally irregular edge colorings of colorable graphs
R023.statement:
All graphs in this paper are finite and simple. A graph is **locally irregular** if the degrees of the endpoints of every edge are distinct. A locally irregular edge coloring is an edge coloring in which every color class induces a locally irregular subgraph. A graph is **colorable** if it admits such a coloring, and for a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a locally irregular edge coloring.

**Four-color bound.** Every colorable connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\operatorname{irr}}^{\prime}(G)\leq 4.
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of the refuted Local Irregularity Conjecture, motivated by the bow-tie graph, which requires four colors. The supplied text does not establish whether the four-color bound is proved or remains open.
R023.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “A note on the locally irregular edge colorings of cacti”, arXiv:2207.03143 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03143

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2022). “Recently, it has been observed that the conjecture does not hold for the bow-tie graph $B$, since $B$ is colorable and requires at least $4$ colors for a locally irregular edge coloring.”

R023.title: The four-color bound for locally irregular edge colorings
R023.statement:
A graph is **locally irregular** if the degrees of the end-vertices of every edge are distinct. An edge coloring is **locally irregular** if every color induces a locally irregular subgraph. A graph is **colorable** if it admits a locally irregular edge coloring. For a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\rm irr}^{\prime}(G)$ be the smallest number of colors required by such a coloring. **The four-color bound.** Every colorable connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\rm irr}^{\prime}(G)\leq 4.
$$

This weaker version of the Local Irregularity Conjecture is established for all colorable cacti, as stated in the paper’s context, so the candidate is treated as solved.
R023.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Local Irregularity Conjecture vs. cacti”, arXiv:2207.03941 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03941

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a gap-free graph and let $I=I(G)$ be its edge ideal. For each integer $s\ge 2$, write $I^{(s)}$ for the $s$-th symbolic power of $I$. **Regularity conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I^s)=\operatorname{reg}(I^{(s)})=\max\{\operatorname{reg} I+s-1,2s\}.
$$

The proposed formula extends the preceding results for small powers, which establish the equality for $s\le 3$ and prove the displayed bound for $s=2,3$ in the gap-free case. Whether the formula holds for every $s\ge 2$ is left open in the source.
R023.source_name: Nguyen Cong Minh and Thanh Vu, “Characterization of graphs whose a small power of their edge ideals has a linear free resolution”, arXiv:2208.13745 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.13745

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

R023.title: Madani–Kiani's maximal-clique regularity conjecture for binomial edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $S$ be the polynomial ring used to define its binomial edge ideal $J_G$, and let $c(G)$ be the number of maximal cliques of $G$. **Madani–Kiani's conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/J_G)\leq c(G).
$$

The conjecture was proved for closed graphs, generalized block graphs, chordal graphs, fan graphs of complete graphs, $P_4$-free graphs, block graphs, and semi-block graphs, among other classes. The source states that it was subsequently proved for all graphs with a sharp bound, so the conjecture is resolved.
R023.source_name: Priya Das, “Recent results on homological properties of binomial edge ideal of graphs”, arXiv:2209.01201 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01201

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2022). “The conjecture in general remains as one of the important open problem in this area.”

R023.title: Integrability conjecture for the Fourier transform of extremal functions
R023.statement: Let $\varphi_p$ be the extremal function for the Paley–Wiener extremal problem, and let $\widehat{\varphi}_p$ denote its Fourier transform. **Fourier-transform regularity conjecture.** If $1<p<\infty$, then $\widehat{\varphi}_p$ is a continuous integrable function on $(-\pi,\pi)$. The source explains that the analogous properties are automatic for $0<p\leq1$ and conjectures them in the strictly convex regime.
R023.source_name: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Andrés Chirre, Joaquim Ortega-Cerdà and Kristian Seip, “Point evaluation in Paley–Wiener spaces”, arXiv:2210.13922 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

R023.title: Regularity of successor thorns under large-cardinal assumptions
R023.statement:
Let $\textit{\th}_0=\omega$, let $\textit{\th}_{\alpha+1}=\textup{\TH}(\textit{\th}_\alpha^\omega)$, and for limit $\gamma$ let $\textit{\th}_\gamma=\bigcup_{\alpha<\gamma}\textit{\th}_\alpha$. Assume sufficient large cardinals and $\mathrm{V}\ne\mathrm{L}(X^\omega)$ for every set $X$. **Regularity conjecture.** For every ordinal $\alpha>0$, 
$$
\textit{\th}_{\alpha+1}=\textit{\th}_\alpha^+
$$
 is regular. This anticipated calculation of the thorn sequence is used in the paper's programme of obtaining stronger forms of choice over the Chang model; the supplied text does not establish the assertion or indicate whether it has been resolved.
R023.source_name: James Holland and Grigor Sargsyan, “Forcing More DC Over the Chang Model Using the Thorn Sequence”, arXiv:2210.16359 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16359

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

R023.title: Strict hierarchy conjecture for polynomial partition regularity
R023.statement: For $d\geq 1$, let $P_d$ be the set of polynomials in countably many variables with nonnegative integer coefficients, constant term, and degree at most $d$ in each variable. A pattern is **partition regular** over $P_d$ if every finite coloring of $P_d$ contains a monochromatic realization of the pattern, and it **appears** in $P_i$ if its one-coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $P_i$. **Strict hierarchy conjecture.** For all $1\leq i<j$, there exists a pattern $\mathcal{F}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is partition regular in $P_j$ but not in $P_i$, while $\mathcal{F}$ appears in $P_i$. This proposes that partition regularity over the bounded-degree polynomial settings has genuinely distinct levels; the paper gives the conjecture as complementary to the non-partition-regularity conjecture for $\{x,y,x+y,xy\}$, and no general resolution is supplied.
R023.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, “Monochromatic Sums and Products of Polynomials”, arXiv:2211.00766 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00766

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

R023.title: The bow-tie version of the Local Irregularity Conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $\mathfrak{T'}$ be the family consisting of the recursively defined family $\mathfrak{T}$ together with all odd-length paths and odd-length cycles, and let $B$ be the bow-tie graph. Let ${\rm lir}(G)$ denote the locally irregular chromatic index of a locally irregular colorable graph $G$. **Bow-tie version of the Local Irregularity Conjecture.** Every connected graph $G\notin\mathfrak{T'}$, except for the bow-tie graph $B$, satisfies 
$$
{\rm lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$
 This formulation incorporates the bow-tie counterexample to the original conjecture. The cited work proves the bound for every locally irregular colorable cactus other than $B$, but the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec and Mariusz Woźniak, “Local Irregularity Conjecture for 2-multigraphs versus cacti”, arXiv:2211.08270 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.08270

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2022). “Recently it has been proved that there is only one cactus which requires 4 colors for a locally irregular coloring and therefore the Local Irregularity Conjecture was disproved.”

R023.title: Hasse-regularity conjecture for flag strata of Hodge-type Shimura varieties
R023.statement: Let $(G,\mu)$ be a cocharacter datum over $\mathbb{F}_q$, and let $(X,\zeta)$ satisfy the paper's stated assumptions. Let $Y$ be the flag space of $X$, stratified by flag strata $Y_w$, and let $z=\sigma(w_{0,I})w_0$, where $w_{0,I}$ and $w_0$ are the relevant longest Weyl-group elements. A flag stratum is **Hasse-regular** when the saturated cone generated by sections induced from the Hasse stack equals the saturated cone of all sections on its closure. **Hasse-regularity conjecture.** The flag stratum $Y_z$ is Hasse-regular. This property would control the weights of sections on the maximal open flag stratum through Hasse invariants. It is known in the Hilbert--Blumenthal example described in the paper, but the general assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: Wushi Goldring and Jean-Stefan Koskivirta, “Griffiths-Schmid conditions for automorphic forms via characteristic p”, arXiv:2211.16819 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16819

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2022). “In particular, Conjecture says in this case that $\langle C_{X} \rangle = C_{\Hasse}$, which was indeed proved in .”

R023.title: Regularity bound for squarefree parts of symbolic powers of edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $I(G)$ denote its edge ideal, let $I(G)^{\{s\}}$ denote the squarefree part of its $s$-th symbolic power, and let ${\rm match}(G)$ denote the matching number of $G$. **Squarefree symbolic-power regularity conjecture.** For every integer $s$ such that $I(G)^{\{s\}}\neq 0$, one has

$$
{\rm reg}(I(G)^{\{s\}})\leq {\rm match}(G)+s.
$$

This proposes that the matching-number upper bound known in the source for squarefree powers should also hold for squarefree parts of symbolic powers. The source presents this as a conjecture and supplies no evidence of resolution.
R023.source_name: S. A. Seyed Fakhari, “On the Regularity of squarefree part of symbolic powers of edge ideals”, arXiv:2303.02791 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02791

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for Šoltés graphs
R023.statement: A **Šoltés graph** is a graph $G$ for which deleting any vertex leaves the Wiener index unchanged. **Regularity conjecture.** If $G$ is a Šoltés graph, then $G$ is regular. This conjecture proposes that every solution to the Šoltés problem has all vertices of the same degree; the source gives no resolution.
R023.source_name: Nino Bašić, Martin Knor and Riste Škrekovski, “On regular graphs with Šoltés vertices”, arXiv:2303.11996 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11996

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for monomial geometric subsets
R023.statement:
Let $(A_1,\ldots,A_s)$ be a tuple of monomial algebras, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}^{A_1,\ldots,A_s}(X)$ be the associated monomial geometric subset. Write $k=\dim(A_1)+\cdots+\dim(A_s)$, and call the tuple regular when

$$
\mathrm{Hilb}^{A_1+\cdots+A_s}(X)=\mathrm{CHilb}^k(X)\cap\mathrm{Hilb}^{A_1,\ldots,A_s}(X).
$$
 **Regularity conjecture.** All monomial geometric subsets are regular. The authors state that regularity should not be restrictive, but no proof or resolution is supplied in the given text.
R023.source_name: Gergely Bérczi, “Tautological integrals on Hilbert scheme of points II: Geometric subsets”, arXiv:2303.14812 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14812

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

R023.title: Bounded additive group irregularity strength for graphs without small components
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with no connected components of order less than $3$. A **$\Gamma$-irregular labeling** is a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of an abelian group $\Gamma$ such that the induced vertex weights are pairwise distinct; denote the group irregularity strength by the least group order guaranteeing such a labeling for every abelian group of that order. **Bounded additive group irregularity conjecture.** There exists a constant $K$ such that every such graph $G$ has a $\Gamma$-irregular labeling for every group $\Gamma$ satisfying

$$
|\Gamma|\geq n+K.
$$

The conjecture asserts a uniform additive bound on the group irregularity strength for graphs whose components all have order at least $3$, extending the preceding bounds for broad classes of disconnected graphs. Its resolution would determine whether the dependence on the graph order can always be reduced to $n+O(1)$ in this setting.
R023.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz and Barbara Krupińska, “Group irregularity strength of disconnected graphs”, arXiv:2306.11914 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11914

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

R023.title: Trinajstić's regularity conjecture for zero index
R023.statement:
Let $NT(G)$ denote the Trinajstić index of a graph $G$. The conjecture concerns graphs attaining its minimum value.

**Trinajstić regularity conjecture.** The minimum value of the Trinajstić index is $0$, and being regular is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a graph to attain this minimum.

The paper states that this conjecture is false and presents a class of nonregular graphs with zero Trinajstić index. Thus, regularity is not necessary for attaining the minimum.
R023.source_name: Linus Tang, “Extremal Bounds on Peripherality Measures”, arXiv:2306.15702 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15702

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for graphs with lexicographically optimal Cartesian squares
R023.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and consider the Cartesian square $G\times G$. An ordering of the vertices is optimal for the edge-isoperimetric problem (EIP) when it minimizes the number of boundary edges among vertex sets of each prescribed size. The **lexicographic order** on tuples is defined by declaring $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ greater than $(y_1,\dots,y_n)$ if, for some $i$, one has $x_j=y_j$ for $1\leq j<i$ and $x_i>y_i$. **Regularity conjecture.** If the lexicographic order is optimal for $G\times G$, then $G$ is regular. The conjecture seeks to characterize graphs for which the lexicographic order is optimal on all Cartesian powers. The local-global principle shows that optimality for $G\times G$ implies optimality for $G^n$ for every $n\geq 3$, but no general method is known for establishing optimality on Cartesian squares of concrete graphs.
R023.source_name: Sergei L. Bezrukov, Pavle Bulatovic and Nikola Kuzmanovski, “New infinite family of regular edge-isoperimetric graphs”, arXiv:2307.05332 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05332

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R023.title: Alweiss's non-partition-regularity conjecture for sums and products over polynomial colorings
R023.statement:
For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P_d$ be the set of polynomials in a countable set of variables $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, constant term, and degree at most $d$ in each variable. A pattern is **partition regular over $P_d$** if every finite coloring of $P_d$ contains a monochromatic realization of that pattern.

**Alweiss's non-partition-regularity conjecture.** There exists $n$ such that, for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, the pattern

$$
\left\{\sum_{i\in S}x_i,\ \prod_{i\in S}x_i: \varnothing\ne S\subseteq[n]\right\}
$$

is not partition regular over $P_d$.

The statement is presented as essentially asserting that the methods of the paper are necessary for addressing Hindman's conjecture over polynomial colorings. It remains open; even the weaker assertion that Hindman's conjecture is false over $P_d$ is not known.
R023.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, “Monochromatic Sums and Products over Q”, arXiv:2307.08901 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08901

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R023.title: C^{1,1} geodesic conjecture for the coupled dHYM system
R023.statement: Let $(X,\alpha^{\mathbb{C}})$ be a complexified Kähler manifold in the hypercritical range, and let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the space of admissible potentials. **C^{1,1} geodesic conjecture.** If $(X,\alpha^{\mathbb{C}})$ is hypercritical, then for every $\varphi_0,\varphi_1\in\mathcal{H}$ there is a unique path $\varphi_t\in\mathcal{H}$ solving the coupled geodesic equation, joining $\varphi_0$ to $\varphi_1$, such that $\varphi_t\in\mathcal{C}^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{C})$. This is expected to extend the known $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$ regularity for the degenerate dHYM geodesic equation to the coupled system, giving geodesic connectivity of the space of admissible potentials.
R023.source_name: Carlo Scarpa, “A K-energy functional for complexified Kähler classes”, arXiv:2307.09904 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09904

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R023.title: Boundary-determined maximal regularity conjecture for Gaussian stochastic fields
