R023.statement: A **Gaussian stochastic field** is a stochastic field whose finite-dimensional distributions are Gaussian. Its **boundary behaviour** means the behaviour of the field when restricted to the boundary of its parameter domain. **Boundary regularity conjecture.** For a Gaussian stochastic field, the maximal regularity is in general dictated by its behaviour on the boundary. This conjecture suggests that regularity estimates for local times should reflect the regularity of the field on the boundary; the source does not establish sharpness of its regularity results, and the conjecture remains open.
R023.source_name: Florian Bechtold, Fabian A. Harang and Hannes Kern, “A multiparameter Stochastic Sewing lemma and the regularity of local times associated to Gaussian sheets”, arXiv:2307.11527 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.11527

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R023.title: Non-regularity of polar spaces induced from proper dual subspaces
R023.statement:
Let $q$ be the form described in the paper's construction, let $V$ be its underlying vector space, and let $V'$ be a proper subspace of $V^*$ such that

$$
\ker(V')=\{0\}.
$$

Let the induced form on $V\oplus V'$ define a polar space.

**Non-regularity conjecture.** The polar space associated to this induced form is non-regular.

The conjecture is motivated by the failure of the identity needed to reproduce the regularity proof for the original quadric when $V^*$ is replaced by a proper subspace $V'$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
R023.source_name: Antonio Pasini, “Regularity in polar spaces of infinite rank”, arXiv:2307.16293 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.16293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R023.title: The Mumford–Shah conjecture on planar minimizer structure
R023.statement:
Let $(K,u)$ be a normalized minimizer of the Mumford–Shah functional $E_\lambda$ in a planar domain. The singular set $K$ is the union of finitely many closed $C^1$ arcs $\gamma_i$ that do not cross and may meet at their endpoints at angles of $120$ degrees in triple junctions. In particular, for every $x\in K$, the set $K\cap B_r(x)$ in any sufficiently small disk is diffeomorphic to one of the following: a radius of $B_r(x)$, a diameter of $B_r(x)$, or three radii of $B_r(x)$ meeting at angles of $120$ degrees.

**Mumford–Shah conjecture.** If $(K,u)$ is a minimizer of $E_\lambda$, then $K$ has the structure described above.

This is the central planar regularity conjecture for the Mumford–Shah functional and remains unsolved. The statement predicts that minimizer singular sets have only smooth arcs, crack tips, and triple junctions, with no further pathological terminal or accumulation points.
R023.source_name: Camillo De Lellis and Matteo Focardi, “The regularity theory for the Mumford-Shah functional on the plane”, arXiv:2308.14660 (2025).
R023.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1610.03784](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.03784), [arXiv:1610.01846](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.01846), [arXiv:0809.4174](https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.4174), [arXiv:0806.2994](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2994).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14660

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

R023.title: The K-global F-regularity conjecture for semiample anticanonical pairs
R023.statement:
Let $(X,B)$ be a normal projective complex pair with klt singularities such that $-K_X-B$ is semiample. **K-global F-regularity conjecture.** For every model $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{B})\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $(X,B)$, the locus

$$
\left\{\mathfrak{p}\in\operatorname{Spec}(A)\ \middle|\ (X_{\mathfrak{p}},B_{\mathfrak{p}})\text{ is K-globally F-regular}\right\}
$$

is dense in $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. This extends the expected dense reduction behavior from log Calabi--Yau and log Fano settings to semiample anticanonical klt pairs; the source does not state a resolution.
R023.source_name: Marta Benozzo, Iacopo Brivio and Chi-Kang Chang, “On the superadditivity of anticanonical Iitaka dimension”, arXiv:2309.16580 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16580

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “Although still open in general, this conjecture is proven for many important classes of fibrations ().”

R023.title: $C^{1,1}$ regularity conjecture for the minimal Bellman function
R023.statement: Let $f$ be a smooth uniformly bounded function, and let $\mathbb{B}_\varepsilon$ denote the minimal function associated with $f$ on the domain $\Omega_\varepsilon$. **$C^{1,1}$ regularity conjecture.** The function $\mathbb{B}_\varepsilon$ is of class $C^{1,1}$. The conjecture is motivated by known $C^{1,1}$ regularity results for the homogeneous Monge–Ampère equation on strictly convex domains with smooth boundary data, while the free-boundary setting here remains unresolved. The source notes that the smoothness and boundedness assumptions on $f$ may be stronger than necessary.
R023.source_name: Dmitriy Stolyarov, Vasily Vasyunin and Pavel Zatitskii, “Martingale transforms of bounded random variables and indicator functions of events”, arXiv:2310.02362 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02362

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

R023.title: $C^{1,1}$ regularity conjecture for the functions $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$
R023.statement: Let $f$ be a smooth uniformly bounded function, and let $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ be the two functions associated with $f$ in the paper's Bellman-function formulation. **$C^{1,1}$ regularity conjecture for $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$.** The functions $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ are of class $C^{1,1}$. This is the second smoothness conjecture proposed after comparison with regularity results for homogeneous Monge–Ampère boundary value problems. The source gives no evidence that either conjecture has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Dmitriy Stolyarov, Vasily Vasyunin and Pavel Zatitskii, “Martingale transforms of bounded random variables and indicator functions of events”, arXiv:2310.02362 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02362

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

R023.title: The strong $\pi$-regularity conjecture for pseudo $\pi$-polar $\pi$-UU rings
R023.statement: Let $R$ be a ring. A ring is **pseudo $\pi$-polar** if it satisfies the pseudo $\pi$-polar condition, and **$\pi$-UU** if every unit $u\in U(R)$ has $1-u^n\in J(R)$ for some integer $n\geq 1$. **Strong $\pi$-regularity conjecture.** Every pseudo $\pi$-polar $\pi$-UU ring is strongly $\pi$-regular, and hence periodic. This would extend the established equivalence between strongly $\pi$-regular pseudo $\pi$-polar rings and periodic rings, while the preceding example shows that pseudo $\pi$-polarity alone does not imply the $\pi$-UU property.
R023.source_name: Jian Cui, Peter Danchev and Yuedi Zeng, “Some New Results on Pseudo n-Strong Drazin Inverses in Rings”, arXiv:2312.02347 (2023).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for horospherical tangent cones of symmetric spaces
R023.statement: Consider the horospherical tangent cones at infinity of symmetric spaces, with restricted root systems whose factors determine the relevant types. **Regularity conjecture.** The horospherical tangent cones at infinity of the symmetric spaces are irregular, except for the symmetric spaces whose restricted root system has all factors of type $A$. Explicit rank-two computations suggest this pattern, but the systematic determination of regularity is stated to be unknown.
R023.source_name: Tran-Trung Nghiem, “Calabi-Yau metrics on rank two symmetric spaces with horospherical tangent cone at infinity”, arXiv:2401.05122 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05122

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

R023.title: Irrationality conjecture for the roots associated with an infinite family of horospherical cones
R023.statement:
For each integer $r\geq 5$, define

$$
Q(t,r)=\int_{\frac{-4}{2+t}}^{\frac{2r-6}{1+t}}p(4+(2+t)p)^2(4r-8-tp)^2(2r-6-(1+t)p)^{2r-7}(2r-2+p)^{2r-7}\,dp.
$$

The equation $Q(t,r)=0$ has a unique positive root. **Irrationality conjecture.** For all $r\geq 5$, this unique positive root is irrational. This is presented as an algebro-arithmetic reformulation of the regularity conjecture for the family $\operatorname{SL}_{r}/\operatorname{S}(\operatorname{GL}_2\times\operatorname{GL}_{r-2})$; the source attributes the polynomial characterization of the K-stability condition to previous work, while the irrationality remains conjectural.
R023.source_name: Tran-Trung Nghiem, “Calabi-Yau metrics on rank two symmetric spaces with horospherical tangent cone at infinity”, arXiv:2401.05122 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05122

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

R023.title: The Dao-number regularity conjecture for ideals
R023.statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be the local ring under consideration, let $I\subset R$ be an ideal, let $\mathcal{R}(\mathfrak{m})=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathfrak{m}^k$ be the Rees algebra of $\mathfrak{m}$, and let $\mathcal{R}(\mathfrak{m},I)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}I\mathfrak{m}^k$ be the extension of $I$ in $\mathcal{R}(\mathfrak{m})$. Write $\mathfrak{d}_1(I)$, $\mathfrak{d}_2(I)$, and $\mathfrak{d}_3(I)$ for the Dao numbers of $I$. **Dao-number regularity conjecture.** For all ideals $I\subset R$:

$$
\mathfrak{d}_2(I)\le\mathfrak{d}_3(I)=\mathfrak{d}_1(I)\le\operatorname{reg}_{\mathcal{R}(\mathfrak{m})}\mathcal{R}(\mathfrak{m},I).
$$

The paper proves this bound under additional hypotheses, namely when $\operatorname{depth}\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(I)>0$ or when $R$ is regular; the conjecture asserts that the same inequality holds for every ideal in the setting considered.
R023.source_name: Antonino Ficarra, “Dao numbers and the asymptotic behaviour of fullness”, arXiv:2402.05555 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05555

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

R023.title: Regularity formula for t-path ideals of unicyclic graphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple graph having at most one cycle $C$ of length $m$. Let $t\geq 2$ be a natural number. Write $S$ for the polynomial ring associated with $G$, $I_t(G)$ for its $t$-path ideal, $\nu_t(G)$ for the maximum number of pairwise suitable $t$-paths in $G$, and call $G$ **$t$-proximal** when it satisfies the corresponding $t$-proximity condition. Then

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(G))=\begin{cases}
(t-1)\nu_t(G)+\left(\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(C))-(t-1)\nu_3(C)\right), & \text{if }G\text{ is }t\text{-proximal},\\
(t-1)\nu_t(G), & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Regularity conjecture for t-path ideals.** The displayed formula should hold. In particular,

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/I_t(G))=(t-1)\nu_t(G)
$$

when $G$ is a tree. This conjecture is presented as a natural generalization of the paper's theorem for $3$-path ideals; the supplied text gives no resolution status for the general $t$-path statement.
R023.source_name: Nguyen Thu Hang and Thanh Vu, “Projective dimension and regularity of 3-path ideals of unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:2402.16166 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for the quasi-canonical intersection space
R023.statement:
For $0\leq r\leq n$, let $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_n$ be the formal scheme constructed from the relevant Rapoport--Zink spaces, and let $p$ be the residue characteristic. **Regularity and tame normal-crossings conjecture.** The formal scheme $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_n$ is regular, and its special fiber is a tame divisor with normal crossings: for every geometric point $x$, there are regular parameters $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ in the completed local ring such that

$$
\varpi=\prod_{i=1}^n X_i^{m_i},
$$

where each $m_i$ is prime to $p$. This local-structure conjecture would provide the regularity and controlled reduction needed for the arithmetic intersection theory developed in the paper; the general structure is described as mysterious.
R023.source_name: Chao Li, Michael Rapoport and Wei Zhang, “Quasi-canonical AFL and Arithmetic Transfer conjectures at parahoric levels”, arXiv:2404.02214 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for finite-state string machines without a meta-vertex
R023.statement: Let a **string machine** be composed only of finite-state transducers, with the input and output categories of each transducer being tape categories. Suppose it has one free input $X\to X$ in a tape category $\mathcal{X}$ whose generating morphisms form a set $\Sigma$ and are all endomorphisms of the generating object $X$. Assume its sole output is a state space $S(A)$, with some subset designated as accepting. An endomorphism $X\to X$ in $\mathcal{X}$ that contains no instances of the copy morphism is regarded as a string over $\Sigma$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every language over $\Sigma$ accepted by this string machine is regular. The conjecture asserts that finite-state string machines without a meta-vertex have no more language-recognition power than finite automata; the paper presents a sketch intended to establish it, but the supplied text gives no resolution status.
R023.source_name: Nur Cataltepe and Vanessa Kosoy, “Time complexity for deterministic string machines”, arXiv:2405.06043 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06043

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Generic existence of regular points and Birkhoff averages
R023.statement: Let a dynamical system have a positive-volume subset of its ambient space. A point is **$p\omega$-regular** if it has the regularity property denoted by $p\omega$ in the source; forward Birkhoff averages and forward Lyapunov exponents are understood in the usual sense. **Generic regularity conjecture.** For a dense/generic subset of dynamical systems, there exists a positive-volume subset in the ambient space such that at least one of the following holds: the points are $p\omega$-regular; forward Birkhoff averages exist at all points; or forward Lyapunov exponents exist and the points are Lyapunov regular. This would yield physical measures for the smooth systems in the open classes of non-uniformly hyperbolic flows and diffeomorphisms discussed in the paper, and a criterion for obtaining physical/SRB measures from the sectional Lyapunov spectrum.
R023.source_name: Vitor Araujo and Luciana Salgado, “A characterization of physical measures for systems with mixed central behavior”, arXiv:2405.10144 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: The Local Irregularity Conjecture excluding the bow-tie graph
R023.statement:
Let $B$ be the bow-tie graph, and let $G$ be a connected graph that is locally irregularly colorable. Write $\operatorname{lir}(G)$ for its locally irregular chromatic index.

**Local Irregularity Conjecture.** If $G\neq B$, then

$$
\operatorname{lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This is the improved form of the original conjecture after the bow-tie graph was found to require four colors. The source reports this as a conjecture established by Sedlar and Škrekovski, with the bound proved for cacti other than $B$.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Tomáš Madaras, Alfréd Onderko and Roman Soták, “On a new problem about the local irregularity of graphs”, arXiv:2405.13893 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13893

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Regularity extensions of Pyber, Cameron and Vdovin's conjectures
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with a core-free maximal subgroup, and let $m(G)$ be the minimal index of a core-free maximal subgroup. Let $R_{\rm max}(G)$, $R_{\rm ns}(G)$ and $R_{\rm sol}(G)$ be the corresponding regularity invariants. **Regularity conjectures.**

$$
R_{\rm max}(G)\leqslant c\log_{m(G)}|G|
$$

for an absolute constant $c$; $R_{\rm ns}(G)\leqslant 7$ for every finite almost simple group $G$, with equality if and only if $G={\rm M}_{24}$; and $R_{\rm sol}(G)\leqslant 5$ for every finite group $G$ with trivial soluble radical. These are proposed natural extensions of the preceding base-size conjectures; the supplied text records partial results and special cases, but does not establish resolution of the full three-part proposal.
R023.source_name: Marina Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Timothy C. Burness, “On the regularity number of a finite group and other base-related invariants”, arXiv:2405.15300 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Mixed nilpotent-soluble regularity conjecture for symmetric and alternating groups
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be either $S_n$ or $A_n$ with $n\geqslant 13$, and let $(H,K)$ be a pair of subgroups of $G$, where $H$ is nilpotent and $K$ is soluble. A pair $(H,K)$ is **regular** when it satisfies the regularity condition defined for subgroup tuples in the paper. **Mixed nilpotent-soluble regularity conjecture.** Every such pair $(H,K)$ is regular.

The conjecture extends known results that every nilpotent pair is regular for $n\geqslant 5$ except for $S_8$. It is motivated by computations in low degrees, and its general validity remains open.
R023.source_name: Marina Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Timothy C. Burness, “On the regularity number of a finite group and other base-related invariants”, arXiv:2405.15300 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for t-connected ideals of trees
R023.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $J_t(T)$ denote the $t$-connected ideal of $T$. Let $\mathcal H$ be the hypergraph corresponding to $J_t(T)$, and write $\nu(\mathcal H)$ for its matching number. **Regularity conjecture for t-connected ideals.** One has

$$
\operatorname{reg}(R/J_t(T))=(t-1)\nu(\mathcal H).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computational evidence and by the fact that the analogous formula holds in the examples discussed in the paper, but its general validity for trees is left open.
R023.source_name: Kanoy Kumar Das, Amit Roy and Kamalesh Saha, “On the path ideals of chordal graphs”, arXiv:2405.15897 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15897

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Anderson's generic regularity conjecture for the boundary map of Einstein 3-manifolds
R023.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a $3$-dimensional manifold with smooth boundary $\Sigma$ satisfying $\pi_1(\Omega,\Sigma)=0$. For fixed $k$ and $\alpha$, let $\mathcal{M}^{k,\alpha}_\Lambda(\Omega)$ denote the moduli space of Einstein metrics with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, modulo the group $\mathscr D^{k+1,\alpha}(\Omega)$ of $\mathcal{C}^{k+1,\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms restricting to the identity on $\Sigma$. For a metric $g$, write $g^\intercal$ for its induced boundary metric, let $[g^\intercal]$ be its conformal class, let $H_g$ be its boundary mean curvature, and let $\mathcal{S}_1^{k,\alpha}(\Sigma)$ be the space of conformal classes of $\mathcal{C}^{k,\alpha}$ Riemannian metrics on $\Sigma$, identified with unit-determinant representatives. The boundary map is

$$
\Pi:\mathcal{M}^{k,\alpha}_\Lambda(\Omega)/\mathscr D^{k+1,\alpha}(\Omega)\longrightarrow\mathcal{S}_1^{k,\alpha}(\Sigma)\times\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}^{k-1,\alpha}(\Sigma),\qquad \Pi(g)=([g^\intercal],H_g).
$$

**Anderson's conjecture.** For each fixed $\Lambda$, the boundary map $\Pi$ is regular at generic metrics, meaning that its linearization is surjective with split kernel at those metrics.

Because Einstein metrics in dimension $3$ have constant sectional curvature, they are more rigid than higher-dimensional Einstein metrics. The conjecture asserts that this rigidity does not prevent generic regularity of the boundary data map; its resolution is not supplied in the source, so it is recorded as open.
R023.source_name: Zhongshan An and Lan-Hsuan Huang, “Local structure theory of Einstein manifolds with boundary”, arXiv:2405.17577 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17577

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R023.title: Asymptotic uncovered-vertex probability for dense almost-regular hypergraphs
R023.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be a positive integer and let $0<\delta,\varepsilon<1$ be positive real numbers. There is an $n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, if $H$ is an $n$-vertex $k$-graph whose vertex degrees lie between $(1-n^{-\delta})d$ and $(1+n^{-\delta})d$ for some $d>n^{\varepsilon}$, and whose maximum codegree is at most $n^{-\delta}d$, then, for a uniformly random matching $M$ of $H$, writing $\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})$ for the probability that $M$ does not cover $v$, **the dense almost-regularity conjecture.** For every $v\in V(H)$,

$$
\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})=(1+o_n(1))d^{-1/k}.
$$

This is posed in the concluding remarks as the regime in which the disproved regular-linear conjecture may still hold: the paper's counterexamples rely on fixed $d$ and very large constructions, while the claim concerns degrees growing faster than a power of $n$.
R023.source_name: Hyunwoo Lee, “Random matchings in linear hypergraphs”, arXiv:2406.06421 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06421

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

R023.title: Conjecture on regularity bounds for squarefree powers of simplicial trees
R023.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial tree of dimension $t-1$, let $I(\Delta)$ denote its facet ideal in the polynomial ring $R$, and let $\nu_1(\Delta)$ and $\nu(\Delta)$ denote its induced matching number and matching number, respectively. The squarefree power $I(\Delta)^{[k]}$ is defined for $1\leq k\leq \nu(\Delta)$. **Regularity conjecture.**

$$
k-1+(t-1)\nu_1(\Delta) \leq \operatorname{reg}\left(\frac{R}{I(\Delta)^{[k]}} \right)\leq k-1+(t-1)\nu(\Delta)
$$

for all $1\leq k\leq \nu(\Delta)$. This would extend the expected regularity bounds for squarefree powers of edge ideals to simplicial trees; the preceding proposition establishes the lower bound, while the upper bound is the conjectural part.
R023.source_name: Elshani Kamberi, Francesco Navarra and Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, “On squarefree powers of simplicial trees”, arXiv:2406.13670 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

R023.title: The FKM conjecture on pairwise partition regularity of quadratic equations
R023.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in \mathbb{Z}$ be nonzero, and consider the homogeneous quadratic equation

$$
a x^2+b y^2=c z^2.
$$

An equation is **partition regular with respect to $x,y$** if every finite coloring of the positive integers admits a monochromatic choice of $x,y$ for which the equation has a solution in the remaining variable $z$.

**FKM's pairwise partition-regularity conjecture.** If at least one of $ac$, $bc$, or $(a+b)c$ is a square, then $a x^2+b y^2=c z^2$ is partition regular with respect to $x,y$.

The assumptions are motivated by necessary conditions developed in the paper, and the conjecture is known when $ac$ or $bc$ is a square. The remaining cases, including the equation $x^2+y^2=2z^2$ with respect to any two variables, remain open.
R023.source_name: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Oleksiy Klurman and Joel Moreira, “Partition regularity of generalized Pythagorean pairs”, arXiv:2407.08360 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08360

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2024).

R023.title: Booher–Cais conjecture for higher a-numbers in minimal-break-ratio towers
R023.statement:
Let $\{X_n\}$ be a $\mathbf Z_p$-tower of curves totally ramified over one point of $X_0\simeq\mathbf P^1$, with minimal break ratios and ramification invariant $d$. For a positive integer $r$, define

$$
a^r(X_n)=\dim_k\ker\left(V_{X_n}^r:\operatorname{H}^0(X_n,\Omega^1_{X_n})\to\operatorname{H}^0(X_n,\Omega^1_{X_n})\right).
$$

**Booher–Cais conjecture.** For each $r\geq 1$, there exist an integer $m_r$ and functions $b_r,\nu_r,\lambda_r:\mathbf Z/m_r\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$ such that, for $n\gg0$,

$$
a^r(X_n)=d\cdot\frac{r(p-1)}{2(p+1)((p-1)r+(p+1))}\cdot p^{2n}+b_r(n)\cdot p^n+\lambda_r(n)\cdot n+\nu_r(n).
$$

This is the specialization of the broader regularity conjecture to towers over $\mathbf P^1$ with minimal break ratios. The paper states that the formula is proved for the specific class under study, but the supplied status is unknown; the conjecture is therefore recorded as open.
R023.source_name: Jeremy Booher, Jack Hsieh, Rakesh Rivera, Vincent Tran, James Upton and Carol Wu, “Higher a-numbers in Z_p-towers via Counting Lattice Points”, arXiv:2407.13969 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13969

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

R023.title: The equitable semialgebraic regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-partite semialgebraic hypergraph in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with total degree $D$, and let $\varepsilon>0$. An **equitable partition** is a partition of each vertex part into parts of equal size, with the regularity properties asserted by the equitable semialgebraic regularity lemma.

**Equitable regularity conjecture.** The equitable semialgebraic regularity lemma holds with partitions into

$$
O_{d,k}\left((D/\varepsilon)^d\right)
$$

parts.

The proved regularity lemma has a loss in the dependence on $\varepsilon$ when passing to equitable partitions. The conjecture asks whether that loss can be removed in every dimension; the source notes that this is possible by a direct argument in dimension $d=1$.
R023.source_name: Jonathan Tidor and Hung-Hsun Hans Yu, “Multilevel polynomial partitioning and semialgebraic hypergraphs: regularity, Turán, and Zarankiewicz results”, arXiv:2407.20221 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

R023.title: Optimal regularity conjecture for K-finite matrix coefficients on compact symmetric spaces
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a semisimple Lie group with finite center, let $U$ be the compact simply connected semisimple Lie group with complexified Lie algebra corresponding to the compact dual, and let $K\subset U$ be the associated maximal compact subgroup. Write

$$
r=\lfloor \kappa(G)\rfloor,\qquad \delta=\kappa(G)-r,
$$

and let $U_r$ denote the subset of regular points. A matrix coefficient is **$K$-finite** if it is finite under the left and right actions of $K$.

**Optimal regularity conjecture.** Any $K$-finite matrix coefficient of a unitary representation of $U$ is in $C^{(r,\delta)}(U_r)$, and this regularity is optimal.

This conjecture concerns the sharp Hölder regularity of coefficients on the regular set of the compact symmetric space $U/K$. The paper proves the corresponding result for $K$-bi-invariant coefficients and establishes the full statement in special cases, while the general $K$-finite assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: Guillaume Dumas, “Regularity of K-finite matrix coefficients of semisimple Lie groups”, arXiv:2409.07944 (2024).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2305.09291](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.09291).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07944

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the stable moduli hypersurfaces
R023.statement: Let $\mathfrak M$ be a Banach-space moduli space of initial data, and for $\mathfrak r\in[0,1]$ let $\mathfrak M^\mathfrak r_\mathrm{stab}\subset\mathfrak M$ consist of initial data forming a black hole with asymptotic parameter ratio $|e_\infty|/M_\infty=\mathfrak r$. Let $\mathfrak M_\mathrm{black}$ be the subset of seed data forming a black hole in evolution. **Regularity conjecture.** For every $\mathfrak r\in[0,1]$, $\mathfrak M^\mathfrak r_\mathrm{stab}$ is a $C^1$ hypersurface in $\mathfrak M$. Moreover, $\mathfrak M_\mathrm{black}$ is foliated by the collection $\{\mathfrak M^\mathfrak r_\mathrm{stab}\}$. This conjectural picture concerns the local structure of the moduli space; the stable set associated with extremal black holes is expected in particular to be a connected regular hypersurface, but the asserted regularity and foliation are not established here.
R023.source_name: Yannis Angelopoulos, Christoph Kehle and Ryan Unger, “Nonlinear stability of extremal Reissner-Nordström black holes in spherical symmetry”, arXiv:2410.16234 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16234

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

R023.title: Extension of the moduli-space conjectures to slowly rotating extremal Kerr–Newman black holes
R023.statement: Consider very slowly rotating extremal Kerr–Newman black holes, with parameters satisfying $M^2=e^2+a^2$ and $|a|\ll M$, in the setting without spherical symmetry. Let the regularity conjecture and the extremality-as-critical-phenomenon conjecture be interpreted in this nonsymmetric setting. **Kerr–Newman extension conjecture.** The regularity and local-moduli-space conjectures hold, suitably interpreted, in a neighborhood of very slowly rotating extremal Kerr–Newman, without symmetry. This proposes that the local separating-hypersurface and critical-threshold picture persists beyond spherical symmetry for very slowly rotating extremal Kerr–Newman black holes.
R023.source_name: Yannis Angelopoulos, Christoph Kehle and Ryan Unger, “Nonlinear stability of extremal Reissner-Nordström black holes in spherical symmetry”, arXiv:2410.16234 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16234

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

R023.title: Regularity of finitary semi-upho posets
R023.statement:
A semi-upho poset is a poset satisfying the corresponding principal-filter self-similarity condition for semi-upho posets; it is **finitary** when its relevant rank layers are finite. A semi-upho poset is **regular** if it lies in the image of the forgetful map from finitary colored semi-upho posets.

**Regularity conjecture.** Every finitary semi-upho poset is regular.

This is the semi-upho counterpart of the monoid-representation problem for upho posets. The source states that even the finite-type graded cases remain open.
R023.source_name: Ziyao Fu, Yulin Peng and Yuchong Zhang, “The monoid representation of upho posets and total positivity”, arXiv:2411.04123 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04123

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “As far as we know, even the finite type $\mathbb{N}$-graded cases of these conjectures remain open, and proving them would represent significant progress in the study of upho posets.”

R023.title: Maximum sigma_t-irregularity conjecture for connected triangle-free graphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. Write $sigma_t(G)$ for its $sigma_t$-irregularity. Among such graphs, the extremal complete bipartite graphs are conjectured to have maximum $sigma_t(G)$.

**Triangle-free extremal conjecture.** Among connected triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the extremal complete bipartite graphs have the maximum $sigma_t(G)$-irregularity.

The paper proves the corresponding extremal result among complete bipartite graphs and proposes this conjecture as the extension to all connected triangle-free graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Slobodan Filipovski, Darko Dimitrov, Martin Knor and Riste Škrekovski, “Some results on σ_t-irregularity”, arXiv:2411.04881 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04881

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

R023.title: Quantum regularity inherited from an associated classical model
R023.statement:
Let $(\rho,\sigma(\theta))$ be a quantum model and let $(q(x),p(x\mid\theta))$ be its associated classical model. A quantum model is **quantum regular** when its quantum parameter set has a unique minimizer, the Hessian of the quantum relative entropy at that minimizer is positive definite, and the minimizer has an open neighborhood in the parameter space. The associated classical model is called regular when it satisfies the corresponding classical regularity conditions.

**Quantum regularity conjecture.** If $(q(x),p(x\mid\theta))$ is regular, then $(\rho,\sigma(\theta))$ is also quantum regular.

This conjecture proposes that introducing measurements and passing to the associated classical model cannot make a regular quantum model singular. Its resolution is not established in the supplied source.
R023.source_name: Hiroshi Yano, Yota Maeda and Naoki Yamamoto, “Statistical inference for quantum singular models”, arXiv:2411.16396 (2024).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.16396

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

R023.title: Partition regularity conjecture for generalized Pythagorean pairs
R023.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$ be non-zero, and consider the homogeneous quadratic equation

$$
ax^2+by^2=cz^2.
$$

An equation is **partition regular with respect to $x,y$** if every finite coloring admits a solution in which $x$ and $y$ have the same color. A non-zero integer is a square if it is the square of an integer.

**Generalized Pythagorean-pair conjecture.** If at least one of $ac$, $bc$, or $(a+b)c$ is a square, then $ax^2+by^2=cz^2$ is partition regular with respect to $x,y$.

This is presented as a variant of the main Rado triple conjecture covering partition regularity of pairs. The source does not report a resolution, so the assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: Nikos Frantzikinakis, “Partition regularity of homogeneous quadratics: Current trends and challenges”, arXiv:2411.17523 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17523

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “In this section we present some open questions linked to the topics already discussed.”

R023.title: Local Irregularity Conjecture for 2-multigraphs
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, and let $^2G$ denote the 2-multigraph obtained by doubling every edge of $G$. Let $\operatorname{lir}(H)$ be the smallest number of colors in a locally irregular edge coloring of a multigraph $H$.

**Local Irregularity Conjecture for 2-multigraphs.** For every connected graph $G$ which is not isomorphic to $K_2$,

$$
\operatorname{lir}(^2G)\leq 2.
$$

The conjecture was proposed by Grzelec and Woźniak. The paper proves it for regular 2-multigraphs; its status in the generality stated here is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “On Local Irregularity Conjecture for 2-multigraphs”, arXiv:2412.04200 (2024).
R023.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2405.13893](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13893), [arXiv:2211.08270](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.08270).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04200

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for the Real global group law
R023.statement:
Let $\mathbf{R}$ denote the Real global group law constructed from the Real globally oriented spectrum $\mathbf{MR}$. For each torus $\mathbb{T}^n$, let $\Phi^{\mathbb{T}^n}\mathbf{R}$ denote its geometric-fixed-point target, and let $\mathbf{R}(\mathbb{T}^n)$ be the corresponding value of the global group law. **Regularity Conjecture.** The global group law $\mathbf{R}$ is regular in the sense of Hausmann's Definition 5.9. In particular, the maps

$$
\mathbf{R}(\mathbb{T}^n)\longrightarrow\Phi^{\mathbb{T}^n}\mathbf{R}
$$

are injective. Regularity is proposed as an alternative conjectural assumption for proving injectivity of the restriction maps for augmented tori. The source does not establish it, so its status remains open.
R023.source_name: Jack Carlisle, Noah Wisdom and Guoqi Yan, “Real Global Group Laws and Hu-Kriz Maps”, arXiv:2501.05469 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05469

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

R023.title: Brue–Pigati–Semola local biHölder regularity conjecture for RCD spaces
R023.statement:
Let $(X,\mathsf{d},\mathscr{H}^3)$ be an $\operatorname{RCD}(-2,3)$ space such that every blow-up is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$.

**Brue–Pigati–Semola conjecture.** $(X,\mathsf{d})$ is locally biHölder homeomorphic to a smooth, complete Riemannian manifold $(M^3,g)$.

The conjecture asks whether the topological manifold recognition result can be improved to give a more regular homeomorphism. Its status is not specified in the source.
R023.source_name: Daniele Semola, “The large scale structure of complete 4-manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth”, arXiv:2501.07125 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07125

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

R023.title: The Chang-model cardinal-regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $V$ be a hod mouse and let $\lambda$ be a Woodin limit of Woodin cardinals. Let $g\subseteq\operatorname{Coll}(\omega,<\lambda)$ be $V$-generic, and let $(j,M)$ be as in the cited Chang-model theorem. Set $\nu=j(\lambda)$ and $N=j(V_\lambda)$.

**Cardinal-regularity conjecture.** Then

$$
L_\nu(N^\omega,\Gamma_g,\mathbb{R}_g)\vDash\mathsf{ZF},
$$

and

$$
L_\nu(N^\omega,\Gamma_g,\mathbb{R}_g)\vDash “\text{for every cardinal }\eta\geq\Theta,\\ \eta^+\text{ is a regular cardinal}”.
$$

The conjecture concerns the structure above $\Theta$ in a determinacy model arising from a hod mouse. The paper presents this as an important question; its general validity remains open.
R023.source_name: Douglas Blue, Paul B. Larson and Grigor Sargsyan, “Nairian Models”, arXiv:2501.18958 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18958

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “Developing the first order theory of the models of ${\sf{AD^+}}$ that have the form $L(M^\omega, \Gamma_g, \bR_g)$ is one of the most important open problems of the area.”

R023.title: Semiregularity conjecture for twisted coherent sheaves
R023.statement: Let $\pi:{{{{{{{{\mathcal M}}}}}}}}\rightarrow S$ be a deformation of a smooth complex projective variety $M_0$ over a smooth germ $(S,0)$, and write $M_s=\pi^{-1}(s)$. Let ${{{{{{{{\mathcal B}}}}}}}}$ be a semiregular rank-$r$ coherent sheaf on $M_0$, twisted by a cocycle with coefficients in $\mu_r$. Assume that, for every $p$, the class $ch_p({{{{{{{{\mathcal B}}}}}}}})$ extends to a horizontal section of $R^{2p}\pi_*\mathbb Q$ lying in the direct summand $R^p\pi_*\Omega^p_\pi$ under the Hodge decomposition. **Semiregularity conjecture.** The sheaf ${{{{{{{{\mathcal B}}}}}}}}$ extends to a twisted coherent sheaf over $\pi^{-1}(U)$ for some open analytic neighborhood $U$ of $0$ in $S$. This is a twisted-sheaf analogue of a semiregularity theorem; the source says that it should follow from existing work, so the status of this formulation is left open here.
R023.source_name: Eyal Markman, “Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds”, arXiv:2502.03415 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03415

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

R023.title: The corrected Local Irregularity Conjecture excluding the bow-tie graph
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected locally irregular colorable graph, let $B$ be the bow-tie graph, and let $\mathrm{lir}(G)$ denote the minimum number of locally irregular subgraphs whose edge-disjoint union is $G$. A graph is locally irregular if adjacent vertices have different degrees. **Corrected Local Irregularity Conjecture.** If $G\neq B$, then

$$
\mathrm{lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$

The bow-tie graph is the unique counterexample to the original conjecture among colorable cacti, with locally irregular chromatic index four. The corrected statement is presented as the strengthened form motivated by that counterexample; its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “Weak and strong local irregularity of digraphs”, arXiv:2502.07933 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07933

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2025). “During their research, a single counterexample to the Local Irregularity Conjecture was found in .”

R023.title: Two-color conjecture for weak local irregularity of digraphs
R023.statement:
For a digraph $D$, two adjacent vertices are weakly distinguished when their outdegree–indegree pairs differ. Let $\mathrm{lir}(D)$ be the minimum number of colors in an arc coloring such that every color class induces a digraph in which every arc has endpoints with different outdegree–indegree pairs. **Weak local irregularity conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{lir}(D)\leq 2.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the weakening from distinguishing outdegrees or indegrees separately to distinguishing ordered pairs always permits a two-color decomposition. The paper states that it is supported by several results but supplies no resolution.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “Weak and strong local irregularity of digraphs”, arXiv:2502.07933 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07933

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2025). “During their research, a single counterexample to the Local Irregularity Conjecture was found in .”

R023.title: Two-color conjecture for strong local irregularity of digraphs
R023.statement:
For a digraph $D$, define the balanced degree of a vertex $x$ by

$$
\sigma(x)=d^+(x)-d^-(x).
$$

A digraph is strongly locally irregular if $\sigma(x)\neq\sigma(y)$ for every arc $xy$, and let $\mathrm{slir}(D)$ be the minimum number of colors in an arc coloring whose color classes induce strongly locally irregular digraphs. **Strong local irregularity conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{slir}(D)\leq 2.
$$

The source notes that strong local irregularity is not directly controlled by the corresponding notion for orientations of simple graphs and presents the statement as an open conjecture supported by the paper’s investigation.
R023.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “Weak and strong local irregularity of digraphs”, arXiv:2502.07933 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07933

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2025). “During their research, a single counterexample to the Local Irregularity Conjecture was found in .”

R023.title: The high-order contact conjecture for stationary varifolds
R023.statement:
Let $V$ and $x_0$ satisfy the assumptions of the flat tangent-cone regularity conjecture. The **high-order contact conjecture.** There is a smooth classical minimal $m$-dimensional graph $\mathcal{M}$ in some neighborhood of $x_0$ such that

$$
\int_{\mathbf{B}_r(x_0)}\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal{M})^2\,d\|V\|(x)=o(r^N)\qquad\text{for every }N\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a possible route from flat tangent-cone regularity to a unique-continuation problem; the paper does not report a resolution.
R023.source_name: Camillo Brena, Stefano Decio and Camillo De Lellis, “Remarks and Conjectures on Stationary Varifolds”, arXiv:2503.00651 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00651

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

R023.title: The $C^{p'}$-regularity conjecture for elliptic $p$-Laplace equations
R023.statement:
Let $p\in(2,\infty)$, let $B_1$ be the unit ball, and let $\Delta_p u\coloneqq\operatorname{div}(|Du|^{p-2}Du)$. A function is locally of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ if it has locally Hölder-continuous first derivatives with exponent $\alpha$. **$C^{p'}$-regularity conjecture.** Every solution $u$ of

$$
-\Delta_p u=f\in L^{\infty}(B_1)
$$

is locally of class $C^{1,\frac{1}{p-1}}=C^{p'}$, where $p'=\frac{p}{p-1}$. This is a well-known open problem concerning optimal regularity in the elliptic setting; the paper studies related optimal regularity for parabolic $p$-Laplace equations.
R023.source_name: Se-Chan Lee, Yuanyuan Lian, Hyungsung Yun and Kai Zhang, “Time derivative estimates for parabolic p-Laplace equations and applications to optimal regularity”, arXiv:2503.04384 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04384

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “This observation gives rise to the following well-known open problem related to the optimal regularity in the elliptic setting, namely $C^{p'}$-regularity conjecture:”

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for imaginary coweights
R023.statement:
Let $\check{\eta}$ be an indecomposable imaginary coweight, let $M(\check{\eta})$ be the associated representation, and let $\gamma_s(\check{\eta})$ denote its Schur rank. The coweight is **regular** when

$$
\hom(\delta,M(\check{\eta}))=\hom(\delta,\gamma_s(\check{\eta})B)
$$

for every $\delta$. **Regularity conjecture.** All imaginary coweights and weights are regular. The paper proves the conjecture for a large class of imaginary weights, but leaves the general assertion open.
R023.source_name: Jiarui Fei, “Schur Rank, Compatibility Degree, and Canonical Decomposition”, arXiv:2503.12700 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12700

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “Despite of some effort in and , this conjecture remains open.”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for antiunitary representations of simply connected Lie groups
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a simply connected Lie group, let $\tau_h$ be the involution associated with an Euler element $h\in\mathfrak g$, and let $(U,\mathcal H)$ be an antiunitary representation of $G_{\tau_h}$. Write ${\tt V}(h,U)$ for the associated standard subspace. The representation is **$h$-regular** when there exists an $e$-neighborhood $N\subeq G$ such that

$$
{\tt V}_N:=\bigcap_{g\in N}U(g){\tt V}(h,U)
$$

is cyclic. **Regularity conjecture.** If $G$ is simply connected and $h\in\mathfrak g$ is an Euler element, then every antiunitary representation of $G_{\tau_h}$ is $h$-regular. This conjecture asks for universal regularity of the standard subspaces arising from antiunitary representations; the paper presents it as an open problem, while earlier results establish regularity in particular settings.
R023.source_name: Daniel Beltita and Karl-Hermann Neeb, “Crowned Lie groups and nets of real subspaces”, arXiv:2506.16422 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16422

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2025). “An interesting open problem in the context of this paper is the regularity conjecture:”

R023.title: Local Hölder regularity conjecture for homogeneous fractional p-Laplace systems
R023.statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\Omega$ be a bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For $s\in(0,1)$ and $p\in(1,\infty)$, let $u\in W^{s,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^N)$ satisfy

$$
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^{p-2}(u(x)-u(y))(\varphi(x)-\varphi(y))}{|x-y|^{n+sp}}\,dx\,dy=0\qquad\forall\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^N).
$$

**Local Hölder regularity conjecture.** Then $u$ is locally Hölder continuous in $\Omega$.

This is the regularity statement for homogeneous fractional $p$-Laplace systems needed to remove the paper's restriction that $sp$ lie sufficiently close to $n$. It is presented as an unknown result and is used as the missing ingredient in a blow-up argument for regularity of minimizing fractional harmonic maps.
R023.source_name: Akshara Vincent, “Hölder continuity of Minimizing W^s,p-Harmonic Maps”, arXiv:2506.16442 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16442

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

R023.title: Schröer's klt type and strong F-regularity conjecture
R023.statement: Let $R=\left(\mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]/(f_1, \dots, f_r)\right)_{(X_1, \dots, X_n)}$, where each $f_i\in\mathbb{Z}[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, and let $R\bmod p$ denote its reduction modulo the prime $p$. **Schröer's conjecture.** $\operatorname{Spec} R$ is of klt type if and only if $R\bmod p$ is strongly $F$-regular for all but finitely many $p$. The only-if direction is known, and the if direction is known when $R$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein or its anti-canonical ring is Noetherian; the general case remains open even in dimension three.
R023.source_name: Shunsuke Takagi and Tatsuki Yamaguchi, “On the uniform positivity of F-signature under reduction modulo p”, arXiv:2507.16566 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16566

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

R023.title: Stable Allen–Cahn level-set curvature conjecture in dimensions at most seven
R023.statement:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain, and let $u_{\varepsilon_j}$ be stable solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation in $\Omega$, where $\varepsilon_j \downarrow 0$. Assume that the sequence has uniformly bounded energy. The interfacial regions are $\{ -0.9 < u_{\varepsilon_j} < 0.9 \}$.

**Stable Allen–Cahn regularity conjecture.** If $n \leq 7$, then the curvatures of the level sets of $u_{\varepsilon_j}$ in these interfacial regions are uniformly bounded along the sequence on compact subdomains of $\Omega$.

A positive answer would give smooth, possibly multiplicity-bearing convergence of stable Allen–Cahn solutions to minimal hypersurfaces in the singular limit. The conjecture is presented as a fundamental regularity question and its resolution is linked to multiplicity-one and Morse-index questions for Allen–Cahn approximations.
R023.source_name: Enric Florit-Simon and Joaquim Serra, “On stable solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation with bounded energy density in R^4”, arXiv:2509.02739 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02739

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

R023.title: Net graph asymptotic regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $N$ be the net graph. Its binomial edge ideal is denoted by $J_N$, and write $\widehat{\operatorname{reg}}(J_N)$ for its asymptotic regularity. **Net graph asymptotic regularity conjecture.**

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{reg}}(J_N)=3.
$$

The paper presents this as an example expected to have asymptotic regularity different from two, in contrast with the preceding results for the considered classes of graphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Dennis Belotserkovskiy, Mariana Landín, Charlie Ruppe and Lizzy Teryoshin, “Asymptotic invariants of symbolic powers of binomial edge ideals”, arXiv:2510.14272 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14272

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

R023.title: Asymptotic regularity conjecture for initial ideals of binomial edge ideals
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be an enumerated graph. Let $\ell$ be the length of the longest induced path in $G$, and let $\ell_{<}$ be the length of the longest admissible path in $G$. Write $\operatorname{gin}(J_G)$ for the generic initial ideal of the binomial edge ideal $J_G$, and $\operatorname{in}_{<}(J_G)$ for its initial ideal with respect to the indicated enumeration-dependent order. **Asymptotic regularity conjecture.**

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{reg}}(\operatorname{gin}(J_G))=\ell,
$$

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{reg}}(\operatorname{in}_{<}(J_G))=\ell_{<}.
$$

These equalities are motivated by lower bounds from induced and admissible paths. The authors state that they are not aware of any graph for which equality fails, but the conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Dennis Belotserkovskiy, Mariana Landín, Charlie Ruppe and Lizzy Teryoshin, “Asymptotic invariants of symbolic powers of binomial edge ideals”, arXiv:2510.14272 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14272

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for antiunitary representations
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a Lie group with Lie algebra ${\mathfrak g}$, let $h\in{\mathfrak g}$ be an Euler element, and let $G_{\tau_h}$ denote the subgroup associated with the involution determined by $h$. An antiunitary representation is a representation $(U,\mathcal{H})$ of $G_{\tau_h}$ by unitary and antiunitary operators on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. **Regularity conjecture.** Any antiunitary representation $(U,\mathcal{H})$ of $G_{\tau_h}$ is $h$-regular, meaning that there exists an open $e$-neighborhood $N\subseteq G$ such that

$$
{\tt V}_N=\bigcap_{g\in N}U(g){\tt V}
$$

is cyclic. This conjecture asks whether the regularity required in the Euler Element Theorem holds for all antiunitary representations of $G_{\tau_h}$ without additional structural assumptions on $G$. It is described in the source as a challenging open problem; the cited cases include the $4$-dimensional split oscillator group.
R023.source_name: Karl-Hermann Neeb, “Nets of real subspaces on homogeneous spaces and Algebraic Quantum Field Theory”, arXiv:2511.09360 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.09360

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

R023.title: Higher-time regularity conjecture for the Augmented formula
R023.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $T_{\varepsilon,\kappa,R}$ denote the time scale introduced for the Augmented formula. The solution takes values in the product of the Sobolev space $\mathbb{H}^1$ and $\mathbb{R}^4$. **Higher-time regularity conjecture.** For any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the Augmented formula is well-posed in

$$
\mathscr{C}^k\left([0,cT_{\varepsilon,\kappa,R}),\mathbb{H}^1\times\mathbb{R}^4\right).
$$

The claim is motivated by applying $\partial_t^k$ to the Augmented formula and seeking to use the same semilinear scheme. The supplied passage gives no result establishing or refuting this conjecture.
R023.source_name: Geoffrey Beck, Ewan Contentin and Ludovic Martaud, “Freely floating cylinder on a 3D fluid governed by the Boussinesq equations in the axisymmetric without swirl case”, arXiv:2601.03133 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03133

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

R023.title: Higher-spatial-regularity conjecture for the Augmented formula
R023.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$ with $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\mathbb{H}^n_\kappa$ be the two-dimensional vectorial field equipped with the weighted norm specified below. For even $n$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert u\rVert_{\mathbb{H}^{n}}^2:= {}&\lVert u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert\partial_r u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert {\rm d}_r\partial_r u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\cdots+\lVert(\partial_r{\rm d}_r)^{n/2}u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2\\
&+\lVert u_2\rVert_{L^2}^2+\lVert{\rm d}_r u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert\partial_r{\rm d}_r u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\cdots+\lVert({\rm d}_r\partial_r)^{n/2}u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\kappa^2\lVert({\rm d}_r\partial_r)^{n/2}{\rm d}_r u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

For odd $n$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert u\rVert_{\mathbb{H}^{n}}^2:= {}&\lVert u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert\partial_r u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert {\rm d}_r\partial_r u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\cdots+\lVert({\rm d}_r\partial_r)^{(n-1)/2}{\rm d}_r u_1\rVert_{L^2_r}^2\\
&+\lVert u_2\rVert_{L^2}^2+\lVert{\rm d}_r u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\lVert\partial_r{\rm d}_r u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\cdots+\lVert{\rm d}_r(\partial_r{\rm d}_r)^{(n-1)/2}u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2+\kappa^2\lVert(\partial_r{\rm d}_r)^{(n+1)/2}u_2\rVert_{L^2_r}^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Higher-spatial-regularity conjecture.** The Augmented formula is well-posed in $\mathscr{C}^k\left([0,T),\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}^4\right)$, with the corresponding weighted norm above according to the parity of $n$. The conjecture is motivated by applying the indicated alternating radial differential operators to the Augmented formula. The supplied passage gives no result establishing or refuting this higher-regularity claim.
R023.source_name: Geoffrey Beck, Ewan Contentin and Ludovic Martaud, “Freely floating cylinder on a 3D fluid governed by the Boussinesq equations in the axisymmetric without swirl case”, arXiv:2601.03133 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03133

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

R023.title: Conjectured conormal regularity for Type I singularity formation
R023.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}=(\{v\leq 0\}\cup \{t\leq -0.9\})\cap\{-1\leq u<0\}$, and let $\phi$ be a solution arising from smooth initial data in the stated Type I self-similar stability results, with singularity formation renormalised to $t=0$. Write $\phi_0$ for the corresponding self-similar solution, $\mathcal{C}$ for the backward light cone, and let $\{u\partial_u,x_i\partial_{x_j}-x_j\partial_{x_i},r\partial_t,1\}^\alpha$ denote products of the listed vector fields of order $|\alpha|$. **Type I regularity conjecture.** There exists $\epsilon>0$, depending on the equation, such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $0\leq|\alpha|\leq k$, the following estimates hold on $\mathcal{C}$:

$$
\left|\{u\partial_u,x_i\partial_{x_j}-x_j\partial_{x_i},r\partial_t,1\}^\alpha(\phi-\phi_0)\right|\lesssim_{|\alpha|}r^\epsilon
$$

for the wave-map equation with $d\geq3$, and

$$
\left|\{u\partial_u,x_i\partial_{x_j}-x_j\partial_{x_i},r\partial_t,1\}^\alpha(\phi-\phi_0)\right|\lesssim_{|\alpha|}r^{\epsilon-1}
$$

for the equation with $d=7$ and $p=3$. These estimates assert the additional conormal and $r\partial_t$ regularity needed for the exterior stability argument. The conjecture concerns precise quantitative control not supplied by the preceding stability theorem, and its resolution is not indicated here.
R023.source_name: Istvan Kadar and Lionor Kehrberger, “A note on exterior stability of isolated singularity formation for nonlinear wave equations”, arXiv:2602.03963 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03963

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the CW-complex of tilted Richardson cells
R023.statement:
For $u,v\in S_n$, let $\mathcal{T}_{u,v}^{\geq0}$ be stratified by the positive tilted Richardson cells as

$$
\mathcal{T}_{u,v}^{\geq0}=\bigsqcup_{[x,y]\subseteq[u,v]}\mathcal{T}_{x,y}^{>0}.
$$

The source proves that this stratification forms a CW-complex.

**Regularity conjecture for tilted Richardson cells.** The CW-complex in the preceding stratification is regular.

Regularity would strengthen the established CW-complex structure and, together with the closure conjecture, would clarify the topology and face-poset structure of the nonnegative tilted Richardson variety. The source does not state that this conjecture is resolved.
R023.source_name: Jiyang Gao, Shiliang Gao and Yibo Gao, “Tilted Richardson Varieties”, arXiv:2602.05326 (2026).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0609764](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609764).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05326

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2026).

R023.title: The super-strong conjecture on F-irregular graphs
R023.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 3$ be an integer. A graph $G$ is **$n$-hyper-irregular** if it is $F$-irregular for every graph $F$, not necessarily connected, with order $|F|\leqslant n$ and size $|E(F)|\geqslant 2$.

**Super-strong conjecture on $F$-irregular graphs.** For each integer $n\geqslant 3$, there exist infinitely many $n$-hyper-irregular graphs.

This is presented as a conjectural strengthening of the preceding $F$-irregularity conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution or partial result for this super-strong version.
R023.source_name: Tatiana Dovzhenok, “Proof of the strong conjecture about F-irregular graphs in the class of graphs \F\ of diameter 2”, arXiv:2602.23227 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23227

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

R023.title: Sedlar–Škrekovski local irregularity conjecture for colorable graphs
R023.statement:
Let $B$ be the bow-tie cactus with $\mathrm{lir}(B)=4$. For a connected graph $G$ that is locally irregular colorable, let $\mathrm{lir}(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a locally irregular coloring. **Local Irregularity Conjecture.** Every connected graph $G\neq B$ that is locally irregular colorable satisfies 
$$
\mathrm{lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$
 The conjecture is presented as an improvement of the earlier universal bound after $B$ was found; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it remains open.
R023.source_name: Anna Flaszczyńska, Aleksandra Gorzkowska, Igor Grzelec, Alfréd Onderko and Mariusz Woźniak, “Locally Irregular Total Colorings of Graphs”, arXiv:2603.13178 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13178

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

R023.title: Boundary regularity conjecture for Hawkes-process resolvent functions
R023.statement:
Let $A>0$, let $\beta>1$, and suppose that the functions $\boldsymbol{h}^0$ belong to $C^\beta([0,A])$. For $(l,j,k)\in[K]^3$, $r\in\{1,\ldots,\lfloor\beta\rfloor\}$, $i\in\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and $c\geq 0$, define

$$
p^{[2]}_{r,k}(x,s,l,j):=\mathbb{E}^{(x,s,l,j)}_0\left[\frac{1}{\lambda_A^k(f_k^0)^r}\right],
$$

and

$$
p^{![2]}_{r,i,c,k}(x,s,l,j):=\mathbb{E}^{(x,s,l,j)}_0\left[\frac{1}{\lambda_A^k(f_k^0,!(s,j))^{r-i}\bigl(\lambda_A^k(f_k^0,!(s,j))+c\bigr)^{i+1}}\right].
$$

Here $\|\cdot\|_{C^\beta}$ denotes the usual Hölder norm on $[0,A]$.

**Boundary regularity conjecture.** For every $x\in[0,A]$, there exists a version of $s\mapsto p^{![2]}_{r,i,c,k}(x,s,l,j)$ that is continuous at $0$ and at $A$. Moreover, there exist versions of $x\mapsto p^{![2]}_{r,i,c,k}(x,A,l,j)$ and $x\mapsto p^{![2]}_{r,i,c,k}(x,0,l,j)$ belonging to $C^\beta([0,A])$, and

$$
\int_0^A\left\|p^{[2]}_{r,k}(\cdot,s,l,j)\right\|_{C^\beta}\,ds<+\infty.
$$

These regularity properties are conjectured uniformly over the displayed choices of indices and parameter $c$; they provide the boundary and Hölder regularity needed for semiparametric analysis of multivariate Hawkes processes. The source does not give evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.
R023.source_name: Mael Duverger and Judith Rousseau, “The Bernstein-von Mises theorem and efficiency for semiparametric inference in multivariate Hawkes processes”, arXiv:2603.23655 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

R023.title: The N-regularity conjecture for mutable lattices
R023.statement:
Let $L$ be a mutable lattice, and let $\operatorname{Hasse}(L)$ denote its Hasse diagram. Consider the underlying undirected graph of this diagram, and let $N$ be a constant.

**N-regularity conjecture.** Every vertex of the underlying undirected graph of $\operatorname{Hasse}(L)$ has degree $N$; equivalently, the graph is $N$-regular.

The paper states that the converse is false, so $N$-regularity does not characterize mutable lattices. The conjecture itself is not resolved in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Kan Nagano, “Flip of lattices”, arXiv:2605.09601 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09601

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026).

R023.title: Bounded-type regularity conjecture for Siegel-disk boundaries
R023.statement:
Let $b1$ be a rotation number of bounded type, let $r_{b1}$ be the radius of convergence of the Siegel-disk parametrization, and define

$$
\Gamma_{b1}(\theta)=\Gamma(r_{b1}e^{i\theta}).
$$

**Bounded-type regularity conjecture.** If $b1$ is of bounded type, then the map $\Gamma_{b1}$ is at least $C^1$.

This conjecture would imply that the boundary parametrization is an embedding and hence a conjugacy for the boundary dynamics. The source provides no resolution status.
R023.source_name: F. M. Tangerman, “Boundaries of Siegel Disks for Conservative Systems”, arXiv:2605.20953 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20953

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

R023.title: Bounded-type nonsmoothness conjecture for Siegel-disk boundaries
R023.statement:
Let $b1$ be a rotation number of bounded type, and let $\Gamma_{b1}(\theta)$ denote the parametrization of the boundary of the corresponding Siegel disk. **Bounded-type nonsmoothness conjecture.** There exists a real number $p$ with $1<p<3$ such that $\Gamma_{b1}$ is not of class $C^p$.

The claim refines the preceding $C^1$ regularity conjecture by predicting limited smoothness of the boundary. The source reports numerical evidence and mentions an estimate around $1.7$ for the last noble invariant circle, but gives no proof.
R023.source_name: F. M. Tangerman, “Boundaries of Siegel Disks for Conservative Systems”, arXiv:2605.20953 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20953

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

R023.title: The $C^{1,b1}$-rectifiability conjecture for the singular set
R023.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be the singular set of the anisotropic obstacle problem, and let $A$ be the coefficient matrix with ellipticity constants. **$C^{1,\alpha}$-rectifiability conjecture.** The singular set $\Sigma$ is $(n-1)$-rectifiable of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ for some $\alpha > 0$ depending only on $n$ and the ellipticity constants of $A$. This strengthens the preceding rectifiability result by asserting uniform $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity of the singular set; the stated context notes that the qualitative structure is stable under small perturbations of the anisotropy, while the limiting behavior for degenerate anisotropies remains open.
R023.source_name: Ezequiel Barbosa, Rosivaldo Antonio Gonçalves and Luan de Figueiredo, “Anisotropic Obstacle Problems for Minimal Surfaces: Regularity of the Free Boundary via the Cahn-Hoffman Transform”, arXiv:2606.29046 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29046

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

R023.title: Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness's unrestricted regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite almost simple group with socle $G_0$, and let a non-standard subgroup mean a subgroup whose associated primitive action is non-standard in the sense defined in the source. **Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness's conjecture.** Every $7$-tuple of non-standard subgroups of $G$ is regular.

This conjecture asks whether the conjugacy condition in Cameron's solved formulation can be removed, and is presented as a conjecture from Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness (2024).
R023.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Lei Wang, “On the regularity of irreducible subgroups of finite classical groups”, arXiv:2607.03307 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03307

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2026). “The precise form of the conjecture was established in later work by Burness et al. , working extensively with a powerful probabilistic approach for bounding the base size of a finite permutation group, which was originally introduced in .”

R023.title: Generalized Pythagorean partition-regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$, and call the equation $ax^2+by^2=cz^2$ **partition regular** when every finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits a solution $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{N}^3$ whose three entries have the same colour.

**Generalized Pythagorean partition-regularity conjecture.** The equation

$$
ax^2+by^2=cz^2
$$

is partition regular if and only if $c\in\{a,b,a+b\}$.

Rado's theorem gives the necessity of the condition $c\in\{a,b,a+b\}$, but its sufficiency remains open. Indeed, it is unknown whether any choice of $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$ makes this equation partition regular. The paper proves a special case when $a,b,c$ are perfect squares and either $a=c$ or $a+b=c$.
R023.source_name: Guilherme Azevedo and Joel Moreira, “Pythagorean triples in level sets of completely multiplicative functions”, arXiv:2607.04903 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04903

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

R023.title: Ergodic Pythagorean recurrence conjecture
R023.statement:
A **multiplicative measure-preserving system** is a probability space $(X,\mu)$ equipped with an action $T=(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of $(\mathbb{N},\times)$ such that every $T_n$ preserves $\mu$. Let $A\subset X$, and suppose that for some $r\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\mu\left(A\cup T_1^{-1}A\cup\cdots\cup T_r^{-1}A\right)=1.
$$

**Ergodic Pythagorean recurrence conjecture.** There exists a solution $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{N}^3$ of $x^2+y^2=z^2$ such that

$$
\mu\left(T_x^{-1}A\cap T_y^{-1}A\cap T_z^{-1}A\right)>0.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent ergodic form of the monochromatic Pythagorean-triples conjecture via Furstenberg's correspondence principle. Since the underlying partition-regularity conjecture remains open, this equivalent formulation is also open.
R023.source_name: Guilherme Azevedo and Joel Moreira, “Pythagorean triples in level sets of completely multiplicative functions”, arXiv:2607.04903 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04903

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

R023.title: White's generic regularity conjecture for area-minimizing cycles
R023.statement: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold and let a homologically area-minimizing cycle in $M$ have a singular set. **White's generic regularity conjecture.** Singularities in a homologically area-minimizing cycle in a Riemannian manifold should disappear after a generic perturbation of the metric. This question concerns whether generic metrics eliminate singularities from area-minimizing representatives when smooth representatives are not excluded by topology. It is known for embedded geodesics and for $2$-dimensional area-minimizing submanifolds of arbitrary codimension, while the general question remains open.
R023.source_name: Zhenhua Liu, “Area-minimizing submanifolds are not generically smooth, except for geodesics, minimal surfaces, and minimal hypersurfaces”, arXiv:2607.24735 (2026).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24735

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

R023.title: Local square-integrability conjecture for first-order differential operators
R023.statement:
Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold, let $E$ be the relevant vector bundle, and let $T:C_0^\infty(E)\to C_0^\infty(E)$ be a first-order differential operator. Assume that $T^2$ is essentially self-adjoint. For $u\in L^2_{\operatorname{loc}}(E)$ satisfying

$$
T^2u\in L^2_{\operatorname{loc}}(E),
$$

the expression $Tu$ is locally square-integrable.

**Local regularity conjecture.** Under these assumptions,

$$
Tu\in L^2_{\operatorname{loc}}(E).
$$

This implication would establish the local integrability condition needed in the essential self-adjointness result for Schrödinger operators of the form $D^tD+V$. The source presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
R023.source_name: Matthias Lesch, “Essential self-adjointness of symmetric linear relations associated to first order systems”, arXiv:math/0005011 (2000).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0005011

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2000).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for tempered solution ind-sheaves
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex manifold, let $\mathcal{D}_X$ denote the sheaf of differential operators on $X$, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a holonomic $\mathcal{D}_X$-module. Write

$$
Sol^t(\mathcal{M})=R\mathcal{I}\operatorname{hom}_{\beta_X\mathcal{D}_X}(\beta_X\mathcal{M},\mathcal{O}_X^t).
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** The module $\mathcal{M}$ is regular holonomic if and only if $Sol^t(\mathcal{M})$ is regular. The text notes that the only-if direction follows from the preceding theorem, leaving the converse as the conjectural part; no resolution is supplied.
R023.source_name: Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, “Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity”, arXiv:math/0108065 (2001).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0108065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2001).

R023.title: Local Sobolev regularity conjecture for Schrödinger operators under Assumption A
R023.statement:
Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold, let $E$ be a Hermitian vector bundle over $M$, and let $V$ be a potential satisfying Assumption A: $V=V_{+}+V_{-}$, with $V_{+}(x)8e0$ and $V_{-}(x)8e0$ as linear operators on each fiber, and for every compact $K\subset M$ there are constants $a_K<1$ and $C_K$ such that

$$
\left(\int_K |V_-|^2|u|^2\,d\mu\right)^{1/2}\leq a_K\|\Delta_Mu\|+C_K\|u\|,
$$

for all $u\in C_c^\infty(M)$. Let $H_{V,\max}$ denote the maximal domain of the associated Schrödinger-type operator. **Local regularity conjecture.** If $V$ satisfies Assumption A, then

$$
\operatorname{Dom}(H_{V,\max})\subset W^{1,2}_{\operatorname{loc}}(E).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the established local regularity theorem under the additional assumption that $D^*D$ has a scalar principal symbol; the authors note that the assertion is nontrivial even when $M=\mathbb{R}^n$.
R023.source_name: Maxim Braverman, Ognjen Milatovic and Mikhail Shubin, “Essential self-adjointness of Schroedinger type operators on manifolds”, arXiv:math/0201231 (2002).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0201231

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2002).

R023.title: Sturmfels's regularity conjecture for unions of subspaces
R023.statement:
Let $I$ be the vanishing ideal of a union of $d$ subspaces.

**Sturmfels's conjecture.** The Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $I$ is at most $d$.

This is a strengthening of the Subspace Conjecture, replacing a generator-degree bound by a bound on Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity. The source states that both conjectures were proven by the authors in the cited work.
R023.source_name: Harm Derksen and Jessica Sidman, “Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity by approximation”, arXiv:math/0211279 (2003).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211279

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2002). “It was proven by the authors in that both conjectures are true.”

R023.title: Weibel's vanishing and regularity conjecture for negative K-theory
R023.statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme of dimension $d$. For a contravariant functor $F$ on schemes, call $X$ **$F$-regular** if, for every $r\geq 0$, the map $F(X)\to F(X\times\mathbb{A}^r)$ is an isomorphism. **Weibel's conjecture.**

$$
K_m(X)=0\quad\text{for }m<-d,
$$

and $X$ is $K_{-d}$-regular. This predicts vanishing of algebraic $K$-theory below the negative of the dimension together with regularity in the boundary degree. It is proved for schemes essentially of finite type over a field of characteristic zero, but remains open in characteristic $p>0$ except for curves and surfaces.
R023.source_name: G. Cortiñas, C. Haesemeyer, M. Schlichting and C. A. Weibel, “Cyclic homology, cdh-cohomology and negative K-theory”, arXiv:math/0502255 (2005).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0502255

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2005). “We remark that this conjecture is still open in characteristic $p>0$, except for curves and surfaces; see .”

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the equivariant asymptotic solution
R023.statement: Let $R_{\sigma\tau}^{(n)}(t,\lambda)$ be the coefficient of $\hbar^n$ in the asymptotic solution matrix $R_{\sigma\tau}(t,\lambda,\hbar)$ of the equivariant quantum differential equation, normalized by the stated classical-limit condition. Let $\lambda=0$ be the non-equivariant limit, and let $t$ be a semisimple point of the non-equivariant theory. **Regularity conjecture for the equivariant asymptotic solution.** If the non-equivariant quantum cohomology is generically semisimple, then $R_{\sigma\tau}^{(n)}(t,\lambda)$ is regular at $\lambda=0$ for such a point $t$. The conjecture is stated after the canonical-coordinate regularity conjecture and is later asserted to hold for toric varieties using the equivariant mirror.
R023.source_name: Hiroshi Iritani, “Convergence of quantum cohomology by quantum Lefschetz”, arXiv:math/0506236 (2006).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506236

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2005). “For a class of Fano toric varieties, the $R$-conjecture was proved by Givental .”

R023.title: Spectrum regularity conjecture for rainbow cycle lengths
R023.statement: Let $S$ be a spectrum of rainbow cycle lengths, namely the set of cycle lengths occurring as rainbow cycles under a fixed edge-coloring. **Spectrum regularity conjecture.** The asymptotic behavior of $S$ should be classified into exactly one of the following three categories: (a) $S$ contains all sufficiently large numbers; (b) $S$ contains all sufficiently large even numbers; or (c) $S$ contains all sufficiently large numbers congruent to $2\bmod 4$. Equivalently, in terms of monoids, the spectrum should become regular modulo one, two, or four.
R023.source_name: Boris Alexeev, “On lengths of rainbow cycles”, arXiv:math/0507456 (2006).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0507456

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2005).

R023.title: Stone-regularity conjecture for boundary-value problems with polynomial resolvent growth
R023.statement: Let a boundary-value problem be subject to the estimate referenced in the source as $$, with smooth coefficients $p_k$. A boundary-value problem is **Stone-regular** when it has the corresponding Stone-regularity property. **Stone-regularity conjecture.** Every such boundary-value problem is Stone-regular. Moreover, this assertion should also hold for general boundary conditions $$.
