The conjecture proposes a general regularity consequence of polynomial resolvent growth, extending the expected conclusion from smooth-coefficient problems to general boundary conditions; the source does not state a resolution.
R023.source_name: Arkadi Minkin, “Equiconvergence theorems for differential operators”, arXiv:math/0602406 (2006).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602406

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2006).

R023.title: The strict inequality conjecture for primitive detection degrees
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $e(G)$ be the degree associated with the top primitives, and let $e^{\prime}(G)$ be the largest degree $d$ for which $Q_A Cess^d(G)$ is nonzero when $Cess^*(G)$ is nonzero; if $Cess^*(G)=\mathbf 0$, set $e^{\prime}(G)=-1$.

**Strict inequality conjecture.** If $G$ is not $p$-central, then

$$
e^{\prime}(G)<e(G).
$$

This conjecture compares the primitive detection degree with the top primitive degree. The source proves it when $r-c=1$ and explains that the Strong Regularity Conjecture implies it for a fixed finite group; Benson's conjecture is known when $r-c\leq 2$, but the general status remains open.
R023.source_name: Nicholas J. Kuhn, “Primitives and central detection numbers in group cohomology”, arXiv:math/0612133 (2007).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612133

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2006).

R023.title: Abstract Birkhoff-regularity conjecture for completely continuous operators
R023.statement:
Let $G$ be an abstract completely continuous operator, let $Lambda:=\left\{\lambda_j\right\}$ be the set of its eigenvalues, and fix $delta>0$. For each $lambda$, define the circle

$$
K_\lambda:=\left\{\left|z-\lambda\right|\leq\delta\cdot\left(1+\left|\operatorname{Im}\lambda\right|\right)\right\}.
$$

Let $T_\varepsilon^\pm$ be the sectors referred to in the paper. **Abstract Birkhoff-regularity conjecture.** Existence of an invertible limit of the characteristic function of $G$ in the sectors $T_\varepsilon^\pm$, away from the circles $K_{\lambda_j}$ and $K_{\overline{\lambda_j}}$ for $lambda_j\in\Lambda$, is a correct reformulation of the Birkhoff-regularity condition and yields unconditional basicity of the eigenvectors of $G$, perhaps with brackets. This proposed abstract reformulation is intended to connect characteristic-function asymptotics with Birkhoff regularity and spectral decompositions. The source presents it as a supposition and does not provide a proof or a resolution.
R023.source_name: A. Minkin, “Regularity of dissipative operators”, arXiv:math/9909092 (2010).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9909092

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 1999).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the free boundary in dimension two
R023.statement: Let $D$ be an optimal configuration in a planar domain, and let $\partial D$ denote its free boundary. **Two-dimensional free-boundary regularity conjecture.** In dimension two, the free boundary $\partial D$ is smooth outside a finite set. The authors prove restrictions on the singular set, while the stated smoothness assertion remains open.
R023.source_name: S. Chanillo, D. Grieser, M. Imai, K. Kurata and I. Ohnishi, “Symmetry breaking and other phenomena in the optimization of eigenvalues for composite membranes”, arXiv:math/9912116 (2000).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9912116

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 1999).

R023.title: Strict pairwise regularity conjecture for critical-circle conjugacies
R023.statement:
Let $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ be critical invariant circles in the same universality class, and let $h_{\gamma_i}$ be their conjugacies to the reference dynamics. Write $H_{\gamma_1,\gamma_2}=h_{\gamma_1}\circ h_{\gamma_2}^{-1}$, and let $\kappa(\cdot)$ denote Hölder regularity. **Strict pairwise regularity conjecture.** For $i=1,2$, 
$$
\kappa(h_{\gamma_i})<\kappa(H_{\gamma_1,\gamma_2}),\qquad \kappa(h_{\gamma_i}^{-1})<\kappa(H_{\gamma_1,\gamma_2}).
$$
 The conjecture predicts cancellation of singularities for critical circles in the same universality class, improving on the general composition lower bound; it is presented as an expectation and remains unproved in the source.
R023.source_name: Arturo Olvera and Nikola P. Petrov, “Regularity properties of critical invariant circles of twist maps, and their universality”, arXiv:nlin/0609024 (2006).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/nlin/0609024

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

R023.title: Matrix Stahl–Totik regularity conjecture for matrix-valued measures
R023.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite union of disjoint closed intervals in ${\mathbb{R}}$. Suppose $\mu$ is an $l\times l$ matrix-valued measure on ${\mathbb{R}}$ with

$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(d\mu)=E.
$$

For each $\eta>0$ and $m=1,2,\dots$, define

$$
S_{m,\eta}=\left\{x\colon \mu\left([x-\tfrac{1}{m},x+\tfrac{1}{m}]\right)\geq e^{-\eta m}{\boldsymbol{1}}\right\}.
$$

Suppose that for each $\eta$, with $|\cdot|$ denoting Lebesgue measure,

$$
\lim_{m\to\infty}|E\setminus S_{m,\eta}|=0.
$$

**Matrix Stahl–Totik conjecture.** Then $\mu$ is regular.

This conjecture is the matrix-valued analogue of a theorem of Stahl and Totik. It is known for direct sums by the cited scalar result, while the general matrix case is expected to require a matrix Remez inequality.
R023.source_name: David Damanik, Alexander Pushnitski and Barry Simon, “The Analytic Theory of Matrix Orthogonal Polynomials”, arXiv:0711.2703 (2008).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2703

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2007).

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for cycles of reduced forms of discriminant $a^2+4$
R023.statement:
Let a cycle of reduced forms have caliber $l$, discriminant $a^2+4$, and sum $n$. **Regularity conjecture.** There is an integer $r\geq 0$ such that

$$
n=(2r+1)l+1.
$$

If $r>0$, the cycle consists of imprimitive forms, meaning that the greatest common divisor of the coefficients of each form is greater than $1$. These conjectured regularities arise from computational evidence concerning cycles with fixed sum; the source does not provide a proof or resolution.
R023.source_name: Barry R. Smith, “Reducing quadratic forms by kneading sequences”, arXiv:1408.4631 (2014).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.4631

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

R023.title: Gevrey regularity conjecture for the Lindstedt series of the dissipative standard map
R023.statement:
Let $
u$ be a parameter and let $\boldsymbol{\mathcal D}(
u,1)$ denote the corresponding set of frequencies. For $\omega\in\mathcal D(\nu,1)$, consider the Lindstedt series

$$
u_\varepsilon=\sum_k u_k\varepsilon^k
$$

of quasi-periodic orbits for the dissipative standard map, and let $\|\cdot\|_\rho$ denote the norm at analyticity width $\rho$. **Gevrey regularity conjecture.** The Lindstedt series belongs to a Gevrey class with Gevrey exponent $\sigma\leq 0.307$; specifically,

$$
\|u_n\|_\rho\leq CR^n n^{\sigma n},\qquad \sigma\leq 0.307,
$$

with $\rho\leq 10^{-7}$. This is a reformulation of Conjecture 9 from the cited earlier work for a more general range of frequencies, based on numerical computations and fits; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
R023.source_name: Adrian P. Bustamante and Renato C. Calleja, “Corrigendum and Addendum to "Computation of domains of analyticity for the dissipative standard map in the limit of small dissipation" [arXiv:1712.05476]”, arXiv:2010.07500 (2020).
R023.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1712.05476](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05476).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

R023.title: The regularity conjecture for D(4)-quadruples
R023.statement:
Let a $D(4)$-quadruple be a set of four distinct positive integers such that the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $4$, is a perfect square. A regular $D(4)$-quadruple is one obtained from a $D(4)$-triple $\{a,b,c\}$ by adjoining

$$
d_{\pm}=a+b+c+\frac{1}{2}\left(abc\pm\sqrt{(ab+4)(ac+4)(bc+4)}\right).
$$

**Regularity conjecture.** Any $D(4)$-quadruple is regular.

Regular quadruples are explicitly generated from triples, while an irregular quadruple would be one not arising in this way. The paper studies this conjecture for pairs of the form $\{a,ka\}$ with $k\in\{2,3,6\}$ and proves that every $D(4)$-quadruple containing such a pair is regular; the general case remains open.
R023.source_name: Kouèssi Norbert Adédji, Marija Bliznac Trebješanin, Alan Filipin and Alain Togbé, “On the D(4)-pairs \a, ka\ with k\2,3,6\”, arXiv:2206.12842 (2022).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

R023.title: Regularity from a unique flat tangent cone and density concentration
R023.statement:
Let $V$ be a stationary integer rectifiable varifold, let $x_0$ be a point with a unique flat tangent cone, let $\Theta(V,x_0)$ denote its density at $x_0$, and let $\mathbf{B}_r(x_0)$ be the radius-$r$ ball centered at $x_0$. **Regularity conjecture.** If

$$
\lim_{r\searrow 0}\frac{\\|V\\|\left(\\{\Theta(V,\cdot)\neq\Theta(V,x_0)\\}\cap\mathbf{B}_r(x_0)\right)}{r^m}=0,
$$

then $x_0$ is a regular point. This is presented as a sufficient condition that would imply the paper's broader measure-zero conjecture; its resolution is not specified in the provided text.
R023.source_name: Camillo Brena, Stefano Decio and Camillo De Lellis, “Remarks and Conjectures on Stationary Varifolds”, arXiv:2503.00651 (2025).
R023.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00651

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

R023.title: Aizenbud–Gourevitch regularity conjecture
R023.statement: For every connected complex reductive algebraic group $G$ and every involutive automorphism $\theta:G\to G$, let $H=G^\theta$ and let $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{s}$ be the corresponding eigenspace decomposition of $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, where $\mathfrak{s}=\{X\in\mathfrak{g}:d\theta(X)=-X\}$. Every $H$-invariant Schwartz distribution on $\mathfrak{s}$ is invariant under the map $X\mapsto -X$; equivalently, every symmetric pair $(G,H)$ is regular in the sense of Aizenbud–Gourevitch.
R023.source_name: arXiv
R023.references: - [Regularity and the Gelfand Property for Complex Symmetric Pairs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18928) — arXiv

R023.title: Benson’s regularity conjecture for cohomology rings
R023.statement: Benson’s regularity conjecture: Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity is always zero for a cohomology ring.
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2006/30, page 61

R023.title: Epsilon-regularity conjecture for the Calabi–Yau equation on symplectic four-manifolds
R023.statement:
Let $(M,\c9)$ be a compact symplectic four-manifold equipped with an almost-complex structure $J$ tamed by $\c9$. Let $\c3$ be a smooth volume form on $M$. Suppose that $\widetilde{\u0003c9}$ is a symplectic form cohomologous to $\c9$, compatible with $J$, and solving the Calabi–Yau equation $\widetilde{\u0003c9}^{2}=\u0003c3$. Let $g$ and $\widetilde g$ be the metrics associated with $(\u0003c9,J)$ and $(\widetilde{\u0003c9},J)$, respectively. Conjecture: there exist uniform constants $\varepsilon,C>0$ such that, for a point $p\in M$ and a sufficiently small radius $r>0$, if
\[
\frac{1}{r^{2}}\int_{B_g(p,r)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\widetilde g\,dV_g\leq\varepsilon,
\]
then
\[
\sup_{B_g(p,r/2)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\widetilde g\leq\frac{C}{r^{4}}\int_{B_g(p,r)}\operatorname{tr}_{g}\widetilde g\,dV_g.
\]
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2010/26, page 19
R023.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/26](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4339), page 19. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R023.title: Regularity conjecture for the transformed gradient of p-harmonic functions
R023.statement:
Conjecture: For a p-harmonic solution $u$, the quantity $V(
abla u):=|
abla u|^{(p-2)/2}
abla u$ is locally of class $C^1$, i.e. $V(
abla u)\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, in all dimensions.
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2013/08, page 10
R023.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12336), page 10. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R023.title: Higher-dimensional regularity of the nonlinear gradient field for p-harmonic functions
R023.statement:
Conjecture: For every dimension $n\ge 3$, every $p\in(1,\infty)$, and every scalar $p$-harmonic function $u$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the field
\[
V(\nabla u):=|\nabla u|^{(p-2)/2}\nabla u
\]
belongs to $C^1$.
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2013/08, page 45
R023.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12336), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R023.title: Strong comparison principle for p-harmonic functions
R023.statement:
Suppose that $u_1$ and $u_2$ are two solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation
$$\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u\bigr)=0$$
in a domain $\Omega$ in $n$-dimensional space. If $u_2\ge u_1$ in $\Omega$, is it then true that either $u_2\equiv u_1$ or $u_2>u_1$ in $\Omega$?
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2013/08, page 46
R023.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12336), page 46. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R023.title: The Toms–Winter regularity conjecture
R023.statement:
Let \(\mathcal A\) denote the class of separable, unital, simple, nuclear, infinite-dimensional \(C^*\)-algebras. Let \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{dimnuc}}\), \(\mathcal A^Z\), and \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{comparison}}\) be the subclasses consisting, respectively, of algebras with finite nuclear dimension, \(\mathcal Z\)-stability, and strict comparison of positive elements. The regularity conjecture asserts that
\[
\mathcal A^{\mathrm{dimnuc}}=\mathcal A^Z=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{comparison}}.
\]
R023.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2016/40, page 7
R023.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/40](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14748), page 7. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R023.title: The C^{p′}-regularity conjecture
R023.statement: For every dimension $n\ge 2$ and every $p>2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be open and let $u\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a weak solution of the inhomogeneous $p$-Laplace equation $-\operatorname{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)=f$ in $\Omega$, where $f\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. Then $u\in C^{1,p'-1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)=C^{1,1/(p-1)}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, where $p'=p/(p-1)$; equivalently, $u$ has locally Hölder-continuous gradient of exponent $1/(p-1)$.
R023.source_name: arXiv
R023.references: - [The $C^{p'}$-regularity conjecture near $p=2$](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09966) — arXiv

R024.title: Crouzeix's conjecture
R024.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$. Write

$$
W(A) = \{\, x^{*}Ax : x \in \mathbb{C}^{n},\ \|x\|_{2} = 1 \,\}
$$

for the field of values (numerical range) of
$A$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{C}$, and let
$\|\cdot\|$ denote the operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$,
i.e. the spectral $2$-norm.

Let $f$ be a complex-valued function that is analytic in the interior of $W(A)$
and continuous on $W(A)$, and let $f(A)$ be the corresponding matrix, defined
for polynomials by substitution and extended by continuity. Then

$$
\|f(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|.
$$

Equivalently, for every $n \ge 1$, every $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ and
every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[z]$,

$$
\|p(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|.
$$

The constant $2$ is independent of $n$, of $A$, and of $f$.
R024.source_name: Wikipedia
R024.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Crouzeix's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crouzeix%27s_conjecture), the article this problem comes from.

R024.title: Finite-defect numerical-range conjecture for unitary dilations
R024.statement:
Suppose $T\in {\mathcal L}({\mathcal H})$ is a contraction with

$$
\dim{\mathcal D}_T=\dim{\mathcal D}_{T^*}=N<\infty.
$$

Let ${\mathcal U}$ be the set of unitary $N$-dilations of $T$ to ${\mathcal H}\oplus \mathbb{C}^N$, and define $\tau:{\mathcal U}\to\mathfrak{K}$ by $\tau({\bf U})=\overline{W({\bf U})}$. **Finite-defect numerical-range conjecture.** The map $\tau$ wraps $\overline{W(T)}$. In particular,

$$
\overline{W(T)}=\bigcap_{{\bf U}\in{\mathcal U}}\overline{W({\bf U})}.
$$

Here $\mathfrak{K}$ is the ambient space of compact convex subsets in which the closures of the numerical ranges are viewed. The conjecture would complement Choi and Li's solved answer to Halmos's question, but the source states that it remains open even for $N=1$.
R024.source_name: Chafiq Benhida, Pamela Gorkin and Dan Timotin, “Numerical ranges of C_0(N) contractions”, arXiv:1009.2249 (2010).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.2249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

R024.title: Borcea's normal-matrix spectral-distance conjecture
R024.statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ normal matrix. Write $W(A)$ for its numerical range, $\Sigma(A)$ for its spectrum, and let $A_k$ be the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix obtained by deleting the $k$th row and column of $A$. For compact sets, let $H$ denote the symmetrized Hausdorff distance.

**Borcea's normal-matrix spectral-distance conjecture.**

$$
H\left(W(A),\bigcup_{k=1}^n\Sigma(A_k)\right)\leq\min_{c\in\mathbb C}\|A-cI\|.
$$

This is presented as a matrix-theoretic generalization of Schmeisser's conjecture. The source provides no resolution.
R024.source_name: Dmitry Khavinson, Rajesh Pereira, Mihai Putinar, Edward B. Saff and Serguei Shimorin, “Borcea's variance conjectures on the critical points of polynomials”, arXiv:1010.5167 (2011).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

R024.title: Asymptotic existence of nodal curve components with expected moduli
R024.statement:
For integers $r,d,g,t$ with $0\le t\le g$, let $E'(r,d,g,t)$ be the locus of integral, non-degenerate degree-$d$ curves in $\mathbb{P}^r$ of arithmetic genus $g$ having exactly $t$ ordinary nodes as their only singularities and satisfying $h^1(C,\mathcal{O}_C(2))=0$. An irreducible component $\Gamma$ of this locus has expected dimension when its Hilbert-scheme dimension is $(r+1)d-(r-3)(g-1)$, and has the expected number of moduli when

$$
\dim\bigl(u_{r,d,g,t}(\Gamma)\bigr)=\min\{3g-3-t,3g-3+\rho(d,g,r)-t\}.
$$

**Asymptotic existence conjecture.** Fix an integer $r\geq 3$. There is a function $\mathbb{O}_r:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $\lim_{g\to+\infty}\mathbb{O}_r(g)/g=0$ and an integer $g_0$ such that, for all integers $g,t,d$ with $g\geq g_0$, $0\leq t\leq g$, and $-\rho(g,r,d)+t\leq 2g-\mathbb{O}_r(g)$, the locus $E'(r,d,g,t)$ has an irreducible component with expected dimension and the expected number of moduli.

This predicts asymptotic existence of components of the Hilbert scheme of curves in projective space having both unobstructed deformation theory and the smallest dimension permitted by the moduli map. The statement concerns all sufficiently large genera in the specified numerical range; no resolution status is supplied in the source.
R024.source_name: Edoardo Ballico, “Nodal curves and components of the Hilbert scheme of curves in P^r with the expected number of moduli”, arXiv:1304.5840 (2013).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5840

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

R024.title: The factor-valued pinching conjecture for type-II-infinity and type-III factors
R024.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak{R}}$ be a type-${\mathrm{II}}_{\infty}$ or type-${\mathrm{III}}$ factor, let $W_e^{\mathfrak{R}}(A)$ denote its essential numerical range, and let ${\mathcal{D}}$ be the set used in the preceding pinching results. An **isometric decomposition** of ${\mathfrak{R}}$ is a sequence $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ of isometries in ${\mathfrak{R}}$ such that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}V_iV_i^*=I.
$$

**Factor-valued pinching conjecture.** If $A\in{\mathfrak{R}}$ satisfies $W_e^{\mathfrak{R}}(A)\supset{\mathcal{D}}$ and $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}\subset{\mathfrak{R}}$ satisfies $\sup_i\|X_i\|<1$, then there exists an isometric decomposition $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ of ${\mathfrak{R}}$ such that

$$
V_i^*AX_i=X_i
$$

for all $i$. The conjecture proposes that the pinching theorem extends from ${\mathrm{L}}({\mathcal{H}})$ to these von Neumann factors, giving affirmative answers to the preceding extension questions; the source indicates that this is suggested by related decompositions of positive operators, but does not establish the factor version.
R024.source_name: Jean-Christophe Bourin and Eun-Young Lee, “Pinchings and Positive linear maps”, arXiv:1505.02341 (2015).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.02341

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

R024.title: Conjecture on numerical ranges of composition operators with elliptic symbols
R024.statement:
Let $D$ be the unit disk, let $H^2(D)$ be the Hardy space on $D$, and let $C_\varphi$ denote the composition operator induced by an elliptic automorphism $\varphi$ of finite order $p$. Assume that the fixed point of $\varphi$ is not $0$.

**Numerical-range conjecture.** The numerical range of $C_\varphi$ on $H^2(D)$ is the interior of the convex hull of an algebraic curve of class $p$ and degree $p^2-p$. Moreover, the real foci of the curve are exactly the eigenvalues of $C_\varphi$ on $H^2(D)$, namely

$$
\{e^{2k\pi i/p}\}_{k=1}^p.
$$

This conjecture proposes a description of the numerical range in the higher-order elliptic case, extending the observed quadratic-curve behavior when the order is smaller. The source gives no resolution, so its status is open.
R024.source_name: Yong-Xin Gao and Ze-Hua Zhou, “Numerical Ranges of Composition Operators with Elliptic Automorphism Symbols”, arXiv:1804.00295 (2023).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00295

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

R024.title: The numerical-range conjecture for periodic tridiagonal operators
R024.statement:
Let $T=T(b,0,1)$ be the tridiagonal operator where $0$ and $1$ are the constant sequences of zeroes and ones, respectively, and let $b$ be the $(n+1)$-periodic sequence with period word $0^{n}1$. Let $J_n$ denote the $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ matrix with value $1$ at positions $(1,1)$ and $(n+1,n+1)$ and zero everywhere else, and let $B_n$ be the $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ matrix with $1$'s above the diagonal and zero everywhere else. For an operator $A$, write $W(A)$ for its numerical range, and let $\overline{W(T)}$ denote the closure of $W(T)$; $\operatorname{co}$ denotes the convex hull.

**The numerical-range conjecture.**

$$
\overline{W(T)}=\operatorname{co}\bigl(W(B_n+J_n)\cup W(B_n-J_n)\bigr).
$$

This conjecture describes the closure of the numerical range of this periodic tridiagonal operator in terms of the numerical ranges of two finite matrices. The displayed examples for $n=1,2,3$ provide supporting evidence, while the supplied text does not establish the equality or state its resolution.
R024.source_name: Benjamín A. Itzá-Ortiz and Rubén A. Martínez-Avendaño, “The numerical range of a class of periodic tridiagonal operators”, arXiv:1910.00720 (2020).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.00720

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

R024.title: The unital antilinear contraction conjecture for uniform algebras
R024.statement:
Let $A$ be a uniform algebra, let $\theta:A\to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ be a continuous homomorphism, and let $\alpha:A\to A$ be a **unital** antilinear contraction, meaning that $\alpha(1)=1$. Define

$$
\theta_\alpha(f)=\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\theta(f)+\theta(\alpha(f))^*\bigr) \quad (f\in A).
$$

**Unital uniform-algebra conjecture.** If $\|\theta_\alpha\|\leq 1$, then

$$
\|\theta\|\leq 2.
$$

This conjecture would provide a homomorphism-theoretic route to the Crouzeix conjecture on numerical ranges, which asserts that $\|p(T)\|\leq 2\max_{z\in W(T)}|p(z)|$ for every polynomial $p$ and matrix $T$. The paper proves the bound $1+\sqrt{2}$ in the non-unital case and establishes the conjecture in two special cases, but the general assertion remains open.
R024.source_name: Raphaël Clouâtre, Maëva Ostermann and Thomas Ransford, “An abstract approach to the Crouzeix conjecture”, arXiv:2011.10422 (2022).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.10422

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

R024.title: A structured numerical-range realization conjecture
R024.statement:
Let $B\in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$, and suppose that its numerical range $\mathcal{W}(B)$ is invariant under multiplication by $e^{2\pi i/n}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathbb{C}}(n,d)$ denote the class of cyclic weighted shift matrices of size $d$ with cyclic structure parameter $n$. **Structured numerical-range realization conjecture.** There exists $A\in \mathcal{C}_{\mathbb{C}}(n,d)$ such that

$$
\mathcal{W}(A)=\mathcal{W}(B).
$$

If $\mathcal{W}(B)$ is also invariant under conjugation, the entries of $A$ can be chosen real. The preceding theorem establishes the analogous realization after enlarging the matrix size to $n\lceil d/n\rceil$; the conjecture asks whether the original size $d$ always suffices.
R024.source_name: Faye Pasley Simon and Cynthia Vinzant, “Invariant hyperbolic curves: determinantal representations and applications to the numerical range”, arXiv:2102.01726 (2021).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01726

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021).

R024.title: An arbitrary-size cyclic weighted-shift conjecture for higher numerical ranges
R024.statement:
Let $F_B\in\mathbb{C}[t,x,y]^{C_n}_d$ be the homogeneous polynomial associated with a matrix $B\in\mathbb{C}^{d\times d}$, and let $\mathcal{W}_k(B)$ denote its $k$-th numerical range. Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathbb{C}}(n,d)$ denote the class of cyclic weighted shift matrices of size $d$ with cyclic structure parameter $n$. **Higher numerical-range realization conjecture.** There exists $A\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathbb{C}}(n,d)$ such that

$$
\mathcal{W}_k(A)=\mathcal{W}_k(B)\qquad\text{for all }1\leq k\leq\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The corollary proves this after replacing $d$ by $n\lceil d/n\rceil$; extending the theorem to arbitrary $d$ would imply the stated same-size realization, which remains unproved in the supplied text.
R024.source_name: Faye Pasley Simon and Cynthia Vinzant, “Invariant hyperbolic curves: determinantal representations and applications to the numerical range”, arXiv:2102.01726 (2021).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01726

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021).

R024.title: Maximizing-pattern conjecture for numerical ranges of cyclic shift matrices
R024.statement:
Let $S(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ denote the $n\times n$ cyclic shift matrix with weights $a_1,\dots,a_n$. For $n\geq 2$, let $0\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$ and set

$$
A=S(a_1,a_3,a_5,\dots,a_6,a_4,a_2).
$$

For a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$, let $A_\sigma$ be the cyclic shift matrix obtained by permuting the entries of $A$, and let $W(\cdot)$ denote numerical range. **Maximizing-pattern conjecture.** For every $\sigma\in S_n$,

$$
W(A_\sigma)\subseteq W(A).
$$

The stated pattern is known to maximize the numerical radius among permutations, and the conjecture asks whether it also maximizes the numerical range by set inclusion. The abstract reports this as established for $n\leq 6$ and conjectures that the pattern extends to general $n$; the general case remains open.
R024.source_name: Mao-Ting Chien, Steve Kirkland, Chi-Kwong Li and Hiroshi Nakazato, “Numerical ranges of cyclic shift matrices”, arXiv:2304.06050 (2023).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06050

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

R024.title: Isometric decomposition conjecture for von Neumann factors
R024.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{R}$ be a type-$\mathrm{II}_{\infty}$ or type-$\mathrm{III}$ factor acting on a separable Hilbert space, and let $W_e^{\mathfrak{R}}(A)$ denote its essential numerical range. An **isometric decomposition** is a sequence $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ of isometries in $\mathfrak{R}$ satisfying 
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}V_iV_i^*=I.
$$
 Let $\mathcal{D}$ be the specified set occurring in the source. **Isometric decomposition conjecture.** If $A\in\mathfrak{R}$ satisfies $W_e^{\mathfrak{R}}(A)\supset\mathcal{D}$ and $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}\subset\mathfrak{R}$ satisfies $\sup_i\|X_i\|<1$, then there exists an isometric decomposition $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^{\infty}$ of $\mathfrak{R}$ such that 
$$
V_i^*AV_i=X_i\qquad\text{for all }i.
$$
 The surrounding section presents this as a possible extension of operator-pinning results from $\mathrm{L}(\mathcal{H})$ to type-$\mathrm{II}_{\infty}$ and type-$\mathrm{III}$ factors; the supplied text gives no resolution.
R024.source_name: Jean-Christophe Bourin, “A Journey into Matrix Analysis”, arXiv:2307.03064 (2023).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03064

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R024.title: Level set Crouzeix conjecture for finite Blaschke products
R024.statement:
Let $\Theta$ and $B$ be finite Blaschke products with $\deg B<\deg\Theta$. Let $M_\Theta$ be the matrix associated with $\Theta$, and define the $1/2$-level set

$$
\Omega^B_{1/2}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|B(z)|<1/2\}.
$$

**Level set Crouzeix conjecture.** One has

$$
W(M_\Theta)\not\subseteq\Omega^B_{1/2}.
$$

This is a weak version of Crouzeix's conjecture for finite compressions of the shift. It is known for certain classes of pairs $(B,\Theta)$, but most cases remain open.
R024.source_name: Kelly Bickel, Georgia Corbett, Annie Glenning, Changkun Guan and Martin Vollmayr-Lee, “Crouzeix's conjecture, compressions of shifts, and classes of nilpotent matrices”, arXiv:2312.04537 (2023).
R024.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2112.06321](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06321).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04537

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023).

R024.title: Pseudohyperbolic disk conjecture for unicritical Blaschke products
R024.statement:
Let $t\in[0,1)$, and let $\Theta_t$ be of the unicritical form referred to in the source. Let $W(\Theta_t)$ denote the associated numerical range. **Pseudohyperbolic disk conjecture.** If $n\geq3$, then $W(\Theta_t)$ contains a pseudohyperbolic disk of radius

$$
\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{n+1}\right).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by evidence for $n=6,7,8,11$ and by a preceding theorem, but the supplied text does not establish it in general. The notation for the unicritical form and the precise meaning of $W(\Theta_t)$ are defined elsewhere in the paper.
R024.source_name: Kelly Bickel, Georgia Corbett, Annie Glenning, Changkun Guan and Martin Vollmayr-Lee, “Crouzeix's conjecture, compressions of shifts, and classes of nilpotent matrices”, arXiv:2312.04537 (2023).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04537

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023).

R024.title: The factorization conjecture for numerical ranges of compressed shifts
R024.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}^2$ be the bidisk, let $\theta=\lambda\frac{\widetilde p}{p}$ be a rational inner function on $\mathbb{D}^2$, and let $S_\theta^1$ and $S_\theta^2$ denote the two compressed coordinate shifts associated with $\theta$. A function $\theta$ **factors as a product of one-variable finite Blaschke products** when

$$
\theta=B_1(z_1)B_2(z_2),
$$

for finite Blaschke products $B_1$ and $B_2$.

**Factorization conjecture.** If $\theta$ does not factor in this way, then $W(S_\theta^1)$ and $W(S_\theta^2)$ are open. If $\theta$ does factor in this way, then $W(S_\theta^1)$ and $W(S_\theta^2)$ are closed.

This conjecture proposes that the openness or closedness of the numerical ranges of the two compressed shifts is determined exactly by whether the rational inner function has the indicated product factorization. It is motivated by the degree-$(1,n)$ cases, but the general assertion is presented as speculative and its resolution is not given here.
R024.source_name: Kelly Bickel, Katie Quertermous and Matina Trachana, “Two-Variable Compressions of Shifts, Toeplitz Operators, and Numerical Ranges”, arXiv:2603.08559 (2026).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08559

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

R024.title: Crouzeix's conjecture for scaled q-numerical ranges
R024.statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix, let $0<|q|\leq 1$, and let $\Omega_q$ denote the scaled $q$-numerical range introduced in the source. For a polynomial $p$ with complex coefficients, **the scaled $q$-numerical-range conjecture.**

$$
\|p(A)\|\leq\max\!\left(1,\frac{2|q|}{1+\sqrt{1-|q|^2}}\right)\sup_{z\in\Omega_q}|p(z)|.
$$

This conjecture generalises Crouzeix's conjecture from the classical numerical range to scaled $q$-numerical ranges. When $q=1$, the set $\Omega_q$ reduces to the numerical range $W(A)$, recovering the known $1+\sqrt{2}$ spectral-constant bound; the proposed inequality is presented without a resolution in the source.
R024.source_name: Ryan O'Loughlin and Jyoti Rani, “q-Numerical Ranges and Spectral Sets”, arXiv:2603.15536 (2026).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15536

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

R024.title: Gau–Wang–Wu conjecture about nilpotent partial isometries
R024.statement:
Let $A\in M_n$ be a **nilpotent partial isometry**, and suppose that $A$ is **unitarily irreducible**, meaning that $A$ has no nontrivial reducing subspace. Its numerical range is

$$
W(A)=\{\langle Ax,x\rangle:x\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert x\rVert=1\}.
$$

The matrix $A$ is **rotationally invariant** when, for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$, the matrices $A$ and $e^{i\theta}A$ are unitarily similar.

**Gau–Wang–Wu conjecture.** If the numerical range $W(A)$ is a circular disc centered at the origin, then $A$ is rotationally invariant.

This conjecture concerns the distinction between circular symmetry of the numerical range and the stronger structural condition of unitary similarity to every scalar rotation. The source presents it as one of three conjectures on partial isometries; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
R024.source_name: Eric Shen, “On circular Kippenhahn curves and the Gau-Wang-Wu conjecture about nilpotent partial isometries”, arXiv:2603.25656 (2026).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25656

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

R024.title: Clouâtre–Ostermann–Ransford conjecture on contractive homomorphisms
R024.statement:
Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a uniform algebra, and let $\alpha:{\mathcal A}\to{\mathcal A}$ be a unital anti-linear contraction. Let $\theta:{\mathcal A}\to{\mathcal M}_n(\mathbb C)$ be a continuous unital algebra homomorphism, and define the linear map

$$
\Lambda:{\mathcal A}\to{\mathcal M}_n(\mathbb C),\qquad f\mapsto\theta(f)+\theta(\alpha(f))^*.
$$

**Clouâtre–Ostermann–Ransford conjecture.** (i) If $\|\Lambda\|\leq 2$, then $\|\theta\|\leq 2$. (ii) If $\alpha$ is a complete contraction, $\theta$ is completely bounded, and $\|\Lambda\|_{cb}\leq 2$, then $\|\theta\|_{cb}\leq 2$.

The source states that this conjecture was motivated by proofs related to the Crouzeix conjecture and that, if true, it would imply the Crouzeix conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

R024.title: The foci conjecture for elliptical numerical ranges of block matrices
R024.statement:
Let $H$ be a Hilbert space and let $T\in B(H\oplus H)$ have the form

$$
T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $A=A^*$ and $A^2=I$. Write $W(T)$ for the numerical range of $T$, and let $\operatorname{cl}(W(T))$ denote its closure.

**Foci conjecture.** If $\operatorname{cl}(W(T))$ is an elliptical disk, then its foci are contained in $\{0,1,-1\}$.

The source presents this as a conjecture because the corresponding necessity was known under the additional assumption that the closed numerical range is an elliptical disk with foci in $\{0,1,-1\}$, while it conjectures that this assumption is automatic.
R024.source_name: Hwa-Long Gau, Jia-Huo Hong, Chi-Kwong Li and Kuo-Zhong Wang, “Numerical radius of certain two-by-two block matrices”, arXiv:2606.08576 (2026).
R024.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

solutions.body:
**Counterexample on a separable Hilbert space; every focal distance \(r>1\) occurs.**

Gau–Hong–Li–Wang, [arXiv:2606.08576](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08576), Conjecture 3.5, asks whether
\[
T=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\in B(H\oplus H),
\qquad A=A^*,\quad A^2=I,
\]
and the assumption that \(\overline{W(T)}\) is an elliptical disk force both foci to lie in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). The source already proves the finite-dimensional case. The following infinite-dimensional separable construction disproves the general conjecture.

Let
\[
I=[-1/8,1/8],\qquad D=I\cap\mathbb Q,\qquad H=\ell^2(D;\mathbb C^2),
\]
and define
\[
G(x)=240\frac{1-x^2}{1-4x^2},
\qquad d(x)=G'(x)=\frac{1440x}{(1-4x^2)^2},
\qquad s(x)=G(x)-xG'(x).
\]
Explicitly,
\[
s(x)=240\frac{1-11x^2+4x^4}{(1-4x^2)^2}.
\]
Throughout \(I\), one has \(s(x)>|d(x)|\): for \(t=|x|\le1/8\), this reduces to
\[
1-6t-11t^2+4t^4\ge\frac{81}{1024}>0.
\]
Hence the continuous bounded functions
\[
u(x)=\sqrt{\frac{s(x)+d(x)}2},
\qquad
v(x)=\sqrt{\frac{s(x)-d(x)}2}
\]
are strictly positive. Define bounded operators fiberwise by
\[
A_x=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B_x=\begin{pmatrix}u(x)&0\\v(x)&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad x\in D.
\]
In particular, \(A=A^*\), \(A^2=I\), and \(\|B\|^2=240\).

Write \(c=\cos\theta\). After a unitary removal of the off-diagonal phase, each fiber of \(\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}T)\) equals
\[
K_x(c)\oplus[0],
\qquad
K_x(c)=
\begin{pmatrix}
c&0&u(x)/2\\
0&-c&v(x)/2\\
u(x)/2&v(x)/2&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set
\[
h(c)=\sqrt{60+4c^2},
\qquad y=\frac{c}{h(c)}\in I.
\]
Since \(h(c)>|c|\), the Schur-complement criterion gives
\[
h(c)I-K_x(c)\succeq0
\iff s(x)+d(x)y\le4\bigl(h(c)^2-c^2\bigr)
\iff G(x)+G'(x)(y-x)\le G(y),
\]
where
\[
4\bigl(h(c)^2-c^2\bigr)=240+12c^2=G(y).
\]
But
\[
G''(x)=\frac{1440(1+12x^2)}{(1-4x^2)^3}>0.
\]
Therefore the required inequality is precisely the supporting-tangent inequality for the strictly convex function \(G\), with equality exactly when \(x=y\). Since \(D\) is dense, continuity gives
\[
\sup\sigma\!\left(\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}T)\right)
=\sup_{x\in D}\lambda_{\max}(K_x(\cos\theta))
=\sqrt{60+4\cos^2\theta}.
\]
This is the support function of
\[
\boxed{\overline{W(T)}
=\left\{a+ib:\frac{a^2}{64}+\frac{b^2}{60}\le1\right\}.}
\]
Its semiaxes are \(8\) and \(\sqrt{60}\), so its foci are
\[
\boxed{-\sqrt{64-60}=-2,\qquad \sqrt{64-60}=2,}
\]
neither of which belongs to \(\{-1,0,1\}\).

More generally, let any \(r>1\) be prescribed and put
\[
R=r^2,\quad \alpha=4R,\quad \beta^2=\alpha^2-R,\quad
I_R=[-1/\alpha,1/\alpha],
\]
\[
G_R(x)=4\beta^2\frac{1-x^2}{1-Rx^2},\qquad
d_R=G_R',\qquad s_R=G_R-xG_R'.
\]
One has
\[
G_R''(x)=
\frac{8\beta^2(R-1)(1+3Rx^2)}{(1-Rx^2)^3}>0.
\]
For \(t=|x|\le1/(4R)\), positivity \(s_R>|d_R|\) follows from
\[
1-2(R-1)t-(3R-1)t^2+Rt^4
>1-\frac12-\frac3{16R}>\frac5{16}.
\]
Repeating the countable dense-fiber construction gives support function
\[
h_R(\cos\theta)=\sqrt{\beta^2+R\cos^2\theta}.
\]
The resulting elliptical disk has semiaxes \(\alpha,\beta\), and therefore foci
\[
\boxed{\{-\sqrt{\alpha^2-\beta^2},\sqrt{\alpha^2-\beta^2}\}
=\{-r,r\}.}
\]
Thus every prescribed focal distance \(r>1\) furnishes a separable counterexample to the exact closure formulation of Conjecture 3.5.

R024.title: The extended local-permutation conjecture for block-shift matrices
R024.statement:
Let $E(\mathfrak{t}_{\mathrm{loc}})$ be the relevant set of matrices, and let $\Pi_{\mathrm{loc}}$ be the subgroup of signed local permutations consisting of matrices

$$
P_1\otimes\dots\otimes P_n,
$$

where, for $k=1,\dots,n$,

$$
P_k\in\left\{\pm I_2,\ \pm\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}\right\}.
$$

Let $P_{\rm out}$ be the displayed permutation matrix in the source, and let $\Pi_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the subgroup generated by inserting $P_{\rm out}$ in every possible tensor-factor position. Define

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ex}}:=\Pi_{\mathrm{loc}}\cdot\Pi_{\mathrm{out}}.
$$

A block-shift matrix is a matrix of the block-shift form described in the preceding classification.

**Extended local-permutation conjecture.** Every element of $E(\mathfrak{t}_{\mathrm{loc}})$ is similar to a block-shift matrix via an element of $\Pi_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ex}}$.

This conjecture seeks the smallest natural enlargement of local signed permutations that accounts for all observed matrices with circular local $C$-numerical range; the proposed enlargement is generated by local permutations together with the displayed outer permutation in every tensor position.

R024.title: Crouzeix conjecture
R024.statement: For every integer $n\ge 1$, every matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, and every polynomial $p\in\mathbb{C}[z]$, one has $\|p(A)\|_2\le 2\sup_{z\in W(A)}|p(z)|$, where $W(A)=\{x^*Ax:x\in\mathbb{C}^n,\ \|x\|_2=1\}$ is the numerical range of $A$.

R024.title: Investigation of the Crouzeix-Palencia proof (problem 2)
R024.statement:
Let $\theta$ be a continuous homomorphism from a uniform algebra $A$ into a $C^{*}$-algebra $B$ and $\alpha:A\rightarrow A$ be antilinear and such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[*] $\|\alpha f\|\leq \|f\|$ for all $f\in A$,
\item[*] $\|\theta f +(\theta\alpha f)^{*}\|\leq 2\|f\|$ for all $f\in A$, and 
\item[*] $\alpha 1=1$.
\end{itemize}
Does this imply that $\|\theta\|=2$?

R024.title: Non-self adjoint spectral problems
R024.statement: Much is now known, theoretically and also numerically, about the spectrum of self-adjoint operators. This is in great contrast to the situation regarding non-self-adjoint operators, where the spectral theory is far more subtle and numerical schemes must overcome significant, inherent instabilities. The heart of the difficulties and instabilities lies in the following fact: in the self-adjoint case $A=A^*$, the resolvent $(A-\lambda)^{-1}$ is bounded by the distance of $\lambda$ to the spectrum of $A$, but in the non-self-adjoint case, this is no longer true, as we see already in the $2\times2$ case, $A=\begin{bmatrix}0 n\\0 0\end{bmatrix}$, $n\to\infty$. In recent years, a number of authors (e.g. Trefethan, Davies,...) have initiated a systematic approach to non-self-adjoint spectral problems, notions such as pseudospectrum have come into prominence, and other authors have conducted in depth studies of particular non-self-adjoint spectrum problems which arise in practice. For example, in analyzing the semi-classical limit of the focusing NLS equation, one must analyze the spectrum of the associated AKNS operator $T(h)$, as Planck's constant $h$ goes to zero. The operator is non-self-adjoint, and as $h$ goes to zero more and more eigenvalues, corresponding to solitons, emerge in the complex plane. It is of critical importance to the analysis of the semi-classical limits for NLS to determine where in the plane, and at what rate, the eigenvalues accumulate. The difficulty in doing this, theoretically and numerically, is illustrated by the following fact: the spectrum of $T(h)$ off the real axis is a discrete set, whereas the numerical range of $T(h)$ is an open subset of the plane. Nevertheless, every point $\lambda$ lying in the numerical range of $T(h)$ is an eigenvalue of $T(h)$ to all orders in $h$, $\|(T(h)-\lambda)u\|=O(|h|^k)$ for any $k\geq 1$, for some $u=u(h)$, $\|u\|=1$. In the language of Kruskal, the computation of the spectrum of $T(h)$ is a problem ``beyond all orders.'' Much has been done (Kamvissis-Miller-McLaughlin, Tovbis-Venakides-Zhou,...) in analyzing the semi-classical limit for NLS in special situations where the spectral problem can be solved explicitly. The spectral problem with general data, both for NLS and also other related non-self-adjoint problems, however, is far from understood, and poses a great challenge whose resolution is still only in the initial stages.
R024.source_name: Deift - Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems (2007) (proposed by Percy Deift)

R024.title: Complete Crouzeix conjecture
R024.statement: For every $n,m\ge 1$, every matrix $A\in M_n(\mathbb{C})$, and every matrix-valued polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^d P_k z^k$ with $P_k\in M_m(\mathbb{C})$, one has $\left\|\sum_{k=0}^d A^k\otimes P_k\right\|\le 2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|$, where $W(A)=\{\langle Ax,x\rangle:x\in\mathbb{C}^n,\ \|x\|=1\}$ is the numerical range of $A$ and the norms are operator norms.
R024.source_name: arXiv

R024.title: A posteriori upper error bound for the nonconforming Crouzeix–Raviart approximation of Stokes flow
R024.statement:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d\), \(d\in\{2,3\}\), be an open polygonal or polyhedral domain. For the stationary incompressible Stokes problem with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and pressure normalized by \(\int_\Omega p=0\), let \(u_h\) and \(p_h\) be the nonconforming Crouzeix–Raviart finite-element approximations. With \(f_K\) a constant approximation of \(f\) on each element \(K\), define
\[
\eta=\eta_c+\eta_{nc},
\]
where
\[
\eta_c:=\frac{1}{d^2(d+1)}\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\,\lVert f_K\rVert^2\sum_{\gamma\subset\partial K}\lVert x_\gamma-x_K\rVert^2\right)^{1/2}
\]
and, for any \(u^*\in H^1_0(\Omega)^2\),
\[
\eta_{nc}:=\lVert\nabla_h(u^*-u_h)\rVert+\frac{1}{c_0}\lVert\nabla\!\cdot u^*\rVert,
\]
with \(c_0\) a lower bound for the continuous inf-sup constant. Then
\[
\lVert\nabla_h(u-u_h)\rVert\leq \eta+C\,\operatorname{osc}_{\mathcal K}(f),
\]
where \(C>0\) depends only on the shape regularity of the mesh. Thus the estimator gives an explicit computable upper bound in the leading order.
R024.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2004/16, page 17
R024.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/699), page 17. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R024.title: Converse comparison between Crouzeix–Raviart and Raviart–Thomas errors
R024.statement:
For the Poisson problem on a bounded polygonal Lipschitz domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2\), with \(f\in L^2(\Omega)\), weak solution \(u\in H^1_0(\Omega)\), and a shape-regular triangulation \(\mathcal T\), the converse estimate
\[
\|\nabla u-\nabla_{NC}u_{CR}\|\not\lesssim \|\nabla u-p_{RT}\|+\operatorname{osc}(f,\mathcal T)
\]
is false in general. Here \(u_{CR}\) and \(p_{RT}\) are the Crouzeix–Raviart and Raviart–Thomas finite-element solutions, respectively; \(\lesssim\) denotes a bound with a constant depending only on the minimal angle of \(\mathcal T\), not on \(\Omega\) or the mesh size, and \(\operatorname{osc}(f,\mathcal T)=\|h_{\mathcal T}(f-\Pi_0f)\|\).
R024.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2012/09, page 39
R024.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/09](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11576), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R024.title: Comparison result for first-order finite element methods in linear elasticity
R024.statement:
For the Navier–Lamé problem (2), comparing the conforming Courant FEM, the nonconforming Kouhia–Stenberg FEM, and the nonconforming Crouzeix–Raviart FEM, with respective stress solutions \(\sigma_C\), \(\sigma_{KS}\), and \(\sigma_{CR}\), the report states
\[
\|\sigma-\sigma_C\|\lesssim_{\lambda}\|\sigma-\sigma_{KS}\|\lesssim_{\lambda}\bigl(\|\sigma-\sigma_C\|+\operatorname{osc}(f,\mathcal T)\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\|\sigma-\sigma_{KS}\|+\operatorname{osc}(f,\mathcal T)\approx
\|\sigma-\sigma_{CR}\|+\operatorname{osc}(f,\mathcal T).
\]
Here the comparison is for the finite element spaces and bilinear forms specified in the report; the constants in the \(\lesssim\) notation are stated to be independent of the Lamé modulus \(\lambda\).
R024.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2012/09, page 40
R024.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/09](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11576), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R024.title: Quasi-optimal and λ-robust adaptive Crouzeix–Raviart FEM for pure displacement elasticity
R024.statement:
For the approximation class $A_s:=\{(u,f)\mid |(u,f)|_{A_s}<\infty\}$ with $s>0$, the report states that the adaptive algorithm $A_{\mathrm{crfem}}$, for every $0<\theta<\theta_0\le 1$ with $\theta_0$ independent of the Lamé parameter $\lambda$, generates triangulations $(\mathcal T_\ell)_\ell$ and discrete solutions $(u_\ell)_\ell$ with quasi-optimal convergence rates, expressed as
$$
|\mathcal T_\ell|-|\mathcal T_0|
\le C_{\mathrm{opt}}\left(\|u-u_\ell\|_{\mathrm{NC}(\ell)}^2+\|h_\ell f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\right)^{-1/(2s)}.
$$
The report further states that the analysis is robust as $\lambda\to\infty$.
R024.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2012/09, page 74

R024.title: Crouzeix’s numerical-range spectral-set conjecture with constant $Q=2$
R024.statement:
Let $A\in L(D(A),H)$ be a linear operator on a complex (or complexified) Hilbert space $H$, and let
$$
W(A)=\{\langle Av,v\rangle:\ v\in D(A),\ \|v\|_H=1\}
$$
be its numerical range. The conjecture is that $W(A)$ is a $2$-spectral set for $A$; equivalently, for every rational function $r$ bounded on $W(A)$,
$$
\|r(A)\|\le 2\sup_{z\in W(A)}|r(z)|.
$$

R025.title: Fluid-phase repulsion conjecture for hard-sphere and hard-core models
R025.statement: Let the hard-sphere model or hard-core model be at density $\alpha$. The hard-sphere model consists of nonoverlapping spheres, while the hard-core model consists of particles occupying lattice sites subject to the hard-core exclusion constraint. The model is said to be in the **fluid phase** if, for example, it exhibits exponentially fast decay of correlations or the single-particle global-move Markov chain with the model's distribution as stationary distribution mixes rapidly. The **repulsion inequality** compares the expected volume or number of covered sites under repulsion conditioning, and the birthday inequality is the corresponding collision bound. **Fluid-phase repulsion conjecture.** If the hard-sphere or hard-core model is in the fluid phase, then the repulsion inequality, and hence the birthday inequality, holds. The conjecture predicts that these inequalities remain valid throughout the fluid phase, while the authors explain that long-range correlations beyond the fluid/solid phase transition may cause the repulsion inequality to fail. A proof would yield phase-transition bounds for hard-sphere and fixed-size hard-core models; the source does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
R025.source_name: Will Perkins, “Birthday Inequalities, Repulsion, and Hard Spheres”, arXiv:1506.02700 (2015).
R025.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02700

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2015).

R025.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the annihilated Boltzmann hierarchy with hard-sphere interactions
R025.statement:
Assume that the collision kernel $\mathsf{B}$ is given by

$$
\mathsf{B}(v-v_{*},omega)=frac{1}{2pi}left|left(v-v_{*}right) cdot omegaright|,
$$

for $(v,v_{*})in \mathbb{R}^{3}timesmathbb{R}^{3}$ and $omegain \mathbb{S}^{2}$, and let $\mathcal{Q}$ be the corresponding Boltzmann operator. Let $f_{0}$ be a non-negative probability distribution satisfying the normalization condition. For the unique solution $f(t)$ of the Boltzmann equation with initial datum $f(0)=f_{0}$, define

$$
nu_{k}(t)=f(t)^{otimes k},qquad tgeq 0,qquad kgeq 1.
$$

**Uniqueness conjecture.** The sequence $bm{nu}^{infty}={nu_{k}}_{k}$ is the unique solution in $L^{infty}([0,infty),\mathcal{X})$ to the annihilated Boltzmann hierarchy in the sense of the stated weak-solution definition, with initial data $nu_{k}(0)=f_{0}^{otimes k}$ for every $kgeq 1$. This uniqueness would yield propagation of chaos for hard-sphere interactions, extending the result beyond bounded collision kernels; the obstruction is the lack of a suitable uniqueness proof for the annihilated Boltzmann hierarchy, since the De Finetti approach fails in this setting.
R025.source_name: Bertrand Lods, Alessia Nota and Federica Pezzotti, “A Kac model for kinetic annihilation”, arXiv:1904.03447 (2019).
R025.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

R025.title: Translation invariance of the two-dimensional hard-sphere Gibbs model
R025.statement:
Let $r>0$, let $|\cdot|$ be any norm on $\mathbb{R}^{2}$, and define the pure hard-core potential
\[
U_{\mathrm{hc}}(x_1,x_2):=
\begin{cases}
\infty,& |x_1-x_2|\le r,\\
0,& |x_1-x_2|>r,
\end{cases}
\qquad x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}^{2}.
\]
Then, for every activity $z>0$, all equilibrium states corresponding to $U_{\mathrm{hc}}$ and $z$ are translation-invariant.

R025.title: Boltzmann-limit convergence for unscattered hard spheres
R025.statement:
Let $n$ hard spheres of diameter $a$ evolve by force-free Newtonian dynamics under the Boltzmann–Grad scaling $n a^{d-1}=1$, with independent, identically distributed initial data $(u_0,v_0)=(z_1,\ots,z_n)$ having density $f_0$. Particles that overlap at $t=0$ are removed, and $\beta_i^{(a)}(t)$ equals $1$ for an unscattered particle and $0$ for a scattered or removed particle. Assume that moments of $f_0$ through order two are finite and that the initial data are $L^\infty$ in space. If $f_t$ is the unique mild solution of
$$
\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_u f=-Q^-[f,f],\qquad f(u,v,0)=f_0(u,v),
$$
where
$$
Q^-[f,g](u,v)=\left(\int_{\mathbb R^d}g(u,v')\,\kappa_d|v-v'|\,dv'\right)f(u,v),
$$
then, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every open $A\subset U\times\mathbb R^d$, uniformly for $t\in[0,T]$,
$$
\lim_{a\to0}\mathop{\rm Prob}\!\left(\left|\frac1n\#\left\{i:(u_i(t),v_i(t))\in A,\ \beta_i^{(a)}(t)=1\right\}-\int_A f_t(u,v)\,du\,dv\right|>\varepsilon\right)=0.
$$
R025.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12594), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R025.title: Kac’s spectral-gap conjecture for the hard-sphere gas
R025.statement:
Let $S_{N,E,p}$ be the space of velocity vectors satisfying the total-energy and total-momentum constraints, equipped with the uniform normalized measure $\d70e_N$, and let the hard-sphere Dirichlet form and spectral gap be defined by

$$
\mathcal E_N(f,f)=\frac{1}{N^2\binom{N}{2}}\sum_{i<j}\int_{S_{N,E,p}}\int_{S^2}|v_i-v_j|\,[f(\vec v)-f(R_{i,j,\sigma}\vec v)]^2\,d\sigma\,d\u0001d70e_N,
$$

$$
\Delta_N(E,p)=\inf\left\{\mathcal E_N(f,f): f\in L^2(S_{N,E,p},\u0001d70e_N),\ \langle f,1\rangle_{L^2(\u0001d70e_N)}=0,\ \|f\|_{L^2(\u0001d70e_N)}=1\right\}.
$$

Then there exists a positive constant $K$, independent of $N$, such that

$$
\Delta_N(E,p)\ge K\bigl(E-|p|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
R025.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/41](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17137), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R025.title: Correct second-order upper bound for the dilute hard-sphere Bose gas
R025.statement: In the hard-sphere Bose-gas setting of the report, establish an upper bound for the ground-state energy per particle that captures the second term in the Lee–Huang–Yang expansion (4), with the correct constant. The report states this as: “It remains an important open problem to establish such an upper bound with the correct constant.”
R025.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2025/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299579), page 14. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

R026.title: Saxl's staircase tensor-square conjecture
R026.statement:
For $k\geq 1$, let

$$
\delta_k=(k,k-1,\ldots,1)
$$

be the staircase partition, which has size $\binom{k+1}{2}$. For partitions of this size, $g(\delta_k,\delta_k,\mu)$ is the multiplicity of the irreducible $S_{\binom{k+1}{2}}$-module indexed by $\mu$ in the tensor square of the module indexed by $\delta_k$.

**Saxl's conjecture.**

$$
g(\delta_k,\delta_k,\mu)>0
$$

for all $k$ and all $\mu\vdash\binom{k+1}{2}$.

This is a concrete proposed choice of the symmetric partition in the tensor square conjecture. Its significance is that the staircase partition is specified uniformly rather than existentially.
R026.source_name: Greta Panova, “Complexity and asymptotics of structure constants”, arXiv:2305.02553 (2023).
R026.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02553

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023).

R026.title: Saxl's conjecture for staircase partitions
R026.statement:
Let $\rho_m$ be the staircase partition of size $n=\binom{m+1}{2}$, and let $g(\lambda,\lambda,\mu)$ denote the Kronecker coefficient. **Saxl Conjecture.** For every partition $\mu\vdash n$, one has

$$
g(\rho_m,\rho_m,\mu)>0.
$$

This is the staircase-shape specialization of the tensor-square problem for irreducible representations of $S_n$. The source attributes it to Jan Saxl in 2012 and does not indicate a resolution.
R026.source_name: Chenchen Zhao, “On the Kronecker product of Schur functions of square shapes”, arXiv:2309.00764 (2023).
R026.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1903.07717](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07717), [arXiv:1704.04425](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04425), [arXiv:1511.02387](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02387).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00764
Jan Saxl (2012), as attributed in the source
Pak, Panova, and Vallejo (2013), cited in the source as pak2013kronecker

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

R026.title: Saxl's conjecture on tensor squares of staircase representations
R026.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, set $n=k(k+1)/2$, and let $\lambda=(k,k-1,\ldots,2,1)$ be the staircase partition of $n$. Let $\sigma_\lambda$ be the irreducible representation of $S_n$ indexed by $\lambda$. **Saxl's conjecture.** The tensor product $\sigma_\lambda\otimes\sigma_\lambda$ contains every irreducible representation of $S_n$ as a constituent. This is a well-known open problem about decomposing tensor products of irreducible representations of symmetric groups; the paper presents progress and generalisations, but the conjecture itself remains open.
R026.source_name: Yutong Chen, Felix Gu and Will Osborne, “Spin Representations of Finite Coxeter Groups and Generalisations of Saxl's Conjecture”, arXiv:2409.17540 (2024).
R026.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2309.00764](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00764), [arXiv:1903.07717](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.07717), [arXiv:1704.04425](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04425), [arXiv:1511.02387](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02387).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17540

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

R027.title: The conjecture that optimal rectilinear drawings of $K_n$ are 3-decomposable
R027.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $K_n$ be the complete graph drawn with straight-line edges on a point set in general position. A drawing is **optimal** if it minimizes the number of crossings among rectilinear drawings of $K_n$, and it is **3-decomposable** if its underlying point set admits the three-part decomposition described in the paper.

**3-decomposability conjecture.** For each positive integer $n$ divisible by $3$, all optimal rectilinear drawings of $K_n$ are 3-decomposable.

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that all best crossing-wise known drawings have underlying point sets minimizing the number of $(\leq k)$-sets for every $k\leq n/3$, a property equivalent to 3-decomposability. It remains open in general.
R027.source_name: B. Ábrego, M. Cetina, S. Fernández–Merchant, J. Leaños and G. Salazar, “3–symmetric and 3–decomposable drawings of K_n (extended version)”, arXiv:0805.0016 (2008).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0016

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2008).

R027.title: The conjecture that every divisible-order complete graph has a 3-symmetric optimal drawing
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph drawn geometrically, with vertices represented by points in general position and edges by straight-line segments. A drawing is **optimal** if it has the minimum possible number of crossings among geometric drawings of $K_n$, and it is **3-symmetric** if it has 3-fold symmetry.

**3-symmetric optimal-drawing conjecture.** For each positive integer $n$ divisible by $3$, there is an optimal geometric drawing of $K_n$ that is 3-symmetric.

The conjecture is suggested by the resemblance between known optimal constructions and 3-symmetric point sets, although the paper notes that previously known explicit best constructions were generally not 3-symmetric. The assertion remains open.
R027.source_name: B. Ábrego, M. Cetina, S. Fernández–Merchant, J. Leaños and G. Salazar, “3–symmetric and 3–decomposable drawings of K_n (extended version)”, arXiv:0805.0016 (2008).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0016

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2008).

R027.title: Ilmanen's outermost-horizon topology conjecture
R027.statement: Let $(M^n,g,k)$ and $\bar\Sigma$ be as in Ilmanen's conjecture: the data are complete and asymptotically flat, $3\le n\le 7$, and $\bar\Sigma$ is the unique outermost generalized trapped surface that is a generalized apparent horizon. **Ilmanen's topology conjecture.** The surface $\bar\Sigma$ is strictly area outerminimizing, meaning every other surface enclosing it has larger area; when $n=3$, the region exterior to $\bar\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^3$ minus finitely many disjoint closed balls. This generalizes the Meeks--Simon--Yau result for $k=0$; the source reports announced proofs of the geometric assertions, except for the topological part.
R027.source_name: Hubert L. Bray and Marcus A. Khuri, “P.d.e.'s which imply the Penrose conjecture”, arXiv:0905.2622 (2009).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.2622

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2009). “The following existence conjecture for these equations implies the outermost case of the generalized Penrose conjecture, conjecture , using the Riemannian Penrose inequality, and is therefore an important open problem.”

R027.title: The outermost case of the generalized Penrose conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $(M^3,g,k)$ be complete Cauchy data satisfying $\mu\ge |J|$, Schwarzschild at infinity with total mass $m$ in a chosen end. Let $\Sigma^2=\partial U^3\in\mathcal S$ be a strictly area outerminimizing generalized apparent horizon, assume no other generalized trapped surfaces enclose it, and assume $M^3\setminus\overline{U^3}$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^3$ minus finitely many disjoint closed balls. **Outermost generalized Penrose conjecture.** If $A$ is the area of $\Sigma^2$, then

$$
m\ge \sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}.
$$

Equality should occur if and only if $(M^3\setminus U^3,g,k)$ is the pullback of Cauchy data induced on the image of a spacelike embedding into the exterior of a Schwarzschild spacetime, mapping $\Sigma^2$ to a generalized apparent horizon. The source explains that the Ilmanen conjectures would reduce the generalized Penrose conjecture to this case; it remains open.
R027.source_name: Hubert L. Bray and Marcus A. Khuri, “P.d.e.'s which imply the Penrose conjecture”, arXiv:0905.2622 (2009).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.2622

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2009). “The following existence conjecture for these equations implies the outermost case of the generalized Penrose conjecture, conjecture , using the Riemannian Penrose inequality, and is therefore an important open problem.”

R027.title: The blocker number of simple drawings of complete graphs
R027.statement: A drawing of a graph represents vertices by distinct plane points and edges by simple curves, with a vertex meeting an edge only at an endpoint. A drawing is **simple** if any two edges intersect at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A set of points blocks a drawing if it contains no vertex and every edge contains a blocker. **Simple-drawing blocker conjecture.** The minimum number of blockers in a simple drawing of $K_n$ equals $2n-3$. A construction gives an upper bound of $2n-3$, while the general lower bound stated in the source is only $n-1$; the conjectured exact value remains open.
R027.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2009). “BigClique} is true for $k\leq 5$ or $\ell\leq3$ , and is open for $k=6$ or $\ell=4$.”

R027.title: The superlinear crossing-family conjecture for geometric complete graphs
R027.statement:
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of colours needed to colour the edges of some geometric drawing of $K_n$ so that every pair of edges with the same colour crosses; each colour class is a crossing family. **Crossing-family conjecture.** The colouring number satisfies

$$
\frac{t(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

Since each crossing family can be associated with blockers, this is stated as a strengthening of the superlinear blocking conjecture and remains open.
R027.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2009). “BigClique} is true for $k\leq 5$ or $\ell\leq3$ , and is open for $k=6$ or $\ell=4$.”

R027.title: The complexified Volume Conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot, meaning that its complement $S^3\setminus K$ possesses a complete hyperbolic structure. Let $J_N(K;q)$ be the $N$-dimensional colored Jones polynomial, and let $\operatorname{CS}(S^3\setminus K)$ denote the Chern--Simons invariant of the three-manifold with torus boundary. **The complexified Volume Conjecture.**

$$
2\pi\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log J_N(K;\exp(2\pi\sqrt{-1}/N))}{N}\equiv \operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)+\sqrt{-1}\operatorname{CS}(S^3\setminus K)\pmod{\pi^2\sqrt{-1}\mathbb{Z}}.
$$

This conjecture incorporates the Chern--Simons invariant as the imaginary part of the complexified volume. The paper presents it as a natural strengthening of the Volume Conjecture, with the stated general claim not established in full.
R027.source_name: Hitoshi Murakami, “An Introduction to the Volume Conjecture”, arXiv:1002.0126 (2010).
R027.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0802.0039](https://arxiv.org/abs/0802.0039).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0126

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2010).

R027.title: Modified Vojta conjecture with a dimension-dependent discriminant coefficient
R027.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a fixed positive real-valued function. Let $X$ be a nonsingular complete variety of dimension $n$ with canonical divisor $K$, and let $D$ be a normal crossings divisor on $X$. Let $k$ be a number field over which $X$ and $D$ are defined, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $k$, let $A$ be a big divisor on $X$, let $\epsilon>0$, and let $r$ be a positive integer.

**Modified Vojta conjecture.** There exists a proper Zariski-closed subset

$$
Z=Z(f,r,\epsilon,X,D,A)
$$

of $X$ such that

$$
m_{D,S}(P)+h_K(P)\leq f(n)d(P)+\epsilon h_A(P)+O(1)
$$

for all $P\in X(\overline{k})\setminus Z$ with $[k(P):k]\leq r$.

This is a dimension-dependent modification of Vojta's conjecture, introduced to study how the exceptional set depends on the degree bound $r$; the supplied source gives no resolution status, so it is recorded as open.
R027.source_name: Aaron Levin, “The exceptional set in Vojta's conjecture for algebraic points of bounded degree”, arXiv:1011.6561 (2010).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6561

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

R027.title: Ilman's asymptotic-end conjecture for embedded self-shrinkers
R027.statement:
Let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth complete embedded self-shrinker with at most quadratic area growth. An **end** is a connected component of $\Sigma\setminus B_R$ for sufficiently large $R$. For a vector $v_j$, the associated self-shrinking cylinder is

$$
\left\{x: \operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{span}(v_j))=\sqrt{2}\right\}.
$$

**Ilman's asymptotic-end conjecture.** There exists $R>0$ such that $\Sigma\setminus B_R$ decomposes into a finite number of ends $U_j$, and for each $j$ either:

* as $\lambda\longrightarrow 0+$, $\lambda U_j$ converges locally smoothly to a cone $C_j$ such that $C_j\setminus\{O\}$ is smooth; or
* there is a vector $v_j$ such that, as $\tau\longrightarrow +\infty$, $U_j-\tau v_j$ converges to the cylinder

$$
\left\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{span}(v_j))=\sqrt{2}\right\}.
$$

All known examples and numerical evidence support this proposed classification of ends, but the conjecture remains open.
R027.source_name: Lu Wang, “Uniqueness of Self-similar Shrinkers with Asymptotically Conical Ends”, arXiv:1110.0450 (2011).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.0450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

R027.title: Ori's conjecture on perturbations of two-ended Kerr data
R027.statement: Let $(\mathcal{M},g)$ be the maximal vacuum Cauchy development of sufficiently small perturbations of asymptotically flat two-ended Kerr data corresponding to parameters $0<|a|<M$. A future or past extension is an extension $(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}},\widetilde{g})$ of $\mathcal{M}$ with $C^0$ metric $\widetilde{g}$. **Ori's conjecture.** There exist both a future and past extension $(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}},\widetilde{g})$ such that $\partial\mathcal{M}$ is a bifurcate null cone in $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}$ and all future, respectively past, incomplete geodesics in $\gamma$ pass into $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}\setminus\mathcal{M}$. Moreover, for generic such perturbations, any $C^0$ extension has no $L^2$ Christoffel symbols in a neighbourhood of any point of $\partial\mathcal{M}$. This conjecture predicts a weakly singular Cauchy horizon for generic perturbations of subextremal Kerr, extending the corresponding symmetric-model picture; it remains open in the full vacuum, nonsymmetric setting.
R027.source_name: Mihalis Dafermos, “Black holes without spacelike singularities”, arXiv:1201.1797 (2013).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.1797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

R027.title: Kerr–de Sitter Cauchy-horizon extendibility conjecture
R027.statement: Let $(\mathcal{M},g)$ be the maximal Cauchy development for the Einstein vacuum equations with positive cosmological constant of sufficiently small perturbations of subextremal Kerr–de Sitter data with $n$ black-hole regions and initial topology $\mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{S}^2$. **Kerr–de Sitter extendibility conjecture.** The spacetime is future, respectively past, extendible to $(\widetilde{\mathcal{M}},\widetilde{g})$ with $C^0$ metric $\widetilde{g}$, such that $\partial\mathcal{M}$ is the union of $n$ bifurcate null cones and all incomplete future, respectively past, inextendible geodesics of $\mathcal{M}$ pass into $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}\setminus\mathcal{M}$. This is the vacuum analogue of the stated spherically symmetric Reissner–Nordström–de Sitter stability result and challenges strong cosmic censorship at low regularity for positive cosmological constant; the full assertion remains open.
R027.source_name: Mihalis Dafermos, “Black holes without spacelike singularities”, arXiv:1201.1797 (2013).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.1797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

R027.title: The split exactness conjecture for matching-complex deletion sequences
R027.statement:
Let $n\geq3$, let $e$ be an edge of the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathsf{M}_n\setminus e$ be the matching complex with the vertex $e$ deleted. Consider the sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\tilde{H}_d(\mathsf{M}_n\setminus e;\mathbb{Z})\longrightarrow\tilde{H}_d(\mathsf{M}_n;\mathbb{Z})\longrightarrow\langle e\rangle\otimes\tilde{H}_{d-1}(\mathsf{M}_{[n]\setminus e};\mathbb{Z})\longrightarrow0.
$$

**Split exactness conjecture.** This sequence, obtained by cutting the long exact $0$-$e$-$2$ sequence, is split exact for every $n\geq3$ and every $d$.

If true, the long exact deletion sequence would decompose into short split exact sequences, giving a direct-sum description of the homology groups. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
R027.source_name: Jakob Jonsson, “Exact Sequences for the Homology of the Matching Complex”, arXiv:1203.5641 (2012).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.5641

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2012).

R027.title: The DDS optimality conjecture for book crossing numbers of complete graphs
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $
u_k(K_n)$ denote its minimum number of crossings in a $k$-page book drawing, and let $Z_k(n)$ denote the number of crossings in the DDS construction of $K_n$ in $k$ pages. **DDS optimality conjecture.** For all positive integers $k$ and $n$,

$$
\nu_k(K_n) = Z_k(n).
$$

The conjecture asserts the optimality of the DDS construction for every number of pages and every complete graph. The paper presents this as a general conjecture; its $k=3$ case is supported by computations for all 8 values of $n\geq 7$ considered there.
R027.source_name: Etienne de Klerk, Dmitrii V. Pasechnik and Gelasio Salazar, “Improved lower bounds on book crossing numbers of complete graphs”, arXiv:1207.5701 (2012).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.5701

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2012).

R027.title: The crossing-number conjecture for the crown graph
R027.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}-nK_2$ be the bipartite graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$ by deleting a perfect matching, and let $cr(G)$ denote the crossing number of a graph $G$.

**Crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
cr(K_{n,n}-nK_2)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture gives an exact formula for the crossing number of the crown graph. The paper establishes matching upper and substantially weaker lower bounds in general, and proves the formula for $n=5$; the general equality remains open in the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Yuansheng Yang, Baigong Zheng, Xiaohui Lin and Xirong Xu, “The crossing numbers of K_n,n-nK_2, K_nP_2, K_nP_3 and K_nC_4”, arXiv:1211.4437 (2012).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

R027.title: The geometric-solution conjecture for the complex volume of hyperbolic knots
R027.statement:
Let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot, and let $x$ be an algebraic solution of the periodicity equations associated with the braid-induced triangulation of $S^3\setminus K$. For the $j$th octahedron, let $[\overset{k_j\phantom{\varepsilon}}{\mathsf{R}^{\varepsilon_j}}]$ denote its corresponding data, let $\boldsymbol{x}[j]$ denote the associated variables, and let $\operatorname{L}([\overset{k_j\phantom{\varepsilon}}{\mathsf{R}^{\varepsilon_j}}];\boldsymbol{x}[j])$ be the dilogarithm function defined in the paper. The complex volume of $K$ is $\mathrm{i}(\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)+\mathrm{i}\operatorname{CS}(S^3\setminus K))$. **Complex-volume conjecture.** There exists an algebraic solution of the periodicity equations such that

$$
\mathrm{i}\left(\operatorname{Vol}(S^3\setminus K)+\mathrm{i}\operatorname{CS}(S^3\setminus K)\right)=\sum_{j=1}^m\operatorname{L}([\overset{k_j\phantom{\varepsilon}}{\mathsf{R}^{\varepsilon_j}}];\boldsymbol{x}[j]).
$$

The expected solution is geometric: the additional two points have canceling neighbors and determine a complete hyperbolic structure on $S^3\setminus K$. Numerical examples are discussed, but the authors state that they do not know how to extract such a preferred solution in general from the periodicity equations.
R027.source_name: Kazuhiro Hikami and Rei Inoue, “Braids, Complex Volume, and Cluster Algebra”, arXiv:1304.4776 (2014).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.4776

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

R027.title: Conjectured crossing numbers for $K_{1,1,3,n}$ and $K_{2,4,n}$
R027.statement:
Let $K_{a_1,a_2,a_3,n}$ denote the complete multipartite graph whose parts have sizes $a_1,a_2,a_3,n$, let $K_{2,4,n}$ denote the complete multipartite graph with parts of sizes $2$, $4$, and $n$, and let $cr(G)$ be the crossing number of a graph $G$. Let $Z(m,n)$ denote the Zarankiewicz expression

$$
Z(m,n)=\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{m-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$
 **The crossing-number conjectures.** For the relevant positive integer $n$,

$$
cr(K_{1,1,3,n})=Z(5,n)+\left\lfloor\frac{3n}{2}\right\rfloor;
$$

$$
cr(K_{2,4,n})=Z(6,n)+2n.
$$

These are proposed in the paper's conclusion as further crossing-number formulas; the source provides no resolution.
R027.source_name: Pak Tung Ho, “On the crossing number of some complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:1310.4381 (2013).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.4381

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

R027.title: Sano–Mazur–Rubin higher-norm conjecture for Rubin–Stark elements
R027.statement:
