Let $K/L/k$ be a tower of finite extensions of global fields with $K/k$ abelian, let $S$ and $T$ satisfy the paper's standing conditions, and let $V\subset V'\subset S$ be proper subsets such that every place in $V$ splits completely in $K$ and every place in $V'$ splits completely in $L$. Let $\varepsilon_{K,S,T,V}$ and $\varepsilon_{L,S,T,V'}$ be the corresponding Rubin–Stark elements, let $\mathcal{N}_{K/L}$ be the higher norm, let $\nu_{K/L}$ be the canonical injection, and let $\varphi_v$ be the reciprocity-induced maps for $v\in V'\setminus V$. **Sano–Mazur–Rubin conjecture.** The higher norm belongs to the image of the canonical injection and satisfies

$$
\mathcal{N}_{K/L}(\varepsilon_{K,S,T,V})\in\operatorname{im}\nu_{K/L},
$$

and

$$
\nu_{K/L}^{-1}(\mathcal{N}_{K/L}(\varepsilon_{K,S,T,V}))=\operatorname{sgn}(V',V)\left(\bigwedge_{v\in V'\setminus V}\varphi_v\right)(\varepsilon_{L,S,T,V'}).
$$

This is the conjecture proposed by Sano and, essentially equivalently, by Mazur and Rubin. The paper proves it in a special case; the displayed formulation is also equivalent to the original formulation in the case $r=0$.
R027.source_name: Takamichi Sano, “On a conjecture for Rubin-Stark elements in a special case”, arXiv:1406.4940 (2014).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.4940

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2014).

R027.title: The rectilinear crossing-number formula for complete tripartite graphs
R027.statement:
Let $n_1,n_2,n_3\geq 1$, and let $K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $n_1,n_2,n_3$. Its rectilinear crossing number, denoted by $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})$, is the minimum number of crossings in a drawing in which every edge is a straight line segment. Let $A(n_1,n_2,n_3)$ be the upper-bound expression defined in the paper.

**Rectilinear crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})=A(n_1,n_2,n_3).
$$

The preceding upper and lower bounds provide evidence for this formula, which is known in several cases where two parts are small but remains open in general.
R027.source_name: Ellen Gethner, Leslie Hogben, Bernard Lidický, Florian Pfender, Amanda Ruiz and Michael Young, “Crossing numbers of complete tripartite and balanced complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:1410.0720 (2014).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0720

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

R027.title: The crossing-number equality conjecture for complete tripartite graphs
R027.statement:
Let $n_1,n_2,n_3\geq 1$, and let $K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $n_1,n_2,n_3$. Write $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ for the crossing number of a graph $G$, and $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(G)$ for its rectilinear crossing number, the minimum number of crossings in a straight-line drawing of $G$.

**Crossing-number equality conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3})=\operatorname{cr}(K_{n_1,n_2,n_3}).
$$

Since every rectilinear drawing is a planar drawing, the left-hand side is always at least the ordinary crossing number. The conjecture asserts that complete tripartite graphs always admit optimal straight-line drawings; the supplied context gives evidence from the preceding bounds but no resolution.
R027.source_name: Ellen Gethner, Leslie Hogben, Bernard Lidický, Florian Pfender, Amanda Ruiz and Michael Young, “Crossing numbers of complete tripartite and balanced complete multipartite graphs”, arXiv:1410.0720 (2014).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.0720

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

R027.title: Percival's conjecture for mixed dynamical systems
R027.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with flow domain $\mathcal{D}$, and suppose that $\mathcal{D}$ is the disjoint union of two invariant subsets $U$ and $\mathcal{D}\setminus U$, where $U$ is ergodic and $\mathcal{D}\setminus U$ is integrable. Let $(u_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a complete system of eigenfunctions of the Laplace--Beltrami operator. **Percival's conjecture.** There exist subsets $A,B\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
A\cup B\text{ has density }1,
$$

$(u_k)_{k\in A}$ equidistributes in the ergodic region $U$, every semiclassical measure associated to the subset $B$ is supported in the completely integrable region $\mathcal{D}\setminus U$, and

$$
\operatorname{dens}(A)=\mu_L(U).
$$

This conjecture predicts a spectral decomposition reflecting the ergodic and integrable components of a mixed dynamical system. In particular, the natural densities of the two subsets of eigenfunctions should be proportional to the Liouville measures of the corresponding invariant regions; the paper presents the Bunimovich mushroom billiard as a model case where a satisfactory general analogue of quantum ergodicity is not yet known.
R027.source_name: Sean Gomes, “Percival's Conjecture for the Bunimovich Mushroom Billiard”, arXiv:1504.07332 (2016).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.07332

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

R027.title: Moment-curve extremality conjecture for crossing pairs in convex drawings
R027.statement:
Let $K_n^d$ be the complete $d$-uniform hypergraph, and let a **$d$-dimensional convex drawing** of $K_n^d$ place its $n$ vertices in convex position in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with each hyperedge represented by the simplex spanned by its vertices. The **$d$-dimensional moment curve** is the curve $\{(t,t^2,\ldots,t^d):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$.

**Moment-curve extremality conjecture.** Placing the $n$ vertices on the $d$-dimensional moment curve maximizes the number of crossing pairs of hyperedges among all $d$-dimensional convex drawings of $K_n^d$.

The conjecture concerns the extremal crossing behavior of convex drawings of complete uniform hypergraphs. The paper states that for $d>3$ it is an open problem to prove or disprove it; the exact values of the $d$-dimensional convex crossing number of $K_{2d}^d$ are likewise not known for $d>3$.
R027.source_name: Anurag Anshu, Rahul Gangopadhyay, Saswata Shannigrahi and Satyanarayana Vusirikala, “On the Rectilinear Crossing Number of Complete Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1512.01335 (2016).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01335

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2015). “For $d > 3$, it is also an exciting open problem to prove or disprove the following conjecture.”

R027.title: The anchor-cell excess conjecture for canonical systems on metric graphs with skeleton K_4
R027.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a metric graph whose skeleton is the complete graph $K_4$, and let $D=K$ be its canonical divisor. Write $|D|$ for the associated linear system, and call the cells in $|D|$ anchor cells and vertices in $|D|$ vertices. **Anchor-cell excess conjecture.** The number of anchor cells in $|D|$ minus the number of vertices in $|D|$ is always $16$. This is an observed computational pattern for the listed metrics on $K_4$; whether it holds for every metric on a trivalent graph with skeleton $K_4$ remains to be established.
R027.source_name: Bo Lin, “Computing Linear Systems on Metric Graphs”, arXiv:1603.00547 (2016).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.00547

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2016).

R027.title: Blažek–Koman conjecture for the $k$-page book crossing number of $K_n$
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $\nu_k(K_n)$ denote its $k$-page book crossing number. Define

$$
F(r,n):=\frac{r}{24}(r^2-3r+2)(2n-3-r)
$$

and

$$
Z_k(n):=(n\bmod k)\cdot F\left(\left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor+1,n\right)+(k-(n\bmod k))\cdot F\left(\left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor,n\right).
$$

**Blažek–Koman conjecture.** For any positive integers $k$ and $n$,

$$
\nu_k(K_n)=Z_k(n).
$$

The quantity $Z_k(n)$ is the crossing count of standard constructions generalizing the Blažek–Koman construction. These constructions are widely believed to be asymptotically correct, but the exact equality is presented here as a conjecture.
R027.source_name: Bernardo M. Ábrego, Julia Dandurand, Silvia Fernández-Merchant, Evgeniya Lagoda and Yakov Sapozhnikov, “Book crossing numbers of the complete graph and small local convex crossing numbers”, arXiv:1607.00131 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00131

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

R027.title: Classification conjecture for finite filled groups
R027.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. A subset $S\subseteq G$ is **product-free** if $S\cap SS=\emptyset$, and it is **complete** if $G^{\ast}\subseteq S\cup SS$, where $G^{\ast}=G\setminus\{1\}$. A product-free set is **locally maximal** if it is not contained in a strictly larger product-free set. The group $G$ is **filled** if every locally maximal product-free subset of $G$ is complete. Write $C_m$ for the cyclic group of order $m$, $D_m$ for the dihedral group of order $m$, and $Q_8$ for the quaternion group of order $8$; $D_8\ast Q_8$ denotes their central product.

**Classification conjecture.** The group $G$ is filled if and only if $G$ is either an elementary abelian $2$-group or one of

$$
C_3,\ C_5,\ D_6,\ D_8,\ D_{10},\ D_{12},\ D_{14},\ D_8\times C_2,\ D_{22},\ D_8\ast Q_8,\ (D_8\ast Q_8)\times C_2.
$$

The authors report that this list agrees with computations in the small groups library through order $2000$, but the stated classification is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied in the given text.
R027.source_name: Chimere S. Anabanti, Grahame Erskine and Sarah B. Hart, “Groups whose locally maximal product-free sets are complete”, arXiv:1609.09662 (2016).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09662

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2016). “The conjecture was disproved by two of the current authors in , where we also classified the filled groups of odd order.”

R027.title: Ciocan-Fontanine–Kim higher-genus quasimap wall-crossing conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $Z$ be a complete intersection in projective space, and fix $g,n\geq 0$. For each effective degree $\beta$, let $q^\beta$ be the corresponding Novikov monomial, let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}^{\epsilon}_{g,n}(Z,\beta)$ and $\overline{\mathcal{M}}^{\infty}_{g,n}(Z,\beta)$ denote the moduli spaces of $\epsilon$-stable and $\infty$-stable quasimaps, respectively, and let $\mu^{\epsilon}_{\beta}(z)$ be the relevant coefficients of the $I$-function of $Z$. For a tuple $\vec{\beta}=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_k)$, let $b_{\vec{\beta}}$ convert the additional marked points to basepoints, and let $c$ be the contraction morphism from $\infty$-stable to $\epsilon$-stable quasimaps. **Ciocan-Fontanine–Kim's higher-genus wall-crossing conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{\beta}q^\beta[\overline{\mathcal{M}}^{\epsilon}_{g,n}(Z,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}}=
\sum_{\beta_0,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_k}\frac{q^{\beta_0}}{k!}(b_{\vec{\beta}})_*c_*\left(\prod_{i=1}^kq^{\beta_i}\operatorname{ev}_{n+i}^*(\mu^{\epsilon}_{\beta_i}(-\psi_{n+i}))\cap[\overline{\mathcal{M}}^{\infty}_{g,n+k}(Z,\beta_0)]^{\mathrm{vir}}\right).
$$

More generally, if $Z=W\mathbin{/\!/_{\theta}}G$ for a complex affine variety $W$ and a reductive algebraic group $G$, there should be an explicit formula, depending only on coefficients of the $I$-function of $Z$, relating the virtual fundamental cycles of the moduli spaces of $\epsilon$-stable and $\infty$-stable quasimaps to $Z$. This is a proposed higher-genus extension of genus-zero quasimap wall-crossing; the displayed formula is presented as a conjecture, while the paper's abstract states that it proves the formula for complete intersections in projective space. The broader GIT-quotient formulation remains conjectural in the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Emily Clader, Felix Janda and Yongbin Ruan, “Higher-genus quasimap wall-crossing via localization”, arXiv:1702.03427 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03427

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

R027.title: Bounded-path partition conjecture for $K^*_{s,t}$-minor-free graphs
R027.statement:
For positive integers $s$ and $t$, let $K^*_{s,t}$ be the complete join of $K_s$ and $\overline{K_t}$. A **connected partition of width $s-1$** is a partition $H_1,\dots,H_\ell$ into connected subgraphs with quotient width $s-1$ in the sense used by the source. A shortest path is a path shortest in the indicated vertex-deleted graph.

**Bounded-path partition conjecture.** For all $t\geqslant s\geqslant1$, there exists an integer $p$ such that every $K^*_{s,t}$-minor-free graph $G$ has a connected partition $H_1,\dots,H_\ell$ with width $s-1$, such that for $i\in[\ell]$,

$$
V(H_i)=V(P_{i,1})\cup\dots\cup V(P_{i,p_i}),
$$

where $p_i\leqslant p$ and each $P_{i,j}$ is a shortest path in

$$
G-\Bigl(\bigl(V(H_1)\cup\dots\cup V(H_{i-1})\bigr)\cup\bigl(V(P_{i,1})\cup\dots\cup V(P_{i,j-1})\bigr)\Bigr).
$$

The source says that this conjecture would imply the polynomial weak colouring-number conjecture together with the preceding BFS-colouring lemma. Its resolution status is not given.
R027.source_name: Jan van den Heuvel and David R. Wood, “Improper Colourings inspired by Hadwiger's Conjecture”, arXiv:1704.06536 (2018).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06536

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2017). “The conjecture remains open for $t\geq7$.”

R027.title: Donald's existence conjecture for stable toric triples
R027.statement: Let $(\Delta,\mathbf L)$ be the momentum polytope of a smooth compact toric Kähler manifold $(X,\omega_0)$, let $F$ be a fixed union of facets of $\Delta$, and let $Z\subset X$ be the divisor corresponding to the momentum preimage of $F$. The triple $(\Delta,\mathbf L,F)$ is stable when it satisfies the nonnegativity condition for the associated functional on convex piecewise affine-linear functions, with equality only for affine-linear functions. **Donald's conjecture.** If $(\Delta,\mathbf L,F)$ is stable, then there exists a complete extremal Kähler metric $g_D$ on $X\setminus Z$. This is a toric existence conjecture relating the stability of the labelled polytope with complete extremal metrics on the complement of the associated divisor; the source does not state a resolution.
R027.source_name: Vestislav Apostolov, Hugues Auvray and Lars Martin Sektnan, “Extremal Kähler Poincaré type metrics on toric varieties”, arXiv:1711.08424 (2017).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08424

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

R027.title: Unique rectification targets in d-complete posets
R027.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a $d$-complete poset and let $\lambda \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ be an order ideal. A rectification target is an increasing $\mathcal{P}$-tableau obtained as the result of rectifying a skew increasing tableau. **Unique rectification target conjecture.** There is an explicitly defined unique rectification target supported on $\lambda$. This conjecture asks whether general $d$-complete posets have enough unique rectification targets to extend the Thomas–Yong jeu de taquin theory beyond minuscule varieties; the precise formulation identifies the target with the minimally labeled tableau described below.
R027.source_name: Rahul Ilango, Oliver Pechenik and Michael Zlatin, “Unique rectification in d-complete posets: towards the K-theory of Kac-Moody flag varieties”, arXiv:1805.02287 (2018).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

R027.title: The rectilinear crossing-number conjecture for complete uniform hypergraphs
R027.statement:
Let $K_{2d}^d$ be the complete $d$-uniform hypergraph on $2d$ vertices, and let $\overline {cr}_d(K_{2d}^d)$ denote its rectilinear crossing number in $d$ dimensions. **Rectilinear crossing-number conjecture.**

$$
\overline {cr}_d(K_{2d}^d)=\Omega (2^d \sqrt{d}).
$$

The paper proves this lower bound for several placements of the vertices, but the conjecture concerns the rectilinear crossing number in general. The preceding discussion establishes only the weaker bound $\overline {cr}_d(K_{2d}^d)=\Omega(2^d)$, so the conjectured improvement remains unresolved in the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Rahul Gangopadhyay and Saswata Shannigrahi, “k-Sets and Rectilinear Crossings in Complete Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:1806.02574 (2019).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02574

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

R027.title: Conjecture on normals of complete minimal surfaces with planar ends
R027.statement: Let $X:\Sigma\setminus\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}\to\mathbb{R}^3$ be a complete minimal surface with $m$ embedded planar ends $\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}$. Let $n_X(p_i)$ denote the normal at the end $p_i$, and set $d=\dim\operatorname{span}\{n_X(p_i):i=1,\ldots,m\}$. **Normals-at-the-ends conjecture.** The normals at the ends span $\mathbb{R}^3$, that is, $d=3$. This conjecture would imply that the Morse index formula for unbranched Willmore spheres has the expected value for the associated minimal surfaces; the paper proves the assertion when there are four embedded planar ends, but its validity for arbitrary $m$ remains open.
R027.source_name: Jonas Hirsch and Elena Mäder-Baumdicker, “On the Index of Willmore spheres”, arXiv:1905.04185 (2019).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.04185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

R027.title: The fixed-arc deletion algorithm conjecture for semicomplete digraphs
R027.statement:
Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer. A **semicomplete digraph** is a directed graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by at least one arc. A **spanning eulerian subdigraph** is a subdigraph containing every vertex in which each vertex has equal indegree and outdegree. For a semicomplete digraph $D=(V,A)$ and a set $A'\subset A$, write $D\setminus A'$ for the digraph obtained by deleting the arcs in $A'$.

**Fixed-arc deletion algorithm conjecture.** For each fixed positive integer $k$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm which, given a semicomplete digraph $D=(V,A)$ and $A'\subset A$ with $|A'|=k$, decides whether $D\setminus A'$ has a spanning eulerian subdigraph.

The paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm when one arc is deleted and conjectures that this tractability extends to every fixed number of deleted arcs. The general fixed-$k$ case remains open.
R027.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Frédéric Havet and Anders Yeeo, “Spanning eulerian subdigraphs in semicomplete digraphs”, arXiv:1905.11019 (2019).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.11019

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

R027.title: Almost-everywhere completeness conjecture for the triple-junction singular basis
R027.statement:
Let $Y$ be the parameter domain for $(\theta_{1},\theta_{2},a,b)$, let $\mathcal{J}$ index the boundary-data components, and let $\beta_{i,j}$ and $\boldsymbol v_{i,j}$ denote the singular exponents and corresponding null vectors. Assume that $\beta_{i,j}:Y\to\mathbb{R}$ are analytic. For real constants $h_{(i,j)}^{k}$, define

$$
h_{(i,j)}(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{N}h_{(i,j)}^{k}t^{k},\qquad 0<t<1.
$$

**Completeness conjecture.** There exists a measure-zero set $S$ such that, for every $(\theta_{1},\theta_{2},a,b)\in Y\setminus S$, there are constants $p_{i,j}$, $i=0,1,\ldots,N$, $j=0,1,2$, for which

$$
\sigma(t)=\begin{bmatrix}\sigma_{1,2}(t)\\sigma_{2,3}(t)\\sigma_{3,1}(t)\end{bmatrix}=\sum_{i=0}^{N}\sum_{j=0}^{2}p_{i,j}\boldsymbol v_{i,j}t^{\beta_{i,j}}
$$

satisfies

$$
\max_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{J}}\left|h_{(i,j)}(t)-\mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{dir}}[\sigma]_{(i,j)}(t)\right|\leq Ct^{N+1},
$$

for $0<t<1$, where $C$ is a constant. The conjecture extends the proved completeness result from neighborhoods of the parameter lines $a=0$, $b=0$, and $c=0$ to all parameters outside a measure-zero exceptional set; the source identifies the exceptional set with parameter values where root multiplicity and null-space dimension disagree.
R027.source_name: Jeremy Hoskins and Manas Rachh, “On the solution of Laplace's equation in the vicinity of triple-junctions”, arXiv:1907.10718 (2020).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10718

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

R027.title: The sine-process hereditary completeness conjecture
R027.statement: Let $X$ be a configuration sampled from the sine process, with law denoted by ${{\mathbb P}_{\mathscr S}}$, and let $p\in X$ be a particle. A set is **hereditarily complete** if every bounded measurable partition of it yields a complete system of reproducing kernels in the associated Paley–Wiener space. **The sine-process hereditary completeness conjecture.** For ${{\mathbb P}_{\mathscr S}}$-almost every configuration $X$ and any particle $p\in X$, the set $X\setminus p$ is hereditarily complete. The paper's main theorem establishes uniqueness after removing one particle, but the stronger hereditary-completeness assertion is not resolved in the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Alexander I. Bufetov, “The sine-process has excess one”, arXiv:1912.13454 (2019).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.13454

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

R027.title: Conjecture on 1-connected minimal diagrams of reducible handlebody links
R027.statement:
Let $L$ be a non-split, reducible handlebody link, and let a **minimal diagram** be a diagram realizing its crossing number. A diagram has **$1$-connectivity** when its connectivity is one in the terminology of the paper.

**Reducible-handlebody-link conjecture.** Every non-split, reducible handlebody link admits a minimal diagram with $1$-connectivity.

The conjecture is motivated by the complete classification of the relevant non-split, reducible $(n,1)$-handlebody links through six crossings. The source notes that not every minimal diagram of a reducible handlebody link has $1$-connectivity and gives no general resolution.
R027.source_name: Giovanni Bellettini, Giovanni Paolini, Maurizio Paolini and Yi-Sheng Wang, “A table of n-component handlebody links of genus n+1 up to six crossings”, arXiv:2003.03748 (2020).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.03748

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

R027.title: The asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture for crossing numbers
R027.statement:
Let $cr(K_{n,n})$ be the crossing number of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $cr_0(K_{n,n})$ be its geodesic crossing number. Define

$$
\lambda:= \lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-4} cr(K_{n,n})
$$

and

$$
\lambda_0:= \lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-4} cr_0(K_{n,n}).
$$

The limits exist, and satisfy $\lambda \leq \lambda_0 \leq \tfrac{1}{16}$. **Asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture.**

$$
\lambda = \lambda_0 = \tfrac{1}{16}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the Zarankiewicz construction is asymptotically optimal both for the usual crossing number and for the geodesic crossing number. The source states that the conjecture remains open.
R027.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Bojan Mohar and Alexandra Wesolek, “Limiting crossing numbers for geodesic drawings on the sphere”, arXiv:2008.10459 (2020).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10459

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

R027.title: The complete intersection characterization of cyclotomic numerical semigroups
R027.statement:
A **numerical semigroup** is a cofinite additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$. It is **complete intersection** when the cardinality of its minimal presentation equals its embedding dimension minus one, and it is **cyclotomic** when its cyclotomic exponent sequence $\mathbf{e}$ has finite support.

**Cyclotomic complete intersection conjecture.** A numerical semigroup is a complete intersection if and only if it is cyclotomic.

This conjecture was checked for numerical semigroups with Frobenius number at most $70$ using the GAP package `numericalsgps`; its general status is not established in the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Alexandru Ciolan, Pedro A. García-Sánchez, Andrés Herrera-Poyatos and Pieter Moree, “Cyclotomic exponent sequences of numerical semigroups”, arXiv:2101.08826 (2021).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.08826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

R027.title: Completeness conjecture for Kähler–Einstein metrics near isolated log canonical singularities
R027.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{U},p)$ be the germ of an isolated log canonical, non-log-terminal singularity, and let $g_{KE}$ be a Kähler–Einstein metric constructed in Theorem 1.1 on $\mathcal{U}\setminus\{p\}$. For a fixed point $q\in\mathcal{U}\setminus\{p\}$ and $R>0$, consider paths in $\mathcal{U}\setminus\{p\}$ joining $q$ to points approaching $p$.

**Completeness conjecture.** The metric $g_{KE}$ is complete near $p$; more precisely, there is an open neighborhood $V_{q,R}$ of $p$ such that for every $x\in V_{q,R}\setminus\{p\}$ and every smooth path $\gamma$ joining $q$ and $x$ in $\mathcal{U}\setminus\{p\}$,

$$
|\gamma|_{g_{KE}}>R,
$$

where $|\gamma|_{g_{KE}}$ denotes the arc length of $\gamma$ with respect to $g_{KE}$.

This conjecture asks whether the finite-volume Kähler–Einstein metric constructed near an isolated log canonical singularity is nevertheless metrically complete toward the singular point. The paper proposes this as the geometric question governing the behavior of the metric near $p$, and does not resolve it in general.
R027.source_name: Ved Datar, Xin Fu and Jian Song, “Kahler-Einstein metric near an isolated log canonical singularity”, arXiv:2106.05486 (2022).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05486

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

R027.title: The converse vanishing theorem in Verdier quotients of stable categories
R027.statement:
Assume $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is a complete local complete intersection of dimension $d$ and codimension $c$, with algebraically closed residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $X$ be an algebraic set in $\mathbb P^{c-1}(k)$, let $\mathcal T_X=\operatorname{\underline{CM}}(A)/\mathcal S_X$, and let $M,N$ be maximal Cohen–Macaulay $A$-modules. Write $\mathcal V_X(M)=\mathcal V^*(M)\setminus X$. **The converse vanishing conjecture.** If

$$
\mathcal V_X(M)\cap\mathcal V_X(N)=\emptyset,
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(M,\Omega^{-n}(N))=0\quad\text{for all }n\gg0.
$$

The paper proves this implication when $M$ or $N$ is essentially disjoint from $X$, while the conjecture asks for it without that additional assumption. The forward implication is established generally, so the open issue is precisely the converse.
R027.source_name: Tony J. Puthenpurakal, “Support Varieties and cohomology of Verdier quotients of stable category of complete intersection rings”, arXiv:2108.00204 (2021).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00204

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

R027.title: The weakened Roberts conjecture for cubic Hurwitz stacks
R027.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not dividing $6$, let $g$ be the genus, and let $\mathrm{Hur}_{3,g,k}$ be the degree-$3$ Hurwitz stack. Write $\mathbb L$ for the class of the affine line and $\widehat{\widetilde{K_0}}(\operatorname{Stacks}_k)$ for the completed Grothendieck ring of stacks. Equality modulo codimension $r$ means that the difference lies in the filtered part of dimension at most the common dimension minus $r$. **The weakened Roberts conjecture.**

$$
\frac{\{\mathrm{Hur}_{3,g,k}\}}{\mathbb L^{\dim \mathrm{Hur}_{3,g,k}}}\equiv (1+\mathbb L^{-1})(1-\mathbb L^{-3})
$$

modulo codimension $\frac{g-1}{3}$ in $\widehat{\widetilde{K_0}}(\operatorname{Stacks}_k)$. This is a motivic analogue of the second-order asymptotic for cubic fields, obtained by weakening the codimension predicted by Roberts' conjecture; the source presents it as the next statement to be established in the Grothendieck-ring setting.
R027.source_name: Aaron Landesman, Ravi Vakil and Melanie Matchett Wood, “Low degree Hurwitz stacks in the Grothendieck ring”, arXiv:2203.01840 (2025).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01840

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2022). “This was proved in and independently.”

R027.title: The plane-path conjecture for complete simple topological graphs
R027.statement:
A **simple topological graph** is a graph drawn in the plane so that vertices are distinct points, edges are simple arcs joining their endpoints, no edge contains a vertex other than its endpoints, and every pair of edges intersects at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A **plane path** is a path whose edges are pairwise noncrossing. The length of a path is its number of edges.

**Plane-path conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph contains a plane path of length $n^{\varepsilon}$.

This conjecture asks for a polynomial-length plane path in every complete simple topological graph. The context notes that related results guarantee many pairwise disjoint edges, but the corresponding polynomial bound for plane paths remains open.
R027.source_name: Andrew Suk and Ji Zeng, “Unavoidable patterns in complete simple topological graphs”, arXiv:2204.04293 (2022).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

R027.title: The crossing-degree conjecture for complete simple topological graphs
R027.statement:
Let $h=h(n)$ be the smallest integer such that every complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph contains an edge crossing at most $h$ other edges. A **simple topological graph** is a graph drawn in the plane so that vertices are distinct points, edges are simple arcs joining their endpoints, no edge contains a vertex other than its endpoints, and every pair of edges intersects at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing.

**Crossing-degree conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that

$$
h(n)\leq n^{2-\varepsilon}.
$$

The source records the lower bound $h(n)=\Omega(n^{3/2})$ and upper bounds of order $n^2/(\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}$. The conjecture seeks a polynomial improvement over the quadratic upper bound and remains open.
R027.source_name: Andrew Suk and Ji Zeng, “Unavoidable patterns in complete simple topological graphs”, arXiv:2204.04293 (2022).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

R027.title: NP-completeness of the planar graph square-root problem
R027.statement:
A graph $G$ is **planar** if it can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings. For a graph class $\mathcal{H}$, the $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem asks whether a given graph has a square root belonging to $\mathcal{H}$.

**Planar square-root conjecture.** The $\mathcal{H}$-square-root problem is NP-complete for the class $\mathcal{H}$ of planar graphs.

The paper proves NP-completeness for the class of $6$-apex graphs, which is minor-closed and lies at the bottom of the bounded-expansion hierarchy. It remains open whether the apex vertices are necessary, or whether the planar square-root problem is already hard.
R027.source_name: Zdeněk Dvořák, Benjamin Moore and Abhiruk Lahiri, “Square roots of nearly planar graphs”, arXiv:2205.12764 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

R027.title: Grothendieck's finite generation conjecture for punctured-spectrum fundamental groups
R027.statement:
Let $A$ be a complete noetherian local ring with algebraically closed residue field $F$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. Let $p$ be the characteristic of $F$ if it is positive and let $p = 1$ otherwise. Assume that the irreducible components of $\operatorname{Spec} A$ have dimension at least $2$, and that the scheme $\operatorname{Spec} A \setminus \{\mathfrak{m}\}$ is connected.

**Grothendieck's conjecture.** The following statements hold:

1. The étale fundamental group $\pi_{1}(\operatorname{Spec} A \setminus \{\mathfrak{m}\})$ is topologically finitely generated.
2. The maximal pro-prime-to-$p$ quotient of $\pi_{1}(\operatorname{Spec} A \setminus \{\mathfrak{m}\})$ is topologically finitely presented.

The conjecture, made in SGA 2, concerns the finiteness properties of the étale fundamental group of a punctured spectrum. The paper proves the weaker assertion that the maximal pro-nilpotent quotient is topologically finitely generated, so the two stated finiteness claims remain unresolved here.
R027.source_name: Takashi Suzuki, “Finite generation of nilpotent quotients of fundamental groups of punctured spectra”, arXiv:2207.01563 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.01563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

R027.title: Bucko–Czap conjecture on 1-planarity of lexicographic products
R027.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph with two vertices. A graph is **1-planar** if it has a drawing in the plane in which every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. A **cactus** is a connected graph in which every edge belongs to at most one cycle. **Bucko–Czap's conjecture.** The graph $G\circ K_2$ is 1-planar if and only if $G$ is a cactus. This open problem characterizes 1-planarity for lexicographic products with $K_2$ and concerns the relationship between graph substitution and sparse crossing structures.
R027.source_name: Licheng Zhang and Yuanqiu Huang, “The reducibility of optimal 1-planar graphs”, arXiv:2211.14733 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14733

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022). “So the study of 1-planarity of the lexicographic products of graphs only leaves the following open problem.”

R027.title: The d-complete-poset LE-cactus conjecture
R027.statement: Let $P$ be a d-complete poset. A poset is **LE-cactus** when its Bender–Knuth group action on its linear extensions satisfies the cactus relations. **The d-complete-poset LE-cactus conjecture.** Every d-complete poset is LE-cactus. This extends the verified result for minuscule posets and other motivating families; the general case remains open.
R027.source_name: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall, Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki and Janabel Xia, “Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets”, arXiv:2302.12425 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12425

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023).

R027.title: The convex-drawing extension conjecture for plane Hamiltonian cycles
R027.statement:
Let $D$ be a convex drawing of the complete graph $K_n$, and let $C$ be a plane Hamiltonian cycle in $D$. A **plane Hamiltonian subdrawing** is a crossing-free subdrawing spanning all vertices.

**Convex-drawing extension conjecture.** Every plane Hamiltonian cycle $C$ in $D$ can be extended to a plane Hamiltonian subdrawing on $2n-3$ edges.

The conjecture asks whether every prescribed plane Hamiltonian cycle in a convex drawing can be enlarged to the target-size subdrawing. The paper reports that this holds computationally for convex drawings with $n\leq 10$, while the analogous assertion fails for general simple drawings.
R027.source_name: Helena Bergold, Stefan Felsner, Meghana M. Reddy and Manfred Scheucher, “Using SAT to study plane Hamiltonian substructures in simple drawings”, arXiv:2305.09432 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.09432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

R027.title: The shtuka cohomology conjecture for proper rigid-analytic varieties
R027.statement:
Let $C$ be the completed algebraic closure of a $p$-adic field, let $\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}}=\operatorname{Spa}(A_{\inf},A_{\inf})\setminus V([p^{\flat}])$, and let $A$ be the ring of analytic functions on $\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}}$. A shtuka of perfect complexes relative to $\operatorname{Spa}\mathbb{Z}_p$ with one leg at $\varphi^{-1}(y_C)$ is a perfect complex $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}}$ equipped with an isomorphism

$$
\varphi_{\mathcal{E}}:(\varphi^*\mathcal{E})|_{\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}}\setminus\{\varphi^{-1}(y_C)\}}\cong \mathcal{E}|_{\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}}\setminus\{\varphi^{-1}(y_C)\}}
$$

that is meromorphic at $\varphi^{-1}(y_C)$. **The shtuka cohomology conjecture.** There exists a cohomology theory $R\Gamma_{\operatorname{sht}}(X/\mathcal{Y}_{\operatorname{FF}})$ for proper rigid-analytic varieties $X$ over $C$, taking values in such shtukas, satisfying: (i) if $X$ is the generic fiber of a proper $p$-adic formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}$ over $\mathcal{O}_C$ with semistable reduction, it is naturally isomorphic to the shtuka associated to $R\Gamma_{A_{\inf}}(\mathfrak{X})\otimes_{A_{\inf}}A$; and (ii) after restriction to $Y_{\operatorname{FF}}$, its cohomology groups are shtukas of vector bundles whose associated admissible modification corresponds, via Fargues' equivalence, to the modification defined by the de Rham lattice. This would provide a direct geometric shtuka-valued cohomology theory for proper rigid-analytic varieties and relate it to $A_{\inf}$-cohomology; the source gives no evidence of a resolution.
R027.source_name: Guido Bosco, “Rational p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties”, arXiv:2306.06100 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

R027.title: The generalized volume conjecture near the complete hyperbolic structure
R027.statement:
Let $\mathscr{H}$ be a hyperbolic knot. Let $\rho_u\colon\pi_1(S^3\setminus\mathscr{H})\to\operatorname{SL}(2;\mathbb{C})$ be an irreducible representation that is a small deformation of the holonomy representation $\rho_0$. Let $T_u(\mathscr{H})$ be the corresponding cohomological adjoint Reidemeister torsion, let $v(u)$ be determined by the meridian and preferred-longitude holonomies, and define

$$
S_u(\mathscr{H})=\operatorname{CS}_{u,v(u)}(\rho_u)+u\pi\sqrt{-1}+\frac{uv(u)}{4}.
$$

**Generalized volume conjecture.** For a hyperbolic knot $\mathscr{H}$, there exists a neighbourhood $U\in\mathbb{C}$ of $0$ such that, if $u\in U\setminus\pi\sqrt{-1}\mathbb{Q}$, then

$$
J_N(\mathscr{H};e^{(u+2\pi\sqrt{-1})/N})\underset{N\to\infty}{\sim}\frac{\sqrt{-\pi}}{2\sinh(u/2)}T_u(\mathscr{H})^{1/2}\left(\frac{N}{u+2\pi\sqrt{-1}}\right)^{1/2}\exp\left(\frac{S_u(\mathscr{H})}{u+2\pi\sqrt{-1}}N\right).
$$

This extends the refined volume conjecture by replacing the root-of-unity parameter with a nearby complex parameter and incorporating deformed Chern–Simons data and torsion. The source presents it as a conjecture proposed in the cited literature; its general status is open.
R027.source_name: Hitoshi Murakami, “The asymptotic behaviors of the colored Jones polynomials of the figure eight-knot, and an affine representation”, arXiv:2307.07100 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R027.title: The short-edge crossing-number conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $h(n)$ denote the maximum, over complete $n$-vertex simple topological graphs, of the minimum number of crossings of an edge in a suitable noncrossing matching construction. **Short-edge crossing-number conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$, 
$$
h(n)=\Theta(n^{3/2}).
$$
 This would improve the currently established bound and sharpen the quantitative understanding of short edges in complete topological graphs; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
R027.source_name: Andrew Suk, “On short edges in complete topological graphs”, arXiv:2307.08165 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R027.title: The polynomial noncrossing-path conjecture
R027.statement: A **complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph** is a drawing of the complete graph on $n$ vertices in which vertices are points and edges are simple curves, with no edge passing through a nonincident vertex and with any two edges meeting at most once. A **noncrossing path** is a path whose edges do not cross. **Polynomial noncrossing-path conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph contains a noncrossing path on $n^{\varepsilon}$ vertices. The conjecture would improve the known lower bound of order $\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$ for noncrossing paths; the source states no resolution.
R027.source_name: Andrew Suk, “On short edges in complete topological graphs”, arXiv:2307.08165 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

R027.title: The conjecture that d-complete posets are LE-cactus
R027.statement: A **d-complete poset** is a poset in the sense of the standard definition of d-completeness. A poset is **LE-cactus** when the Bender–Knuth involutions acting on its linear extensions satisfy the cactus group relations, including $(t_iq_{jk})^2=1$ for $i+1<j<k$, where $q_{jk}=q_{k-1}q_{k-j}q_{k-1}$ and $q_i=t_1(t_2t_1)\cdots(t_it_{i-1}\cdots t_1)$. **The d-complete poset conjecture.** Every d-complete poset is LE-cactus. The conjecture extends the known LE-cactus families, which include Ferrers posets, shifted Ferrers posets, rooted trees, and other minuscule posets; its resolution is not specified in the supplied source.
R027.source_name: Son Nguyen, “The Cactus Group Property for Ordinal Sums of Disjoint Unions of Chains”, arXiv:2308.07240 (2023).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07240

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

R027.title: Nonattainment conjecture for the rectilinear crossing density of the complete graphon
R027.statement:
Let $W^1$ denote the graphon of the complete graph, let $\mathcal F$ be the family of graphon drawings used to define the rectilinear crossing density, and let $\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{cd}}}(W,f)$ be the corresponding density for $f\in\mathcal F$. Write $\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{cd}}}(W^1,\mathcal D)$ for the infimum over the admissible drawing family $\mathcal D$.

**Nonattainment conjecture.** There exists no $f\in\mathcal F$ such that

$$
\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{cd}}}(W^1,\mathcal D)=\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{cd}}}(W^1,f).
$$

In particular, the infimum in

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\overline{\mathop{\mathrm{cr}}}(K_n)}{\binom{n}{4}}=\inf_{R}c(\lambda_R)
$$

can not be substituted for a minimum. This concerns whether the limiting rectilinear crossing density of complete graphs is attained by a single admissible graphon drawing, and the source presents the attainment question as unresolved.
R027.source_name: Oriol Solé-Pi, “An algorithm for estimating the crossing number of dense graphs, and continuous analogs of the crossing and rectilinear crossing numbers”, arXiv:2401.00665 (2025).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00665

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

R027.title: Aichholzer–Orthaber–Vogtenhuber's plane Hamiltonian-connectedness conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let a **simple drawing** be a drawing in which vertices are distinct points, edges are simple curves joining their endpoints and avoiding other vertices, and every two edges meet at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A **plane Hamiltonian path** is a Hamiltonian path whose edges do not cross.

**Aichholzer–Orthaber–Vogtenhuber's conjecture.** For each pair of vertices $s,t$ in a simple drawing of $K_n$, there exists a plane Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$.

This is a strengthening of Rafla's conjecture, requiring Hamiltonian paths with every prescribed pair of endpoints. The source introduces it as a variant of Rafla's conjecture; its general status remains open.
R027.source_name: Helena Bergold, Stefan Felsner, Meghana M. Reddy, Joachim Orthaber and Manfred Scheucher, “Plane Hamiltonian Cycles in Convex Drawings”, arXiv:2403.12898 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12898

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

R027.title: The $2n-3$-edge plane Hamiltonian subdrawing conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let a **simple drawing** be a drawing in which vertices are distinct points, edges are simple curves joining their endpoints and avoiding other vertices, and every two edges meet at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A **plane Hamiltonian subdrawing** is a plane subdrawing containing all $n$ vertices and a Hamiltonian cycle.

**$2n-3$-edge conjecture.** Every simple drawing of $K_n$ with $n\geq 3$ contains a plane Hamiltonian subdrawing on $2n-3$ edges.

This is the second strengthening of Rafla's conjecture stated in the conclusion. The source presents it as conjectural for general simple drawings, with computational evidence for a related weakening.
R027.source_name: Helena Bergold, Stefan Felsner, Meghana M. Reddy, Joachim Orthaber and Manfred Scheucher, “Plane Hamiltonian Cycles in Convex Drawings”, arXiv:2403.12898 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12898

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

R027.title: Fox's conjecture on crossing number and bridge number
R027.statement:
Let ${\mathcal K}$ denote the set of oriented knots, and for a knot $K$ let $c(K)$ be its crossing number and $\operatorname{bridge}(K)$ its bridge number. Define

$$
(c,\operatorname{bridge}-1)({\mathcal K})=\{(c(K),\operatorname{bridge}(K)-1)\mid K\in{\mathcal K}\}.
$$

**Fox's conjecture.**

$$
(c,\operatorname{bridge}-1)({\mathcal K})=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,y)\in({\mathbb Z}_{>0})^{2}\mid y\leq\frac{1}{3}x\}.
$$

This is the asserted complete description of the possible pairs consisting of crossing number and bridge number minus one, equivalent to the inequality $\operatorname{bridge}(K)-1\leq c(K)/3$ for every oriented knot. The source attributes the conjecture to Fox; its resolution status is not established by the supplied text.
R027.source_name: Kouki Taniyama, “Pairs of knot invariants”, arXiv:2404.09283 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09283

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R027.title: Harary–Hill conjecture for the crossing number of complete graphs
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and define

$$
H(n):=\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

Here $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ denotes the minimum number of crossings in a plane drawing of a graph $G$. **Harary–Hill conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=H(n).
$$

The formula is achieved by Hill's drawing of $K_n$ and is conjectured to be optimal; determining the crossing number of complete graphs remains a central open problem in topological graph theory.
R027.source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Rosna Paul, Jenifer Viafara-Chanchi and Alexandra Weinberger, “On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs and layered graphs”, arXiv:2404.13155 (2025).
R027.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.07796](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.07796), [arXiv:1805.06780](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06780), [arXiv:1803.07515](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07515), [arXiv:1307.3297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3297).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R027.title: Strict crossing-number separation for balanced complete 4-partite graphs
R027.statement:
Let $K_n^4$ denote the complete balanced $4$-partite graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ and $\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(G)$ denote respectively its ordinary and rectilinear crossing numbers. **4-partite separation conjecture.** There exists a natural number $n_0>9$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$,

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n^4)<\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(K_n^4).
$$

The known values and upper bounds at $n=8,9$ motivate the conjecture that, eventually, straight-line drawings require strictly more crossings than unrestricted drawings. The source does not determine such an $n_0$.
R027.source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Rosna Paul, Jenifer Viafara-Chanchi and Alexandra Weinberger, “On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs and layered graphs”, arXiv:2404.13155 (2025).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R027.title: The arc-faithful diagram conjecture for hyperbolic knots
R027.statement: Let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot, and call a diagram of $K$ **arc-faithful** when its associated octahedral coloring has the required non-pinched property and holonomy equal to the complete hyperbolic structure. **Arc-faithful diagram conjecture.** Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful diagram. The conjecture is motivated by computational evidence: every hyperbolic knot with at most $12$ crossings has an arc-faithful diagram, and such diagrams are relevant to a general proof of the Volume Conjecture.
R027.source_name: Calvin McPhail-Snyder, “Octahedral coordinates from the Wirtinger presentation”, arXiv:2404.19155 (2025).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R027.title: Kainen's conjecture for complete graphs in arbitrary surfaces
R027.statement:
For each nonnegative integer $g\neq 2$, let

$$
M(g):=\left\lceil\frac{7+\sqrt{1+48g}}{2}\right\rceil
$$

and let $S_g$ denote the orientable surface of genus $g$. A **Kainen drawing** is a drawing attaining Kainen's lower bound for the surface crossing number. **Kainen's arbitrary-surface conjecture.** For each nonnegative integer $g\neq 2$, there exists a Kainen drawing of the complete graph $K_{M(g)}$ in $S_g$. This proposed common generalization of the paper's theorem and the minimum-triangulation result remains a belief stated in the conclusion; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.
R027.source_name: Timothy Sun, “On Kainen's conjectures on surface crossing numbers”, arXiv:2405.06118 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06118

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

R027.title: Bergold–Fabila-Monroy–Roldán-Pensado–Schaefer conjecture on empty cycles in simple drawings
R027.statement:
A **simple drawing** of $K_n$ is a drawing of the complete graph in the plane with no self-intersecting edges, no crossings between adjacent edges, and at most one crossing between any pair of nonadjacent edges. A **plane cycle** is a cycle whose edges do not cross, and it divides the plane into two sides. An **empty $k$-cycle** is a plane cycle of length $k$ such that one of its sides contains no vertices in its interior. Bergold, Fabila-Monroy, Roldán-Pensado, and Schaefer conjectured that

$$
\text{every simple drawing of }K_n\text{ contains an empty }k\text{-cycle for each }3\leq k\leq n.
$$

**Bergold–Fabila-Monroy–Roldán-Pensado–Schaefer conjecture.** Every simple drawing of $K_n$ contains an empty $k$-cycle for each $3 leq k leq n$. The supplied paper proves the case $k=4$, even through every vertex, while the full assertion remains open there; the statement is known for convex drawings.
R027.source_name: Helena Bergold, Joachim Orthaber, Manfred Scheucher and Felix Schröder, “Holes in Convex and Simple Drawings”, arXiv:2409.01723 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01723

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

R027.title: Conjecture on global monodromy of the bi-degree arrangement
R027.statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers with $n\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal A_{m,n}$ be the arrangement whose linear functions are

$$
T_{(j,\ell)}(t)=-\omega_m^j(1+\omega_n^\ell t),
$$

for $(j,\ell)\in[0;m-1]\times[0;n-1]$. Let $\mathbb D_{m,n}$ be the set of parameters where two distinct such functions coincide. For $\xi\in\mathbb D_{m,n}$, let $\{\Lambda_\mu(\xi)\}_{\mu=1}^{\nu_\xi}$ be the corresponding coincidence-index sets, and let $R_{A_\mu(\xi)}$ denote the local monodromy rotation associated with $\Lambda_\mu(\xi)$. **Global monodromy conjecture.** The group of global monodromy transformations for $\mathcal A_{m,n}$ is completely determined by the local monodromies of the functions $T_{(j,\ell)}$. More precisely, if $t$ follows a loop based at $p\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb D_{m,n}$ that encircles $\xi$ and no other point of $\mathbb D_{m,n}$, then the punctures indexed by $\Lambda_\mu(\xi)$ undergo the monodromy transformation

$$
\bigl(R_{A_\mu(\xi)}\bigr)^{|\Lambda_\mu(\xi)|}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed because the rotations observed in the preceding formulas exhibit regularity; the cited main theorem establishes the analogous assertion for the arrangement $\mathcal A_{m,2}$, while the general case is presented as the basis for a future description of the global monodromy group.
R027.source_name: Susumu Tanabé, “Note sur le lieu discriminant d'une hypersurface de bi-degré (m, n).”, arXiv:2409.16479 (2024).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16479

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

R027.title: The bunkbed conjecture for graph percolation
R027.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $BB(G)$ be its bunkbed graph with two layers, whose corresponding vertices are denoted $x^-$ and $x^+$ for $x
obreak\text{ in }
obreak V(G)$. Let

$$
\mu \colon E(BB(G)) \to [0,1]
$$

be a symmetric weight on $BB(G)$, and write $\mathbb{P}_{BB(G),\mu}(u\sim v)$ for the probability that $u$ and $v$ are connected after independently retaining each edge according to its weight. **Bunkbed conjecture.** For every $x,y\in V(G)$,

$$
\mathbb{P}_{BB(G),\mu}(x^-\sim y^-)\geq \mathbb{P}_{BB(G),\mu}(x^-\sim y^+).
$$

The conjecture asserts that, under symmetric edge percolation, vertices in the same layer are at least as likely to be connected as vertices in opposite layers. The paper proves that the conjecture is preserved when graphs are glued along a vertex, with forests as an immediate consequence; explicit proven families include complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and complete graphs minus one edge.
R027.source_name: Paul Meunier and Pegah Pournajafi, “Vertex gluing preserves the bunkbed conjecture”, arXiv:2410.08957 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08957

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2024). “Nevertheless, few explicit families of graphs have been proven to satisfy the bunkbed conjecture: for some versions of the conjecture, examples are complete graphs , complete bipartite graphs , and complete graphs minus one edge .”

R027.title: Rafla's conjecture on crossing-free Hamiltonian cycles in simple drawings
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let a **simple drawing** be a drawing in which any two edges have at most one common point and no two edges incident to the same vertex cross. A **crossing-free Hamiltonian cycle** is a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once and whose edges do not cross. **Rafla's conjecture.** Every simple drawing of $K_n$ with $n \geq 3$ vertices contains a crossing-free Hamiltonian cycle.

This conjecture asks whether the familiar property of straight-line drawings of complete graphs extends to all simple drawings. It was conjectured by Rafla in 1988; the supplied text gives no evidence of a general resolution, although it records proofs for several restricted drawing classes.
R027.source_name: Oswin Aichholzer, Joachim Orthaber and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “Separable Drawings: Extendability and Crossing-Free Hamiltonian Cycles”, arXiv:2410.09922 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

R027.title: The Hamiltonian-path strengthening of Rafla's conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, let $\mathcal{D}$ be a simple drawing of it on $n\ge 2$ vertices, and let $v$ and $w$ be distinct vertices of $\mathcal{D}$. A **crossing-free Hamiltonian path** is a path that visits every vertex exactly once, has no crossing edges, and whose end-vertices are $v$ and $w$. **Hamiltonian-path strengthening.** Every simple drawing $\mathcal{D}$ of $K_n$ on $n\ge 2$ vertices contains, for each pair of vertices $v \neq w$ in $\mathcal{D}$, a crossing-free Hamiltonian path with end-vertices $v$ and $w$.

The source states that this conjecture strengthens Rafla's Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture and that the implication between the two holds for the drawing classes considered there. It was confirmed for cylindrical and strongly c-monotone drawings, but the supplied text leaves the assertion open for arbitrary simple drawings.
R027.source_name: Oswin Aichholzer, Joachim Orthaber and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “Separable Drawings: Extendability and Crossing-Free Hamiltonian Cycles”, arXiv:2410.09922 (2026).
R027.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

R027.title: Stark--Tate conjecture for rank-one abelian extensions
R027.statement:
Let $H/F$ be an abelian extension of number fields, let $W$ be the number of roots of unity in $H$, and let $S$ be a finite set of places of $F$ containing the ramified and infinite places, with $|S|\geq 2$. Suppose a place $\mathfrak p\in S$ splits completely in $F$, put $T=S\setminus\{\mathfrak p\}$, and let $U_{S,H}^T$ be the group of elements satisfying the valuation conditions in the source. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(H/F)$ and a place $\mathfrak P\mid\mathfrak p$, let $\zeta_S^{\operatorname{Gal}}(\sigma,s)$ be the Galois-theoretic partial zeta function. **Stark--Tate conjecture.** There exists $\e\in U_{S,H}^T$ such that

$$
\log|\sigma(\e)|_{\mathfrak P}=-W\zeta_S^{\operatorname{Gal}\prime}(\sigma,0)
$$

for every $\sigma$ and $\mathfrak P\mid\mathfrak p$, and such that $H(\e^{1/W})$ is abelian over $F$. Tate's formulation refines Stark's published assertion and is used to obtain abelian extensions containing the relevant RM values; the conjecture remains unresolved in the source.

R027.title: Characterization of crossing matrices of positive pure braids
R027.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $M$ be an $n\times n$ matrix. A **positive pure braid** is a pure braid admitting a diagram with only positive crossings, and its crossing matrix records the algebraic number of crossings between each pair of strands. A symmetric matrix is **T0** when, for every $i<j$, $M(i,j)=0$ implies that there is some $k$ with $i<k<j$ such that $M(i,k)>0$ or $M(k,j)>0$.

**Characterization conjecture.** An $n\times n$ matrix $M$ is the crossing matrix of some positive pure braid if and only if $M$ is a non-negative integer T0 symmetric matrix.

The conjecture seeks a complete characterization of crossing matrices arising from positive pure braids, extending the known characterization for arbitrary pure braids by zero-diagonal integer symmetric matrices. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied source context.
R027.source_name: Ayaka Shimizu and Yoshiro Yaguchi, “Characterization of the OU matrix of a braid diagram”, arXiv:2502.16035 (2025).

R027.title: Hill's crossing-number conjecture for complete graphs
R027.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{cr}(K_n)$ denote its crossing number, the minimum number of crossings in a drawing of $K_n$ in the plane or sphere. Define

$$
X(n):=\frac{1}{4}\Big\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2}\Big\rfloor.
$$

**Hill's conjecture.** The crossing number satisfies

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=X(n)=\frac{3}{8}\binom{n}{4}+O(n^3).
$$

This is a foundational unsolved problem in geometric graph theory. The conjecture was first studied by Hill in the 1950s, and the displayed quantity is attained by the standard conjectured optimal drawings; the equality is not known for general $n$.

R027.title: The polar-set characterization for strongly incomplete polynomial approximation
R027.statement:
Let $K\subset {\mathbb{C}}\setminus \{0\}$ be a compact set. A polynomial of the indicated form is $\sum_{k=n/\tau_n}^{n}a_kz^k$, where $\tau_n\to 1$. **Polar-set characterization conjecture.** Any function continuous on $K$ (or equivalently, any polynomial) can be uniformly approximated on $K$ by polynomials of the form

$$
\sum_{k=n/\tau_n}^{n}a_kz^k
$$

with $\tau_n\to 1$, if and only if $K$ is polar. This conjecture seeks to characterize exactly the compact sets supporting approximation by strongly incomplete polynomials; the supplied context gives no resolution.

R027.title: Conjectured special values and generating function for the polynomials \(\psi_n\)
R027.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let

$$
\overline{H}_n=\sum_{\nu=1}^{n}\frac{(-1)^{\nu+1}}{\nu}
$$

be the alternating harmonic number. Let $\mathcal{B}_n$ denote the complete Bell polynomial, and evaluate $\psi_n$ at either the all-plus or all-minus tuple, with the corresponding signs chosen consistently.

**Special-values conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$,

$$
\psi_n(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)=-\mathcal{B}_n(\mp\overline{H}_1,\mp2!\,\overline{H}_2,\ldots,\mp n!\,\overline{H}_n),
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n\geq1}\psi_n(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)\frac{x^n}{n!}=1-(x+1)^{\mp1/(1-x)},
$$

choosing the corresponding signs, respectively.

The formulas are supported by computed values, but the source does not provide a proof or a resolution.

R027.title: Complete Kähler metric question for regular loci and complements
R027.statement:
Let $X$ be a weakly pseudoconvex Kähler complex space. Its regular locus is denoted by $X_{\operatorname{reg}}$, and an analytic subset of a complex space is denoted by $A$. **Complete Kähler metric question.** Does there exist an example for which $X_{\operatorname{reg}}$ does not admit a complete Kähler metric? Furthermore, when $X$ is a weakly pseudoconvex Kähler manifold, does there exist an analytic subset $A$ such that $X\setminus A$ does not admit a complete Kähler metric?

The question asks whether the complete-Kähler-metric conclusions known for compact or $1$-convex weakly pseudoconvex spaces, and for complements of analytic subsets in those settings, can fail in the general non-compact case.

R027.title: Minuscule bi-analytic Ax–Schanuel conjecture
R027.statement: Let $G/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a reductive group, let $[\mu]$ be a minuscule conjugacy class of cocharacters of $G_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p}$, and let $b\in G(\breve{\mathbb{Q}}_p)$ represent the unique basic class in $B(G,[\mu^{-1}])$. Let $L/\breve{\mathbb{Q}}_p([\mu])$ be a $p$-adic field. Let $\mathrm{D}$ be the space defined in the source setup, let $C$ be the completed algebraic closure, and suppose $S\subseteq\mathrm{D}_C$ is a smooth locally closed $\overline{L}$-analytic subvariety. An intersection is called **exceptional** according to the source's tangent-dimension condition, and a **strictly special subvariety** is the source's designated special subvariety. **Minuscule bi-analytic Ax–Schanuel conjecture.** If $Z\subseteq\mathcal{M}^{\tau}\cap S$ is an exceptional component, then $Z$ is contained in a strictly special subvariety of $\mathcal{M}^{\tau}_C$. This is the paper's main Ax–Schanuel-type claim: strictly special subvarieties are conjectured to account for all exceptional intersections, and no resolution is supplied.

R027.title: The nested 2-restricted Specht classification conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $I$ be the index set of the affine type ${\tt A}_1^{(1)}$, let $\theta\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}I$, and let $\mathcal{NP}_{\mathrm{2res}}(\theta)$ be the set of skew diagrams $\lambda\backslash\mu$ with $\lambda,\mu$ properly nested 2-restricted partitions of a common residue class and content $\theta$. For each such skew diagram, let $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{S}}(\lambda\backslash\mu)$ be its Specht module and $R_\theta$ the corresponding KLR algebra. Then **nested 2-restricted Specht classification conjecture.** For every $\lambda\backslash\mu\in\mathcal{NP}_{\mathrm{2res}}(\theta)$, $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{S}}(\lambda\backslash\mu)$ has simple head, and

$$
\left\{L(\lambda\backslash\mu):=\operatorname{hd}\boldsymbol{\mathsf{S}}(\lambda\backslash\mu)\mid \lambda\backslash\mu\in\mathcal{NP}_{\mathrm{2res}}(\theta)\right\}
$$

is a complete and irredundant list of simple $R_\theta$-modules up to isomorphism and grading shift. This would give an alternate classification of the simple modules for the type ${\tt A}_1^{(1)}$ KLR algebra, extending known cases involving ordinary and core-deleted skew diagrams.

R027.title: Completeness conjecture for the knot biquandle of virtual links
R027.statement:
A **knotlike biquandle** is a biquandle admitting a presentation in which every explicit relation is short, every generator appears exactly once as input, operator, and output, and the relations occur in the paired switch forms specified above. For a virtual link, its knot biquandle is the biquandle obtained from a diagram by assigning generators to semiarcs and imposing the crossing relations; **Tietze moves** are the standard presentation moves, while **virtual isotopy moves** are the Reidemeister-type moves for virtual link diagrams.

**Knot-biquandle completeness conjecture.** The knot biquandle is a complete invariant of virtual link type: if two knotlike biquandle presentations are related by Tietze moves, then the resulting virtual link diagrams are related by virtual isotopy moves.

Every virtual knot or link biquandle is knotlike, and the biquandle determines the virtual link up to strictly virtual moves. The conjecture asserts that the remaining ambiguity is exactly virtual isotopy, rather than merely strict virtual equivalence.

R027.title: Włodarczyk's weak factorization conjecture
R027.statement:
Let $f:X\dashrightarrow Y$ be a birational map of smooth complete varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, which is an isomorphism over an open set $U$. Then $f$ can be factored as

$$
X=X_0\dashrightarrow X_1\dashrightarrow\cdots\dashrightarrow X_n=Y,
$$

where each $X_i$ is a smooth complete variety and each birational map is a blow-up or blow-down at a smooth center and is an isomorphism over $U$. Moreover, if $X\setminus U$ and $Y\setminus U$ are divisors with normal crossings, then each $D_i:=X_i\setminus U$ is a divisor with normal crossings and each map is a blow-up or blow-down at a smooth center having normal crossings with the components of $D_i$.

**Weak factorization conjecture.** Every such birational map admits this factorization, with the stated preservation of the open set and normal-crossings boundary.

The conjecture is the central factorization statement developed in the paper and is presented there as proved in characteristic zero. A stronger factorization statement, in which all blow-ups precede all blow-downs, remains open according to the surrounding text.

R027.title: Conjecture 2: Euclidean submetries and K-circles in compact Ptolemy spaces
R027.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Ptolemy space satisfying Axioms (1)–(4) on page 6. For every $\c9\in X$, equip $X_\omega=X\setminus\{\omega\}$ with a metric $d$ from the Möbius structure of $X$ having $\c9$ as infinitely remote point. Is there a submetry $\pi_\omega:X_\omega\to B_\omega$ such that $B_\omega$ is isometric to a Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^k$, with $k\le \dim X$, and such that every Möbius automorphism $\phi:X\to X$ satisfying $\phi(\omega)=\omega'$ induces a homothety $\bar\phi:B_\omega\to B_{\omega'}$ with

$$\pi_{\omega'}\circ\phi=\bar\phi\circ\pi_\omega.$$

Moreover, if $F$ is a fiber of $\pi_\omega$, then the completed fiber $\hat F=F\cup\{\omega\}$, called a K-circle, is homeomorphic to a sphere $S^p$, where $k+p=\dim X$, and the following hold: (1K) through any two distinct points of $X$ there is a unique K-circle; (2K) any K-circle and any R-circle in $X$ have at most two points in common; (3K) given a K-circle $\hat F=F\cup\{\omega\}$ through $\omega$ and $x\in X\setminus\hat F$, there is a unique R-circle $\sigma\subset X$ through $x$ and $\omega$ that intersects $F$; and (4K) given distinct K-circles $\hat F=F\cup\{\omega\}$ and $\hat F'=F'\cup\{\omega\}$ through $\omega$, and two R-circles through $\omega$ that intersect $F$ and $F'$, respectively, for any other K-circle $\hat F''=F''\cup\{\omega\}$, if $F''$ intersects one of those R-circles, then it necessarily intersects the other.
