R027.title: Existence of weighted envy-freeness up to one item (WEF1)
R027.statement: Given a finite set of indivisible items $M$, agents $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with positive entitlements $w_i>0$, and additive valuations $v_i:2^M\to\mathbb{R}$, does there always exist a complete allocation $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ of $M$ such that, for every pair of agents $i,j$, there is an item $o\in A_i\cup A_j$ satisfying $\frac{v_i(A_i\setminus\{o\})}{w_i}\geq\frac{v_i(A_j\setminus\{o\})}{w_j}$, where removing $o$ affects only the bundle to which it belongs? Moreover, does such a complete weighted-envy-free-up-to-one-item allocation always admit a polynomial-time construction?
R027.source_name: arXiv
R027.references: - [Weighted Fair Division of Indivisible Mixed Manna](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01580) — arXiv

R029.title: Discrete Borsuk Conjecture 3
R029.statement: For bounded $S\subset\mathbb Z^d$, is $\beta_{\mathbb Z}(S)=2^d$ if and only if $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ is unimodularly equivalent to $[0,m]^d$?
R029.source_name: Open Math Problems Claimed to Be Solved with AI

R029.title: Borsuk's problem
R029.statement:
For a nonempty bounded set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ let

$$
\operatorname{diam} A = \sup\{\, \|x-y\| : x, y \in A \,\},
$$

where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm, and set $\operatorname{diam} \emptyset
= 0$.

For every integer $n \geq 1$ and every bounded set $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with
$\operatorname{diam} E > 0$, there exist sets $E_1, E_2, \dots, E_{n+1}$ with

$$
E = E_1 \cup E_2 \cup \cdots \cup E_{n+1}
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{diam} E_i < \operatorname{diam} E \qquad \text{for every } i \in \{1, \dots, n+1\}.
$$
R029.source_name: Wikipedia
R029.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Borsuk's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borsuk%27s_conjecture), the article this problem comes from.

R029.title: Bing–Borsuk conjecture
R029.statement:
For a metric space $M$, say that $M$ is *homogeneous* if for any two points
$m_1,m_2\in M$ there is a homeomorphism of $M$ onto itself taking $m_1$ to
$m_2$.

Say that a metric space
$M$ is an *absolute neighborhood retract* (ANR) if for every closed embedding $f:M\rightarrow
N$ into a metric space $N$ there exists an open neighbourhood $U$ of $f(M)$ in
$N$ that retracts onto $f(M)$, i.e. there is a continuous map
$r:U\rightarrow f(M)$ with $r\restriction f(M)=\mathrm{id}_{f(M)}$.

Say that $M$ is an *$n$-manifold* if every point of
$M$ has an open neighbourhood homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Let $n\geq 1$ and let
$M$ be a metric space which is homogeneous, is an ANR, and has topological dimension $\dim
M=n$. Then $M$ is an $n$-manifold.
R029.source_name: Wikipedia
R029.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Bing–Borsuk conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing%E2%80%93Borsuk_conjecture), the article this problem comes from.

R029.title: Alternate Bing–Borsuk conjecture via approximate fibrations
R029.statement: Let $X$ be nicely embedded in $\mathbb R^{m+n}$ for some $m\geq 3$, and suppose that $X$ has a mapping cylinder neighborhood $N=C_\phi$ of a map $\phi:\partial N\to X$, with mapping cylinder projection $\pi:N\to X$. An **approximate fibration** is a map having the approximate homotopy lifting property. **Alternate Bing–Borsuk conjecture.** The projection $\pi:N\to X$ is an approximate fibration. This formulation is stated as equivalent to the Bing–Borsuk conjecture and remains open with it.
R029.source_name: Denise M. Halverson and Dušan Repovš, “The Bing-Borsuk and the Busemann Conjectures”, arXiv:0811.0886 (2009).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2008). “The following is the conjecture proposed by Quinn which was proved in 2006 by Bryant .”

R029.title: Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger homogeneity conjecture
R029.statement: Let $X$ be a generalized $n$-manifold with $n\geq 7$ satisfying the disjoint disks property. **Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger conjecture.** The space $X$ is homogeneous. If true, this would contradict the Bing–Borsuk conjecture in dimensions $n\geq 7$, because such spaces are known to be non-resolvable. The source does not report a resolution of this conjecture.
R029.source_name: Denise M. Halverson and Dušan Repovš, “The Bing-Borsuk and the Busemann Conjectures”, arXiv:0811.0886 (2009).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2008). “The following is the conjecture proposed by Quinn which was proved in 2006 by Bryant .”

R029.title: Equivariant classification conjecture for positively curved 4-manifolds with circle actions
R029.statement: Let $M$ be a simply connected positively curved 4-manifold equipped with an isometric circle action. A **linear circle action** is a circle action induced by a linear action on either the sphere or complex projective plane. **Equivariant classification conjecture.** The action on $M$ is equivariantly diffeomorphic to a linear circle action on either $\mathbb{S}^4$ or $\mathbb{C\mkern1mu P}^2$. This proposes a complete equivariant classification of such actions; the preceding discussion explains that the classification up to equivariant diffeomorphism is not yet known because the possible weighted orbit-space data in positive curvature are not fully understood.
R029.source_name: Karsten Grove, “Developments around positive sectional curvature”, arXiv:0902.4419 (2009).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.4419

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2009).

R029.title: Moore–Witten conjecture for SU(2) Donaldson invariants of CP^2
R029.statement: Consider the complex projective plane $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^2$ with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. Its regularized $u$-plane integral has a contribution from the cusp at $\tau=\infty$. **Moore–Witten conjecture for $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^2$.** The contribution from the cusp at $\tau=\infty$ to the regularized $u$-plane integral of $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^2$ for the gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is equal to the generating function for the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-Donaldson invariants of $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^2$. The source explicitly identifies this as the remaining open case of the broader Moore–Witten conjecture.
R029.source_name: Andreas Malmendier, “Donaldson invariants of CP^1 x CP^1 and Mock Theta Functions”, arXiv:1008.0175 (2011).
R029.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0808.1442](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1442).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.0175

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2010). “Based on the work in it follows (cf. Theorem and Corollaries and ) that the only case of Conjecture that remains still o”

R029.title: Borsuk's conjecture on partitioning sets of bounded diameter
R029.statement: Let $S$ be a set of diameter $d>0$ in Euclidean $n$-space $\mathbb R^n$. **Borsuk's conjecture.** Every such set is the union of $n+1$ sets, each of diameter less than $d$. The conjecture is the classical Borsuk problem on reducing the diameter of a set by partitioning it; its resolution depends on the dimension, and the general statement is not valid in all dimensions.
R029.source_name: M. Hujter and Z. Lángi, “On the multiple Borsuk numbers of sets”, arXiv:1206.0892 (2012).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0892

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

R029.title: The asymptotic classification conjecture for simplicial arrangements
R029.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a simplicial arrangement in $\mathbb{C}^3$, and let its incidence mean the incidence structure between its hyperplanes and their intersections. Let $\mathcal{A}(2n,1)$ and $\mathcal{A}(4n+1,1)$ denote the arrangements in the stated infinite series, and let $G(e,1,3)$ denote an imprimitive complex reflection group.

**Asymptotic classification conjecture.** There exists an $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that the incidence of every simplicial arrangement in $\mathbb{C}^3$ with more than $N$ hyperplanes is isomorphic to the incidence of $\mathcal{A}(2n,1)$, $\mathcal{A}(4n+1,1)$, or to the incidence of the imprimitive reflection groups $G(e,1,3)$ for some $e,n\in\mathbb{N}$.

This proposes an extension of Grünbaum's conjecture and would classify all sufficiently large simplicial arrangements in the complex projective plane by their incidence structures. The source presents it as a proposal; no resolution is supplied here.
R029.source_name: Michael Cuntz and David Geis, “Combinatorial simpliciality of arrangements of hyperplanes”, arXiv:1302.2052 (2013).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2052

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

R029.title: The noncommutative Brouwer retract conjecture for C*-algebras
R029.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with a free action of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\Gamma A$ be its cone C*-algebra. Let $\operatorname{ev}_{1/2}:\Gamma A\to A$ be evaluation at the midpoint.

**Noncommutative Brouwer retract conjecture.** There is no $*$-homomorphism

$$
\gamma:A\longrightarrow\Gamma A
$$

such that

$$
\operatorname{ev}_{1/2}\circ\gamma=\operatorname{id}_A.
$$

This is proposed as a noncommutative analogue of the retract formulation of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem and is an immediate consequence of the preceding cone Borsuk–Ulam conjecture. The source says it holds for the even-dimensional quantum $\theta$-ball families, but does not establish it in general.
R029.source_name: Ludwik Dabrowski, “Towards a noncommutative Brouwer fixed-point theorem”, arXiv:1504.03588 (2015).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03588

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

R029.title: Borsuk's transversality conjecture
R029.statement: Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a set of points, let $D$ be the set of pairs of points in $K$ at the diameter distance, and call $(K,D)$ **general** if every continuous deformation of the distances on $D$ is realized by a deformation of $K$. **Borsuk's transversality conjecture.** If $(K,D)$ is general, then $K$ can be partitioned into $d+1$ sets of smaller diameter. The source proposes a stronger infinitesimal-deformation version, but gives no resolution status for the stated conjecture.
R029.source_name: Gil Kalai, “Some old and new problems in combinatorial geometry I: Around Borsuk's problem”, arXiv:1505.04952 (2015).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04952

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

R029.title: Weak Borsuk conjecture for polytopes
R029.statement: Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a polytope with $m$ facets. A covering by smaller-diameter sets is a cover of $P$ by sets whose diameters are strictly smaller than the diameter of $P$. **Weak Borsuk conjecture for polytopes.** Every polytope $P$ with $m$ facets can be covered by $m$ sets of smaller diameter. The source says that a positive answer would give an alternative route concerning projections of the cut polytope, but gives no resolution status.
R029.source_name: Gil Kalai, “Some old and new problems in combinatorial geometry I: Around Borsuk's problem”, arXiv:1505.04952 (2015).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04952

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

R029.title: Conjecture on homogeneous convex divisible domains in flag manifolds
R029.statement: Let $G$ be a connected non-compact simple Lie group with trivial center, and let $P \leq G$ be a parabolic subgroup. A **convex divisible domain** in $G/P$ is a bounded open convex subset of an affine chart on which a discrete subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$ acts properly discontinuously, freely, and co-compactly. Assume that $G/P$ is not isomorphic to a real projective space or the complex projective plane. **Homogeneity conjecture.** Every convex divisible domain in $G/P$ is homogeneous. This conjecture extends known rigidity results for convex divisible domains, including Frankel's theorem in complex affine space and the classification of such domains in $\operatorname{Gr}_p(\operatorname{\mathbb{R}}^{2p})$; the general case remains open.
R029.source_name: Andrew Zimmer, “Proper quasi-homogeneous domains in flag manifolds and geometric structures”, arXiv:1507.06921 (2018).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.06921

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

R029.title: Dąbrowski's suspension conjecture for free involutions
R029.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with a free action of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Its unreduced suspension is

$$
\Sigma A=\{f\in C([-1,1],A):f(-1),f(1)\in\mathbb{C}\}.
$$

The action extends to $\Sigma A$ by $\alpha_\Sigma f(t)=\alpha(f(-t))$. **Dąbrowski's conjecture.** There is no $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant $*$-homomorphism

$$
\phi:A\to\Sigma A.
$$

This conjecture seeks a noncommutative analogue of the Borsuk–Ulam obstruction and was proposed in connection with noncommutative Brouwer fixed point theorems. The source gives no resolution status.
R029.source_name: Benjamin Passer, “Free Actions on C*-algebra Suspensions and Joins by Finite Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:1510.04100 (2017).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.04100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2015).

R029.title: The constant-width illumination conjecture in three dimensions
R029.statement: Let $\mathbf{K}$ be a three-dimensional convex body of constant width. **Constant-width illumination conjecture.** The illumination number satisfies $I(\mathbf{K})=4$. The known general upper bound is $I(\mathbf{K})\leq 6$, and the conjecture would imply a new proof of Borsuk's conjecture in dimension three; it remains open.
R029.source_name: Karoly Bezdek and Muhammad A. Khan, “The geometry of homothetic covering and illumination”, arXiv:1602.06040 (2016).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.06040

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2016). “The X-ray Conjecture is proved only in the plane and it is open in higher dimensions.”

R029.title: Modified noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture of type II
R029.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital C*-algebra equipped with a free action of a non-trivial compact quantum group $(H,\Delta)$, and let $A\circledast^\delta H$ be the equivariant noncommutative join C*-algebra of $A$ and $H$ with the induced free action of $(H,\Delta)$. Assume that $A$ admits a character. **Modified noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture of type II.** There does not exist an $(H,\Delta)$-equivariant $*$-homomorphism

$$
H\longrightarrow A\circledast^\delta H.
$$

Equivalently, the compact quantum principal bundle given by $A\circledast^\delta H$ is not trivializable. The paper presents this as a corollary of the type-I conjecture; the original type-II conjecture has counterexamples, so the character hypothesis is essential to this modified formulation.
R029.source_name: Ludwik Dąbrowski, Piotr M. Hajac and Sergey Neshveyev, “Noncommutative Borsuk-Ulam-type conjectures revisited”, arXiv:1611.04130 (2017).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.04130

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2016); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

R029.title: Persistence conjecture for symplectic mapping groups of the five-point blow-up of the projective plane
R029.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb{C}P^2\#5\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ be the five-point blow-up of the complex projective plane, equipped with any symplectic form. Let $\Gamma(X,\omega)$ denote the symplectic reflection group, let $PR[\Gamma(X,\omega)]$ be its number of positive roots, and let $\operatorname{Rank}$ denote the rank of the relevant group. **Persistence conjecture.** The quantity

$$
PR[\Gamma(X,\omega)]+\operatorname{Rank}[\pi_1(\operatorname{Symp}(X,\omega))]-\operatorname{Rank}[\pi_0(\operatorname{Symp}_h(X,\omega))]
$$

is constant and equal to $15$ for every symplectic form on $\mathbb{C}P^2\#5\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$. This conjecture proposes that the numerical relation found for the previously analyzed symplectic forms persists throughout the space of symplectic forms on this rational four-manifold; its resolution would clarify the extent to which the symplectic mapping group and the homologically trivial symplectomorphism group vary under deformation.
R029.source_name: Jun Li and Tian-Jun Li, “Symplectic (-2) spheres and the symplectomorphism group of small rational 4-manifolds, I”, arXiv:1611.07436 (2019).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07436

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

R029.title: The noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture for equivariant joins
R029.statement:
Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a compact quantum group. The $n$-fold equivariant noncommutative join is denoted by $C(E^\Delta_n\mathbb{G})$, and $\dim_{\rm LT}^{\mathbb{G}}$ denotes the local-triviality dimension of a $\mathbb{G}$-algebra.

**Noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture.** There does not exist a $\mathbb{G}$-equivariant $*$-homomorphism

$$
C(E^\Delta_n\mathbb{G})\to C(E^\Delta_{n+1}\mathbb{G})
$$

and

$$
\dim_{\rm LT}^{\mathbb{G}}(C(E^\Delta_n\mathbb{G}))=n.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the classical Borsuk–Ulam non-existence result from finite and compact Hausdorff groups to compact quantum groups, in the setting of iterated equivariant noncommutative joins. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.
R029.source_name: Eusebio Gardella, Piotr M. Hajac, Mariusz Tobolski and Jianchao Wu, “The local-triviality dimension of actions of compact quantum groups”, arXiv:1801.00767 (2019).
R029.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1504.03588](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.03588).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00767

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

R029.title: Baum-Dąbrowski-Hajac topological Borsuk-Ulam conjecture
R029.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space with a free action of a nontrivial compact group $G$. Equip the join $X * G$ with the diagonal action. **Baum-Dąbrowski-Hajac's topological Borsuk-Ulam conjecture.** There is no equivariant map

$$
X * G \to X.
$$

This generalizes the Borsuk-Ulam theorem from antipodal actions on spheres to free actions of compact groups on compact Hausdorff spaces. The source gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
R029.source_name: Alexandru Chirvasitu and Benjamin Passer, “Invariants in Noncommutative Dynamics”, arXiv:1804.01434 (2019).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01434

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

R029.title: Baum-Dąbrowski-Hajac noncommutative Borsuk-Ulam conjectures
R029.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with a free coaction $\delta$ of a nontrivial compact quantum group $(H, \Delta)$. Equip the join $A \circledast^{\delta} H$ with the induced free coaction $\delta_\Delta$. **Baum-Dąbrowski-Hajac's noncommutative Borsuk-Ulam conjectures.** There are no equivariant unital $*$-homomorphisms

$$
A \to A \circledast^{\delta} H
$$

that are $(\delta, \delta_\Delta)$-equivariant, and

$$
H \to A \circledast^{\delta} H
$$

that are $(\Delta, \delta_\Delta)$-equivariant. Equivalently, both the Type 1 and Type 2 conjectures in the source assert the nonexistence of the respective homomorphisms. These conjectures extend the topological formulation to coactions of compact quantum groups on possibly noncommutative $C^*$-algebras. The source gives no resolution status for either type.
R029.source_name: Alexandru Chirvasitu and Benjamin Passer, “Invariants in Noncommutative Dynamics”, arXiv:1804.01434 (2019).
R029.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1801.00767](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00767), [arXiv:1604.02173](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.02173).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01434

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

R029.title: Type 1 noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture for compact group actions
R029.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial compact group acting freely on a unital $C^*$-algebra $A$. Define the join

$$
A\circledast C(G)=\{f\in C([0,1],A\otimes C(G)): f(0)\in \mathbb{C}\otimes C(G),\ f(1)\in A\otimes\mathbb{C}\}.
$$

Equip $A\circledast C(G)$ with the diagonal action of $G$. **Type 1 noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture.** There is no equivariant, unital $*$-homomorphism

$$
\phi:A\to A\circledast C(G).
$$

This is the compact-group subcase of the Type 1 noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjecture, originally formulated for coactions of compact quantum groups. It asserts that a free action cannot admit an equivariant unital map from $A$ to its join with the acting group.
R029.source_name: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Benjamin Passer and Mariusz Tobolski, “Equivariant Dimensions of Graph C*-algebras”, arXiv:1907.10010 (2020).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

R029.title: The adjunction inequality for the Rasmussen invariant in negative-definite four-manifolds
R029.statement:
Let $W=(\#^r\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2})\setminus B^4$ for some $r\geq 0$. Let $L\subset\partial W=S^3$ be a link, and let $\Sigma\subset W$ be a properly, smoothly embedded oriented surface with no closed components such that $\partial\Sigma=L$. The notation $[\Sigma]$, $|[\Sigma]|$, and $[\Sigma]\cdot[\Sigma]$ denotes the homology class of $\Sigma$, its norm as used in the paper, and its self-intersection, respectively.

**Adjunction conjecture for $s$.**

$$
s(L)\leq 1-\chi(\Sigma)-\left|[\Sigma]\right|-[\Sigma]\cdot[\Sigma].
$$

This extends the Ozsváth–Szabó adjunction inequality for $\tau$ and the paper's previously established null-homologous case to arbitrary properly embedded surfaces in punctured connected sums of negative complex projective planes. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
R029.source_name: Ciprian Manolescu, Marco Marengon, Sucharit Sarkar and Michael Willis, “A generalization of Rasmussen's invariant, with applications to surfaces in some four-manifolds”, arXiv:1910.08195 (2022).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.08195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

R029.title: Modified Bing–Borsuk conjecture for homogeneous ANR-spaces
R029.statement:
Let $X$ be a locally compact homogeneous $ANR$-space of dimension $n$. A generalized $n$-manifold is a locally compact $n$-dimensional $ANR$-space that is a $\mathbb Z$-homology $n$-manifold.

**Modified Bing–Borsuk conjecture.** Every locally compact homogeneous $ANR$-space of dimension $n\geq 3$ is a generalized $n$-manifold.

This modification was suggested by Bryant. The source does not state whether it is resolved; a positive solution of the preceding conjecture would imply that the Bing–Borsuk conjecture is false for $n\geq 6$.
R029.source_name: Vesko Valov, “Homogeneous metric ANR-compacta”, arXiv:2003.06907 (2020).
R029.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0811.0886](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0886).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06907

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2020). “In higher dimensions the Resolution Conjecture is false.”

R029.title: The model complex projective-plane twist conjecture
R029.statement: Let $\varphi\in\operatorname{Symp}_{ct}(T^*\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^2)$ be the compactly supported symplectomorphism constructed from the Lefschetz fibration in the paper. The **complex projective-plane twist** is the local projective twist associated with $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^2$. **Model complex projective-plane twist conjecture.** The symplectomorphism $\varphi$ is isotopic to the $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^2$-twist. The construction gives a symplectomorphism of infinite order, while the relevant symplectic mapping-class group is otherwise poorly understood; consequently, the identification with the projective twist remains conjectural.
R029.source_name: Brunella Charlotte Torricelli, “Model projective twists and generalised lantern relations”, arXiv:2008.02758 (2022).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02758

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

R029.title: The extremal Borsuk number conjecture for normed spaces
R029.statement:
Let $B(n)$ be the maximum, over all norms on $\mathbb{R}^n$, of the Borsuk number of $(\mathbb{R}^n,\left\Vert\cdot\right\Vert)$, where the Borsuk number is the smallest number of sets of strictly smaller diameter needed to partition every bounded subset. **Normed-space Borsuk conjecture.** For each integer $n\geq 3$, 

$$
B(n)=2^n.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the inequality $b_X(K)\leq c(K)$ and Hadwiger's covering conjecture, which predicts the bound $c(K)\leq 2^n$ for convex bodies. Despite progress, it remains open when $n\geq 3$.
R029.source_name: Yanlu Lian and Senlin Wu, “Divide bounded sets into sets having smaller diameters”, arXiv:2103.10679 (2021).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10679

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021). “Despite of these progress, Conjecture is still open when $n\geq 3$.”

R029.title: The Nielsen–Borsuk–Ulam dichotomy conjecture for free involutions on tori
R029.statement:
Let ${\mathbb{T}}^n$ be the $n$-torus, let $f:{\mathbb{T}}^n\to{\mathbb{T}}^n$ be a map, and let $\tau$ be a free involution of ${\mathbb{T}}^n$. **Nielsen–Borsuk–Ulam dichotomy conjecture.** The Nielsen–Borsuk–Ulam number satisfies

$$
\operatorname{NBU}(f,\tau)\in\{2^{n-1},0\}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the computations for free involutions on low-dimensional tori and by the example yielding $\operatorname{NBU}(g,\tau_2)=2^{n-1}$. It predicts that for every map and free involution the invariant can take only these two values; the supplied source does not state a resolution.
R029.source_name: Givanildo Donizeti de Melo and Daniel Vendrúscolo, “Nielsen-Borsuk-Ulam number for maps between tori”, arXiv:2107.02356 (2021).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02356

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

R029.title: The generalized Borsuk covering-number conjecture
R029.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a classifying space $E_dG$, write $
\operatorname{cov}_G(d)$ for its $G$-covering number, namely the minimum number of sets in a $G$-cover. The preceding bounds give

$$
d+|G|\leq \operatorname{cov}_G(d)\leq d(|G|-1)+2.
$$

**Generalized Borsuk covering-number conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cov}_G(d)=|G|+d.
$$

This would make the lower bound sharp for every finite group and every dimension. The paper reports computational evidence, but states that the conjecture remains open; its special cases and the strict-growth assertion below are proposed as related follow-up questions.
R029.source_name: Francisco Martinez-Figueroa, “Generalized Borsuk Graphs”, arXiv:2110.06453 (2021).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

R029.title: The cyclic-group Borsuk covering conjecture
R029.statement:
For $m\geq 2$ and $d\geq 0$, let $\operatorname{cov}_{\mathbb{Z}_m}(d)$ denote the $\mathbb{Z}_m$-covering number of a classifying space $E_d\mathbb{Z}_m$. The general lower bound is $m+d\leq \operatorname{cov}_{\mathbb{Z}_m}(d)$.

**Cyclic-group Borsuk covering conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cov}_{\mathbb{Z}_m}(d)=m+d.
$$

This is a less general conjecture that may remain true even if the generalized Borsuk covering-number conjecture fails. The paper states that both conjectures are open and points to computational work in dimensions $2$ and $3$.
R029.source_name: Francisco Martinez-Figueroa, “Generalized Borsuk Graphs”, arXiv:2110.06453 (2021).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

R029.title: The strict-growth conjecture for equivariant covering numbers
R029.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\operatorname{cov}_G(d)$ denote the $G$-covering number of a classifying space $E_dG$.

**Strict-growth conjecture.** For all $d\geq 0$,

$$
\operatorname{cov}_G(d)<\operatorname{cov}_G(d+1).
$$

This is proposed as a weaker alternative to the generalized Borsuk covering-number conjecture. The paper leaves it open and asks for proofs or counterexamples, together with computations for small groups and low dimensions.
R029.source_name: Francisco Martinez-Figueroa, “Generalized Borsuk Graphs”, arXiv:2110.06453 (2021).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

R029.title: Borsuk–Ulam conjecture for random complexes with free involution
R029.statement:
Let $d\geq 1$ and let $\alpha$ satisfy

$$
\frac{1}{d+1}<\alpha<\frac{1}{d}.
$$

Let $\widetilde Z\sim\widetilde Z(2n,n^{-\alpha})$ be a random simplicial complex on $2n$ vertices with free involution $\iota\colon\widetilde Z\to\widetilde Z$.

**Borsuk–Ulam conjecture.** With high probability, for every continuous map $f\colon\widetilde Z\to\mathbb{R}^{2d+1}$, there exists an $x\in|\widetilde Z|$ such that

$$
f(x)=f(\iota(x)).
$$

The preceding theorem proves the analogous assertion with target $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ in this probability regime, using that $\widetilde Z$ is at least $d$-connected with high probability. The conjecture reflects the observation that the connectivity over the rationals is expected to be about twice as large, but the stated stronger Borsuk–Ulam property remains open.
R029.source_name: Florian Frick and Andrew Newman, “Random complexes with free involution”, arXiv:2210.11316 (2022).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

R029.title: Montiel–Urbano conjecture for the Clifford torus in the complex projective plane
R029.statement:
Let $\mathbb{C}P^2$ be the complex projective plane, let $\mathcal{W}$ be the Willmore functional, and let $\mathcal{W}^-$ denote its component arising from the twistor decomposition. The **Clifford torus** is

$$
T=\Big\{[z_1,z_2,z_3]\in\mathbb{C}P^2\,\Big|\,|z_1|=|z_2|=|z_3|\Big\}.
$$

**Montiel–Urbano conjecture.** The Clifford torus achieves the minimum of the functional $\mathcal{W}^-$, and hence of $\mathcal{W}$, either among all tori in $\mathbb{C}P^2$ or among all Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{C}P^2$.

The conjecture concerns the global minimization of the conformally invariant Willmore functional in the complex projective plane. The paper establishes strict Willmore stability of the Clifford torus, providing evidence, but does not resolve the global minimization claim.
R029.source_name: Changping Wang and Zhenxiao Xie, “Willmore surfaces in 4-dimensional conformal manifolds”, arXiv:2306.00846 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00846

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2023). “Now this conjecture has been proved by Marques and Neves in .”

R029.title: Lattice-determined minimal Jacobian-relation degree conjecture for line arrangements
R029.statement:
Let $\mathcal A:f=0$ be a line arrangement of degree $d$ in the complex projective plane. Let $\operatorname{mdr}(f)$ denote the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation for $f$, and write $r=\operatorname{mdr}(f)$. **Minimal-degree conjecture.** For any line arrangement $\mathcal A:f=0$, the integer $r$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $r<d/2$.

This is presented as a stronger claim that would imply Terao's freeness conjecture through the characterization of free curves by maximal total Tjurina number in the relevant range. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
R029.source_name: Alexandru Dimca and Gabriel Sticlaru, “From Pascal's Theorem to the geometry of Ziegler's line arrangements”, arXiv:2312.11928 (2024).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

R029.title: Nonvanishing conjecture for sesquicuspidal curves in the complex projective plane
R029.statement:
Let $d$ be an integer and let $p/q>1$ be a reduced fraction. The count $\mathbf{T}_{d}^{p/q}$ is the index-zero finite-energy holomorphic-plane count associated with degree $d$ curves in $\CP^2$. **Nonvanishing conjecture.** For any reduced fraction $p/q>1$ satisfying

$$
p+q=3d
$$

and

$$
(p-1)(q-1)\leq(d-1)(d-2),
$$

we have $\mathbf{T}_{d}^{p/q}\neq0$. This is equivalent to the existence of an index-zero $(p,q)$-sesquicuspidal symplectic curve in $\CP^2$ of genus zero and degree $d$ whenever permitted by the adjunction formula. An affirmative answer would imply optimality of Hind's folding embedding in the range described in the source; the conjecture's resolution is not established here.
R029.source_name: Kyler Siegel, “A tree formula for the ellipsoidal superpotential of the complex projective plane”, arXiv:2404.14707 (2024).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14707

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

R029.title: Kneser's conjecture on the chromatic number of the Kneser graph
R029.statement:
Let $[n]$ be a set with $n$ elements, let $k$ satisfy $n\geq 2k-1$, and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ denote the family of all $k$-element subsets of $[n]$. A proper coloring assigns colors to the members of $\binom{[n]}{k}$ so that disjoint subsets receive different colors. **Kneser's conjecture.** The minimum number of colors needed for a proper coloring of elements in $\binom{[n]}{k}$ is

$$
n-2k+2.
$$

This is the chromatic-number statement for Kneser graphs, and it was proved by Lovász using the Borsuk–Ulam theorem; hence the conjecture is solved.
R029.source_name: Jingsi Hou, Guangyan Huang, Sammy Suliman and Haoran Yan, “Lovasz' Conjecture and Other Applications of Topological Methods in Discrete Mathematics”, arXiv:2405.05273 (2024).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05273

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

R029.title: The conjecture on the vanishing of the third James–Hopf obstruction
R029.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map with $X=\Sigma X'$ and $Y=\Sigma Y'$. Write $M_f$ for the mapping cone of $f$, and let $J_2(M_f,A)$ and $J_2(M_f,X)$ denote the corresponding second James constructions. Suppose that $[\operatorname{id}_Y,f]=0$, so that

$$
J_2(M_f,A)\simeq Y\vee Y\wedge X.
$$

Let $j_Y$ and $j_{Y\wedge X}$ be the canonical inclusions of the corresponding wedge summands of

$$
J_2(M_f,X)\simeq X\vee X\wedge A.
$$

**The conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, the map

$$
\gamma_3=[j_Yf,j_{Y\wedge X}]:Y'\wedge X\wedge X\longrightarrow Y\vee Y\wedge X
$$

is null-homotopic.

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that it holds in all special cases encountered by the authors, including attaching maps of the top cell in even-dimensional mod $2^r$ Moore spaces, suspended complex projective planes, and suspended quaternionic projective planes. Its general status is not resolved by the supplied source context.
R029.source_name: Zhongjian Zhu, “The unstable homotopy groups of 2-cell complexes”, arXiv:2410.20416 (2024).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20416

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

R029.title: Finiteness conjecture for characteristic numbers of complex line arrangements
R029.statement:
Let a **line arrangement** be a finite collection of lines in the complex projective plane, and let $\gamma(\mathcal{L})$ denote its characteristic number. For a real number $\varepsilon>0$, consider line arrangements whose characteristic number exceeds $2.5+\varepsilon$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For a given $\varepsilon>0$ there exists only finitely many line arrangements $\mathcal{L}$ such that

$$
\gamma(\mathcal{L})>2.5+\varepsilon.
$$

The conjecture predicts that characteristic numbers of complex line arrangements cannot remain uniformly above $2.5$ along infinitely many arrangements. The source presents it as an extremely challenging conjecture motivated by the scarcity of known families with characteristic numbers in $(\frac{5}{2},\frac{8}{3}]$; no resolution is given.
R029.source_name: Bartosz Naskręcki and Piotr Pokora, “On the geography of log-surfaces”, arXiv:2412.14635 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14635

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

R029.title: Finiteness conjecture for characteristic numbers of conic-line arrangements
R029.statement:
Let a **conic-line arrangement** be an arrangement $\mathcal{CL}$ of lines and smooth conics in the complex projective plane with ordinary singularities, and let $\gamma(\mathcal{CL})$ denote its characteristic number. For a real number $\varepsilon>0$, consider such arrangements whose characteristic number exceeds $2.5+\varepsilon$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For a given $\varepsilon>0$ there exists only finitely many conic-line arrangements $\mathcal{CL}$ with ordinary singularities such that

$$
\gamma(\mathcal{CL})>2.5+\varepsilon.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the absence of known families of conic-line arrangements with the number of lines and conics tending to infinity and characteristic number greater than $\frac{5}{2}$. The source describes it as a challenging conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.
R029.source_name: Bartosz Naskręcki and Piotr Pokora, “On the geography of log-surfaces”, arXiv:2412.14635 (2025).
R029.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2312.12950](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.12950).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14635

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

R029.title: The SU(3)-invariant quadratic-exponential expander-family conjecture
R029.statement: Let $\Lambda^2_-\mathbb{CP}^2$ denote the anti-self-dual bundle of the complex projective plane. A complete expander has **quadratic-exponential volume growth** when its volume grows at the quadratic-exponential rate described by the corresponding end model. **SU(3)-invariant quadratic-exponential family conjecture.** There exists a $1$-parameter family of complete $\textup{SU}(3)$-invariant expanders defined on $\Lambda^2_-\mathbb{CP}^2$, all with quadratic-exponential volume growth. The conjecture describes the expected transition family between AC and forward-incomplete smoothly-closing expanders; it remains open.
R029.source_name: Mark Haskins, Rowan Juneman and Johannes Nordström, “Sp(2)-invariant expanders and shrinkers in Laplacian flow”, arXiv:2501.05437 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05437

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

R029.title: Homologically trivial linearization conjecture for cyclic actions on the complex projective plane
R029.statement: Let $a4n$ act smoothly on $a4cp^2$. The action is **homologically trivial** if it acts trivially on the second homology $H_2(a4cp^2)$. A linear action is one induced by the standard linear action on complex projective space. **Homologically trivial linearization conjecture.** Every homologically trivial $a4n$-action on $a4cp^2$ is smoothly equivalent to a linear action. The conjecture is known in the symplectic case and topologically, while the smooth case remains open. Nonlinear actions of $a4p\oplusa4p$ are known, but in those examples every cyclic subgroup acts linearly.
R029.source_name: Jeffrey Meier and Evan Scott, “Equivariant trisections for group actions on four-manifolds”, arXiv:2501.17999 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17999

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

R029.title: Trisection reformulation of homologically trivial linearization for cyclic actions on the complex projective plane
R029.statement: Let $a4n$ act smoothly and homologically trivially on $a4cp^2$, and let an equivariant trisection be a trisection preserved by the action. **Homologically trivial linearization conjecture, trisection form.** Every homologically trivial $a4n$-action on $a4cp^2$ admits a genus-one equivariant trisection. This is presented as a reformulation of the smooth linearization conjecture above; the corresponding smooth statement remains open, although the conjecture is known in the symplectic case and topologically.
R029.source_name: Jeffrey Meier and Evan Scott, “Equivariant trisections for group actions on four-manifolds”, arXiv:2501.17999 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17999

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

R029.title: The skein lasagna module Poincaré series conjecture for the complex projective plane
R029.statement:
Let $P_n(t,q)$ denote the colored Khovanov Poincaré polynomial used in the paper, let $\mathcal{S}_0^2(\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2};h;\mathbb{Q})$ denote the skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ in $H_2$ grading $h$, and let $(a;q)_m$ denote the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol. **Skein lasagna module Poincaré-series conjecture.** The Poincaré series in $H_2$ gradings $0$ and $1$ are given by

$$
\operatorname{\mathcal{P}}\left(\mathcal{S}_0^2(\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}; 0; \mathbb{Q}) \right) = \lim_{n \to \infty} q^{-2n}P_{2n}(t,q^{-1})
$$

$$
= \frac{1}{1+q^{-4}t} \sum_{k = 0}^\infty t^{-2k^2} q^{2k(k+1)} \frac{(-q^{-4}t; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+1}}{(q^{2}t^{-2}; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k}} + t^{-2(k+1)^2} q^{2((k+1)^2 + k)} \frac{(-q^{-4}t; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+2}}{(q^{2}t^{-2}; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+1}},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{\mathcal{P}}\left(\mathcal{S}_0^2(\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}; 1; \mathbb{Q}) \right) = \lim_{n \to \infty} q^{-2n-1}P_{2n+1}(t,q^{-1})
$$

$$
= \frac{1}{1+q^{-4}t} \sum_{k = 0}^\infty t^{-2k(k+1)} q^{2(k^2+2k-1)} \frac{(-q^{-4}t; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+1}}{(q^{2}t^{-2}; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k}} + t^{-2k(k+1)} q^{2k(k+2)} \frac{(-q^{-4}t; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+2}}{(q^{2}t^{-2}; q^{2}t^{-2})_{2k+1}}.
$$

These formulas are conditional in the surrounding discussion on the recursion conjecture and relate the skein lasagna module to limits of colored Khovanov homology. The supplied text does not state that the formulas have been proved or otherwise resolved.
R029.source_name: Karim Ritter von Merkl, “Computing colored Khovanov homology”, arXiv:2505.03916 (2026).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03916

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

R029.title: Main Borsuk property conjecture for matroids
R029.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid with at least two bases. It has the **Borsuk property** when its bases can be partitioned into finitely many parts of diameter smaller than the diameter of the set of bases, with the Borsuk number measuring the minimum number of parts required. **Matroid Borsuk property conjecture.** Every matroid with at least two bases has the Borsuk property. According to the source, this is equivalent to asking whether any matroid polytope is a counterexample to the Borsuk conjecture. The question is explicitly described as open, and no counterexample is known.
R029.source_name: Gyivan López-Campos, Frédéric Meunier and Jorge L. Ramírez Alfonsín, “Matroids, intersecting bases, and Borsuk property”, arXiv:2506.17082 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17082

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2025). “This question is actually related the celebrated Hedetniemi conjecture , which has been refuted by Shitov in 2019 .”

R029.title: Characterization of extremal discrete Borsuk sets by cubes
R029.statement:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be a bounded set, and let $\beta_{\mathbb{Z}}(S)$ denote its discrete Borsuk partition number. Let $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ be the convex hull of $S$, and call two lattice polytopes **unimodularly equivalent** if one is mapped to the other by an affine unimodular transformation. **Discrete cube characterization conjecture.**

$$
\beta_{\mathbb{Z}}(S)=2^d
$$

if and only if $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ is unimodularly equivalent to a $d$-cube $[0,m]^d$ for some $m \in \mathbb{N}$. The paper proves the upper bound $\beta_{\mathbb{Z}}(S)\leq 2^d$ and that it is attained by $S=\{0,1\}^d$; the conjecture seeks to characterize all equality cases.
R029.source_name: Anouk E. Brose, Jesús A. De Loera, Gyivan Lopez-Campos and Antonio J. Torres, “On Lattice Diameter Segments and A Discrete Borsuk Partition Problem”, arXiv:2508.20009 (2025).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20009

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2025). “As shown in this does not hold when $d \geq 3$.”

R029.title: Logarithmic threshold conjecture for the chromatic number of random Borsuk graphs
R029.statement:
Let $G(n,\alpha)$ be the random Borsuk graph in dimension $d$, and let $\chi(G(n,\alpha))$ denote its chromatic number. **Logarithmic threshold conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ there exists a constant $c=c(d)$ such that, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and every sequence $\alpha=\alpha(n)$, 

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigl(\chi(G(n,\alpha))>d+1\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if }\alpha>(1+\varepsilon)c(\ln n/n)^{1/d},\\
0 & \text{if }\alpha<(1-\varepsilon)c(\ln n/n)^{1/d}.
\end{cases}
$$

The paper identifies the logarithmic regime as the relevant one for chromatic number at least $d+2$ and suggests a connection with coverage of the sphere by random caps. Establishing the claimed threshold and its constant remains open.
R029.source_name: Álvaro Acitores Montero, Matthias Irlbeck, Tobias Müller and Matěj Stehlík, “Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph”, arXiv:2603.05467 (2026).
R029.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0611416](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611416).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05467

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The semi-sharpness of these thresholds leaves open the possibility that they are in fact sharp. We conjecture that this is the case. (See Section for more discussion and more open problems.”

R029.title: Polynomial threshold conjecture for intermediate chromatic numbers of random Borsuk graphs
R029.statement:
Let $G(n,\alpha)$ be the random Borsuk graph in dimension $d$, and let $\chi(G(n,\alpha))$ denote its chromatic number. **Polynomial threshold conjecture.** For each $d\geq 2$, there exist constants $c_3=c_3(d),\dots,c_d=c_d(d)$ such that

$$
c_2<c_3<\dots<c_d,
$$

where $c_2$ is the constant supplied by the paper's theorem, and, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every $3\leq k\leq d$, and every sequence $\alpha=\alpha(n)$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigl(\chi(G(n,\alpha))>k\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if }\alpha>(1+\varepsilon)c_k n^{-1/d},\\
0 & \text{if }\alpha<(1-\varepsilon)c_k n^{-1/d}.
\end{cases}
$$

The claim gives the expected sharp thresholds for the intermediate chromatic-number transitions, refining the paper's almost-all-$n$ result. The constants and the asserted sharpness are not proved.
R029.source_name: Álvaro Acitores Montero, Matthias Irlbeck, Tobias Müller and Matěj Stehlík, “Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph”, arXiv:2603.05467 (2026).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05467

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The semi-sharpness of these thresholds leaves open the possibility that they are in fact sharp. We conjecture that this is the case. (See Section for more discussion and more open problems.”

R029.title: Hitting-angle conjecture for chromatic number and neighbourhood complexes
R029.statement:
Fix $d\geq 2$ and $k\in\{3,\dots,d+1\}$. In the random Borsuk graph process, edges are added in order of decreasing geodesic distance as the angle parameter $\alpha$ increases. For a monotone graph property $\mathcal{R}$, let $\alpha(n,\mathcal{R})$ be the random angle at which the process first attains $\mathcal{R}$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the property of having chromatic number $>k$, and let $\mathcal{Q}$ be the property of containing a subgraph whose neighbourhood complex is homotopy equivalent to $S^{k-1}$. **Hitting-angle conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\alpha(n,\mathcal{P})=\alpha(n,\mathcal{Q})\bigr)=1-o_n(1).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the chromatic transition is asymptotically witnessed exactly when the relevant topological subgraph first appears. The paper notes that the analogous assertion for $k=2$ holds, but the stated range remains open.
R029.source_name: Álvaro Acitores Montero, Matthias Irlbeck, Tobias Müller and Matěj Stehlík, “Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph”, arXiv:2603.05467 (2026).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05467

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The semi-sharpness of these thresholds leaves open the possibility that they are in fact sharp. We conjecture that this is the case. (See Section for more discussion and more open problems.”

R029.title: Two-consecutive-values conjecture for the chromatic number of sparse random Borsuk graphs
R029.statement:
Let $G(n,\alpha)$ be the random Borsuk graph in dimension $d$, let $\chi(G(n,\alpha))$ denote its chromatic number, and let $\alpha_0$ be the constant supplied by the Erdős–Hajnal result mentioned in the paper's introduction. **Two-consecutive-values conjecture.** For all $d\geq 1$ and all sequences $\alpha=\alpha(n)$ with $\alpha<\alpha_0$, there is a sequence of integers $k=k(n)$ such that

$$
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\chi(G(n,\alpha))\in\{k,k+1\}\bigr)=1-o_n(1).
$$

This is presented as a weaker conjecture that might be approachable without first proving the hitting-angle conjecture. It predicts concentration of the chromatic number on two consecutive values in the indicated sparse regime and remains open.
R029.source_name: Álvaro Acitores Montero, Matthias Irlbeck, Tobias Müller and Matěj Stehlík, “Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph”, arXiv:2603.05467 (2026).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05467

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The semi-sharpness of these thresholds leaves open the possibility that they are in fact sharp. We conjecture that this is the case. (See Section for more discussion and more open problems.”

R029.title: Existence of a compact solenoid by holomorphic curves in the complex projective plane
R029.statement: A **solenoid by holomorphic curves** is a compact solenoid in the complex projective plane whose leaves are holomorphic curves. **Holomorphic-solenoid conjecture.** There exists a compact solenoid by holomorphic curves in the complex projective plane that contains no algebraic curve. The authors do not have intuition about whether this solenoid is tangent to a holomorphic foliation.
R029.source_name: Bertrand Deroin, “Surfaces branchées et soléno\"ıdes ε-holomorphes”, arXiv:math/0411593 (2004).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0411593

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2004).

R029.title: Simmons and Su's equivariant Tucker-type conjecture for $S_k^{n(k-1)}$
R029.statement:
Let

$$
S_k^{n(k-1)}=
\left\{(z_0,\ldots,z_{n(k-1)})\in\mathbb C^{n(k-1)+1}:\sum_{i=0}^{n(k-1)}|z_i|=1,\ z_i^k=|z_i|^k\right\},
$$

where $omega=e^{2\pi i/k}$, and let the symmetric group $\operatorname{Sym}(k)$ act on this space by permuting the $k$th roots of unity in each coordinate. Suppose the space is triangulated invariantly under this action, with vertex set $V$ labeled equivariantly by

$$
\ell:V\longrightarrow\{\omega^j m:1\leq j\leq k,;1\leq m\leq n\},
$$

meaning that $\ell(\pi(v))=\pi(\ell(v))$ for every $\pi\in\operatorname{Sym}(k)$ and $v\in V$.

**Simmons and Su's conjecture.** There must exist $k$ adjacent vertices in the triangulation whose labels are $\{\omega^j m:1\leq j\leq k\}$ for some fixed $m$.

This is an equivariant, symmetric-group version of Tucker's lemma and is intended as a combinatorial counterpart to the Borsuk-Ulam property. The supplied text presents it as a conjecture of Simmons and Su but gives no resolution, so its status is recorded as open.
R029.source_name: Mark de Longueville and Rade T. Zivaljevic, “The Borsuk-Ulam-property, Tucker-property and constructive proofs in combinatorics”, arXiv:math/0507269 (2005).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0507269

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2005).

R029.title: Bryant's modified Bing–Borsuk conjecture
R029.statement:
A locally compact space is **homogeneous** if its homeomorphism group acts transitively on the space, and an **ANR-space** is an absolute neighborhood retract. A **generalized $n$-manifold** is a locally compact $n$-dimensional ANR-space that is a $\mathbb Z$-homology $n$-manifold, meaning that for every $x\in X$,

$$
H_k(X,X\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)=0 \quad\text{if } k<n,
$$

and

$$
H_n(X,X\setminus\{x\};\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z.
$$

**Bryant's modified Bing–Borsuk conjecture.** Every locally compact homogeneous ANR-space of dimension $n\geq 3$ is a generalized $n$-manifold. This modifies the Bing–Borsuk conjecture to allow generalized manifolds; it is motivated by known counterexamples to the original conjecture and remains unresolved.
R029.source_name: Vesko Valov, “Homogeneous locally compact spaces”, arXiv:2401.00341 (2023).
R029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00341

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2024). “So, this conjecture is still open in dimensions 3, 4 and 5.”

R029.title: Erdős Problem #505 — A Counterexample to Borsuk’s Conjecture
R029.statement:
Does there exist a natural number $n$ and a bounded set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with positive diameter such that, for every family of $n+1$ subsets $F_1,\ldots,F_{n+1}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ covering $S$, at least one of them satisfies
$$\operatorname{diam}(S)\leq\operatorname{diam}(F_i)?$$

R029.title: Nagata conjecture for general points in the complex projective plane
R029.statement:
Let $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ be general closed points in $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$. If $r\ge 10$ and $d/m\le\sqrt{r}$, then
\[
\bigl[I_{s_1}^{m}\cap\cdots\cap I_{s_r}^{m}\bigr]_d=0.
\]

R029.statement: Let $A$ be a free line arrangement in the complex projective plane, and let $A'$ be a line arrangement with the same combinatorics as $A$, meaning the same intersection lattice. Then $A'$ is free as well; equivalently, freeness of a line arrangement is a combinatorial property.

R029.title: Equality of a plane-curve count and an Euler characteristic
R029.statement: The report states that the number of irreducible degree-$d$ curves in the complex projective plane passing through $2d-1$ points in general position and tangent to order $d$ at a specified point on a specified line equals the Euler characteristic of the moduli space of $2d-1$ points in projective space of dimension $d-1$. It explains that both quantities are computed by the same recursive formula.

R029.title: Tucker's lemma
R029.statement: In mathematics, Tucker's lemma is a combinatorial analog of the Borsuk–Ulam theorem, named after Albert W. Tucker. Let T be a triangulation of the closed n-dimensional ball $B_{n}$. Assume T is antipodally symmetric on the boundary sphere $S_{n-1}$. That means that the subset of simplices of T which are in $S_{n-1}$ provides a triangulation of $S_{n-1}$ where if σ is a simplex then so is −σ. Let $L:V(T)\to \{+1,-1,+2,-2,...,+n,-n\}$ be a labeling of the vertices of T which is an odd function on $S_{n-1}$, i.e., $L(-v)=-L(v)$ for every vertex $v\in S_{n-1}$. Then Tucker's lemma states that T contains a complementary edge - an edge (a 1-simplex) whose vertices are labelled by the same number but with opposite signs.
R029.source_name: Wikipedia
